Build a DCF and comparable-company valuation for your strongest target and create a five-slide investment memo explaining the acquisition rationale, valuation range, major risks, and expected benefits.

reasons: This internship can help you practice company valuation, transaction analysis, financial modeling, presentation building, and the deal-execution skills commonly used later in corporate M&A teams.
preparationSteps: Build a three-statement financial model for a public company and connect the income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement before adding a DCF valuation.
Create a precedent-transactions table using at least five acquisitions from one industry and compare purchase price, revenue multiples, EBITDA multiples, and transaction rationale.

reasons: This internship can help you practice examining a target company's financial statements, identifying deal risks, testing earnings quality, and supporting financial due diligence before an acquisition closes.
preparationSteps: Take a public company's financial statements and create a mock diligence checklist covering revenue quality, margins, debt, working capital, customer concentration, cash flow, and unusual accounting items.
Build an acquisition model showing purchase price, financing assumptions, expected cost or revenue synergies, and how the transaction could change the buyer's earnings under different scenarios.

title: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
shortDescription: Leads enterprise cybersecurity strategy, protects critical systems and data, manages digital risk and incident response, and sets the security architecture and policies used across a large organization.

reasons: This internship can help you practice monitoring security events, documenting incidents, evaluating vulnerabilities, and understanding how enterprise security teams protect systems and data.
preparationSteps: Build a legal home cybersecurity lab with virtual machines and practice reviewing authentication logs, firewall events, failed logins, and other defensive indicators.
Create a small security dashboard that categorizes mock incidents by severity, affected system, business impact, response status, and recommended mitigation.

reasons: This internship can help you practice designing secure systems, reviewing technical risks, configuring security controls, and understanding how cybersecurity fits into enterprise architecture.
preparationSteps: Draw the architecture of a hypothetical cloud application and identify where authentication, encryption, network controls, logging, backups, and access restrictions should be placed.
Choose one security framework such as NIST Cybersecurity Framework and map its major functions to controls in your hypothetical company environment.

reasons: This internship can help you practice evaluating technology risks, documenting security controls, reviewing policies, and translating technical cybersecurity issues into business decisions.
preparationSteps: Create a mock cyber risk register containing 10 risks, their likelihood, business impact, existing controls, owner, and proposed treatment.

Build experience across both technical security and business leadership because CISO is a senior executive role typically reached after years in security engineering, operations, architecture, risk, and management.

title: Cryptographer
shortDescription: Designs and analyzes cryptographic algorithms and secure communication protocols that protect sensitive government, financial, and technology systems from unauthorized access and future computational threats.

reasons: This internship can help you practice mathematical security analysis, reading cryptography papers, evaluating algorithms, and supporting research on secure communications or cryptographic systems.
preparationSteps: Ask a mathematics or computer science professor whether you can assist with research involving number theory, algebra, algorithms, coding theory, or cybersecurity mathematics.
Read one introductory cryptography paper or standard and write a short technical explanation of the mathematical problem it solves, its assumptions, and how its security is evaluated.

reasons: This internship can help you practice implementing established cryptographic systems, testing secure software, measuring algorithm performance, and learning how encryption is deployed in real products.
preparationSteps: Use established cryptographic libraries to build an educational application that encrypts and authenticates sample data and document which standardized algorithms and key-management choices you used.
Compare the runtime and key sizes of several standardized cryptographic algorithms or post-quantum candidates using test data and summarize the engineering tradeoffs.

reasons: This role can help you build the proof-writing, abstract algebra, number theory, and research skills used in advanced cryptography and cryptanalysis.
preparationSteps: Complete a faculty-supervised project in number theory, algebra, combinatorics, or algorithms and aim to present the work at an undergraduate mathematics research event.
By junior year, compare graduate programs in mathematics, computer science, cybersecurity, or cryptography; research-heavy cryptographer roles often value master's or PhD-level mathematical training.

title: Cyber Warfare Analyst
shortDescription: Analyzes adversary cyber capabilities, monitors threats to national-security networks, and supports authorized defensive and offensive cyber operations through technical intelligence, vulnerability research, and secure systems analysis.

reasons: This internship can help you practice monitoring network activity, investigating alerts, analyzing suspicious behavior, and recommending defensive responses for sensitive systems.
preparationSteps: Build a legal virtual network lab and practice analyzing sample firewall, endpoint, and authentication logs to identify abnormal activity and document a defensive response.
Participate in university cybersecurity competitions or authorized capture-the-flag events that emphasize network defense, digital forensics, secure configuration, and incident analysis.

reasons: This internship can help you practice researching threat actors, connecting technical indicators with geopolitical context, and preparing intelligence assessments for security decision makers.
preparationSteps: Choose one publicly documented state-sponsored threat group and build a defensive intelligence brief covering its targets, known behaviors, affected industries, geopolitical context, and recommended mitigations using reputable public sources.
Track major cyber incidents for six weeks and maintain a table connecting each incident to the affected country, organization, attack type, suspected objective, and defensive lesson.

reasons: This experience can help you learn how computer engineering, intelligence analysis, cybersecurity, and national-security missions combine inside government cyber organizations.
preparationSteps: Apply early to NSA, Intelligence Community, Department of Defense, or cleared-contractor student programs because national-security cyber positions commonly involve lengthy citizenship, suitability, and security-clearance processes.

Build a portfolio around defensive security, secure programming, networking, operating systems, and authorized cyber competitions while also studying international politics so you can explain the strategic context behind technical threats.

title: Digital Forensics Expert
shortDescription: Collects and reconstructs digital evidence from computers, networks, mobile devices, and cloud systems to determine how cyber incidents occurred and support criminal, regulatory, or national-security investigations.

reasons: This internship can help you practice preserving evidence, examining forensic images, documenting findings, and reconstructing activity from computers or other digital devices.
preparationSteps: Build a legal forensic lab with a virtual machine and create a sample disk image containing files, browser activity, login records, and deleted data, then document how you recovered and interpreted the evidence.
Write a mock forensic report containing the evidence source, acquisition method, timeline, recovered artifacts, findings, and limitations without modifying the original evidence.

reasons: This internship can help you practice reviewing logs, reconstructing security incidents, identifying affected systems, and documenting how suspicious activity moved through an environment.
preparationSteps: Create a mock incident timeline from sample Windows, firewall, or authentication logs and identify the initial suspicious event, affected accounts, later activity, and recommended containment actions.
Practice using Wireshark and operating-system logs in an authorized lab to understand how network and endpoint evidence can be combined during an investigation.

reasons: This experience can help you understand how technical evidence, investigative procedures, written reports, and legal requirements come together in federal cyber investigations.
preparationSteps: Apply early to FBI, CISA, Department of Justice, or other federal student programs and make sure your coursework includes substantial computer science, information systems, IT, mathematics, or digital-forensics content.
Build a portfolio containing two or three defensive forensic investigations with clear evidence handling, timelines, screenshots, technical findings, and professional written reports.

title: Malware Reverse Engineer
shortDescription: Analyzes malicious software to determine how it behaves, communicates, persists, and avoids detection, then converts those findings into signatures, detections, and defensive protections for affected systems.

reasons: This internship can help you practice examining malicious programs, identifying suspicious behaviors, documenting technical findings, and helping defensive teams understand emerging threats.
preparationSteps: Use intentionally safe malware-analysis exercises or educational samples in an isolated virtual lab and document file behavior, processes, network activity, persistence methods, and defensive indicators.
Create a technical report for each lab sample showing what the program attempted to do, which system artifacts revealed that behavior, and how a defender could detect it.

reasons: This internship can help you practice analyzing software behavior, researching adversary techniques, developing detections, and communicating technical findings to security engineering teams.
preparationSteps: Learn C, operating-system fundamentals, assembly basics, and debugging well enough to follow how a small compiled program moves data through memory and calls system functions.
Take a simple program you wrote yourself, compile it, inspect it with a debugger or disassembler, and document how its source-code functions appear after compilation.

reasons: This internship can help you practice turning threat research into defensive rules, investigating suspicious activity, and testing whether security systems correctly identify malicious behavior.
preparationSteps: Use public defensive datasets or authorized lab logs to write simple detection rules for suspicious process execution, unusual authentication activity, or known malicious indicators.
Build a portfolio connecting each detection rule to the behavior it identifies, sample evidence, likely false positives, and the defensive action an analyst should take.

title: Cybersecurity Counsel
shortDescription: Advises organizations through major data breaches, cybersecurity regulations, government investigations, and lawsuits while helping companies reduce legal exposure before and after security incidents.

reasons: This internship can help you practice researching cybersecurity laws, reviewing breach obligations, preparing legal summaries, and supporting attorneys advising companies on digital risk.
preparationSteps: Choose one major public data breach and write a short legal case brief identifying what happened, what data was affected, which regulators became involved, and what legal claims or obligations followed.
Build a comparison chart showing how federal rules and three state breach-notification laws differ in notification triggers, deadlines, affected data, and required recipients.

reasons: This internship can help you practice interpreting privacy requirements, reviewing corporate policies, documenting compliance controls, and helping organizations prepare for regulatory scrutiny.
preparationSteps: Choose a hypothetical company that collects customer names, payment information, location data, and account credentials and map where each data type is collected, stored, shared, and protected.
Create a one-page incident-response legal checklist covering evidence preservation, internal escalation, outside counsel, regulator notification, customer notification, and documentation.

reasons: This internship can help you practice researching statutes and enforcement actions, writing legal memoranda, and understanding how regulators evaluate cybersecurity failures after major incidents.
preparationSteps: Read several FTC, state attorney general, or other public cybersecurity enforcement matters and summarize the security failures, legal theories, penalties, and remediation requirements in a comparison table.

By junior year, plan your JD pathway by researching law schools with privacy, cybersecurity, technology law, or national-security law offerings and preparing for the LSAT, recommendations, and legal internships.

title: AI Security Researcher
shortDescription: Researches how machine learning systems can be manipulated or compromised and develops defensive controls that make enterprise AI models, agents, and supporting infrastructure more resistant to malicious use.

reasons: This internship can help you practice evaluating machine learning systems, measuring robustness, designing defensive tests, and researching how AI systems respond to unexpected or adversarial inputs.
preparationSteps: Train a small image or text classifier using a public dataset and create a research report measuring how its accuracy changes when inputs contain noise, missing information, or other controlled distortions.
Ask a machine learning, cybersecurity, or computer science professor whether you can assist with model evaluation, robustness testing, dataset analysis, literature reviews, or AI security research.

reasons: This internship can help you practice securing machine learning pipelines, controlling access to models and data, monitoring unusual behavior, and designing protections around deployed AI systems.
preparationSteps: Build a small ML application and create a security architecture diagram showing where training data, model files, user inputs, API access, authentication, logging, and monitoring should be protected.
Write a threat model identifying possible risks to the model, dataset, API, credentials, and infrastructure and pair every risk with a defensive control.

reasons: This role can help you practice reading technical research, designing controlled evaluations, analyzing model failures, and producing research outputs relevant to advanced AI security work.
preparationSteps: Complete a faculty-supervised machine learning security or robustness project and aim to publish the code or present the results at an undergraduate research event.

By junior year, compare graduate programs and research fellowships in machine learning, computer science, AI safety, and cybersecurity and identify which ones emphasize robustness, security, or trustworthy AI.

title: Penetration Testing Director
shortDescription: Leads authorized offensive security teams that test corporate applications, cloud environments, networks, and other systems to expose weaknesses before real attackers can exploit them.

reasons: This internship can help you practice authorized security testing, documenting vulnerabilities, validating defensive controls, and explaining technical security findings to organizations.
preparationSteps: Use legal training environments, cybersecurity labs, or capture-the-flag platforms to practice web, Linux, networking, and security fundamentals without testing systems you do not own or have permission to assess.
Create professional sample reports for your lab exercises containing the affected system, vulnerability category, business risk, supporting evidence, and recommended remediation.

reasons: This internship can help you practice identifying software security weaknesses, reviewing application designs, validating fixes, and working with developers to prevent vulnerabilities from reaching production.
preparationSteps: Build a small web application and create a security review covering authentication, permissions, input validation, secrets management, logging, and dependency risks.
Practice finding and fixing vulnerabilities only in intentionally vulnerable training applications or software you wrote yourself, then document the remediation in GitHub.

reasons: This internship can help you practice prioritizing security findings, tracking remediation, measuring risk, and coordinating with technical teams after vulnerabilities are discovered.
preparationSteps: Create a mock vulnerability register containing severity, affected asset, business importance, remediation owner, deadline, and status and develop a simple method for deciding which issues should be fixed first.

Build experience first as a penetration tester, application security engineer, red teamer, or security consultant because director-level offensive security roles currently expect many years of technical and leadership experience.

title: Critical Infrastructure Security Lead
shortDescription: Protects industrial control systems and operational technology that run power grids, water systems, manufacturing plants, and other essential infrastructure from cyberattacks and operational disruption.

reasons: This internship can help you practice monitoring industrial networks, documenting critical assets, evaluating security controls, and understanding how cybersecurity requirements differ between business IT and physical control systems.
preparationSteps: Build a diagram of a hypothetical industrial facility containing business IT, engineering workstations, controllers, sensors, and physical equipment and show how you would separate the major network zones.

Read introductory NIST guidance on industrial control system security and create a one-page summary of how safety, availability, network segmentation, monitoring, and access control apply differently in an OT environment.

reasons: This internship can help you understand PLCs, sensors, embedded devices, industrial networks, and the engineering constraints that security teams must consider when protecting physical processes.
preparationSteps: Use engineering coursework or a supervised educational lab to learn how sensors, controllers, and actuators interact and create a diagram showing how data moves through a simple automated process.
Ask an electrical engineering, computer engineering, or cybersecurity professor whether you can assist with an embedded systems, controls, networking, or cyber-physical systems research project.

reasons: This experience can help you learn how government agencies, utilities, engineering teams, and cybersecurity specialists work together to protect essential services from operational cyber threats.
preparationSteps: Apply to CISA, Department of Energy, electric utilities, water authorities, industrial cybersecurity firms, or engineering companies offering student programs involving OT, infrastructure, or cyber-physical security.
Build a portfolio containing an industrial network diagram, OT risk assessment, asset inventory, and defensive monitoring plan that explains how each control protects safety and service continuity.

title: Privacy Compliance Director
shortDescription: Leads global privacy compliance programs that control how companies collect, process, share, retain, and delete consumer data while ensuring digital products and data systems comply with international privacy laws.

reasons: This internship can help you practice interpreting privacy requirements, reviewing company processes, completing privacy assessments, and helping organizations document how personal information is handled.
preparationSteps: Create a comparison sheet for GDPR and CCPA/CPRA covering consumer rights, consent requirements, deletion requests, sensitive data, enforcement, and major business obligations.
Choose a hypothetical online company and build a data inventory showing what personal information it collects, why it collects it, where it is stored, who receives it, and when it should be deleted.

reasons: This internship can help you practice mapping enterprise data, defining retention rules, documenting data ownership, and helping organizations maintain controlled and compliant data systems.
preparationSteps: Build a mock database containing customer, payment, marketing, and account data and create a data dictionary identifying each field's sensitivity, owner, retention period, and permitted business use.

Draw a data-flow diagram showing how customer information moves from a website into databases, analytics systems, marketing tools, and outside vendors and mark every point where privacy controls are needed.

reasons: This internship can help you practice privacy risk assessments, control testing, compliance documentation, and coordination between legal, cybersecurity, product, and technology teams.
preparationSteps: Complete a mock privacy impact assessment for a company launching an AI-powered customer service tool, identifying the personal data involved, privacy risks, affected users, and required controls.
Create a sample consumer data-request workflow showing how a company would verify, locate, review, export, correct, or delete an individual's information across several internal systems.

title: Chief Information Officer (CIO)
shortDescription: Leads enterprise technology strategy and oversees the cloud platforms, networks, business software, infrastructure, cybersecurity, vendors, and IT operations that employees use to run a large organization.

reasons: This internship can help you practice supporting enterprise systems, troubleshooting technology problems, documenting IT processes, and learning how infrastructure and software support business operations.
preparationSteps: Build a small mock company IT environment diagram showing employee devices, identity management, networking, cloud services, file storage, business applications, backups, and security controls.
Volunteer to document or improve a real technology process for a campus organization, such as account management, shared-file organization, software access, device tracking, or technical support.

reasons: This internship can help you practice tracking IT services, coordinating technology projects, reviewing system performance, and understanding how companies manage large portfolios of software and infrastructure.
preparationSteps: Create a mock technology inventory containing laptops, servers, cloud subscriptions, software licenses, owners, annual costs, renewal dates, and business importance.
Turn the inventory into a one-page CIO dashboard showing technology spend, system availability, open incidents, security risks, and upcoming software renewals.

reasons: This internship can help you practice supporting ERP, CRM, HR, finance, and other company-wide software while learning how technology decisions affect multiple business departments.
preparationSteps: Choose a hypothetical company and map which systems it would need for finance, HR, sales, operations, analytics, collaboration, cybersecurity, and customer management.
Build experience across infrastructure, applications, cybersecurity, data, and project leadership over time because CIO is a late-career executive role rather than a direct entry-level position.

title: Principal Cloud Architect
shortDescription: Designs large cloud environments that distribute applications and data across regions while maintaining high availability, secure networking, disaster recovery, scalability, and reliable performance.

reasons: This internship can help you practice deploying cloud resources, configuring networks, managing compute and storage, and supporting applications hosted on AWS, Azure, or another cloud platform.
preparationSteps: Deploy a small web application on AWS or Azure with separate application and database components, then document the networking, storage, permissions, and monitoring you configured.
Draw an architecture diagram showing every cloud service in your project and explain what would happen if each major component became unavailable.

reasons: This internship can help you practice designing scalable systems, comparing cloud services, planning resilient infrastructure, and translating application requirements into technical architectures.
preparationSteps: Redesign your cloud project so its application can run in two availability zones and create a diagram showing load balancing, redundant compute, database backups, and failover.
Create a short architecture decision document comparing two possible designs by availability, cost, scalability, security, and operational complexity.

reasons: This internship can help you practice networking, servers, operating systems, storage, monitoring, and reliability concepts that remain important underneath cloud architectures.
preparationSteps: Build a legal virtual lab containing multiple Linux machines and configure basic networking, user permissions, services, logging, backups, and system monitoring.
After gaining cloud fundamentals, study toward an entry-level AWS or Azure certification and keep the certification work secondary to hands-on projects that demonstrate actual architecture skills.

title: Enterprise Architecture Lead
shortDescription: Defines how an organization's applications, cloud platforms, infrastructure, data, security systems, and business processes fit together and guides long-term technology modernization across the enterprise.

reasons: This internship can help you practice documenting technology environments, creating architecture diagrams, identifying system dependencies, and supporting long-term modernization decisions.
preparationSteps: Create an architecture map for a hypothetical company showing its website, CRM, ERP, databases, analytics tools, identity system, cloud infrastructure, networks, and major integrations.
Mark duplicate systems, outdated components, security dependencies, and important business processes and propose a simplified future-state architecture.

reasons: This internship can help you practice translating business requirements into technology solutions, documenting workflows, analyzing system gaps, and working between technical and business teams.
preparationSteps: Choose one campus or small-business workflow and document the users, business requirements, current software, data inputs, outputs, problems, and proposed future system.
Create both a process diagram and a system diagram so you can explain how a change in business operations creates corresponding technology requirements.

reasons: This internship can help you practice evaluating technology environments, recommending modernization plans, and explaining technical tradeoffs to business stakeholders.
preparationSteps: Build a five-slide modernization case for a fictional company moving from fragmented legacy systems toward a standardized cloud and enterprise application architecture.

Develop experience across software, infrastructure, networking, cloud, data, and business analysis because enterprise architecture leadership depends on understanding how multiple technology domains interact rather than specializing in only one.

title: Database Research Scientist
shortDescription: Researches and invents new database algorithms, indexing methods, query optimizers, and distributed data structures that make massive cloud databases retrieve and process information faster.

reasons: This internship can help you practice experimenting with query processing, indexing, storage methods, and database performance while supporting research into faster data systems.
preparationSteps: Build a database containing at least one million generated records and compare query runtimes before and after adding different indexes, then document which queries improve and why.
Ask a computer science or data systems professor whether you can assist with algorithms, database performance experiments, distributed systems research, benchmarking, or research coding.

reasons: This internship can help you practice designing database structures, improving query performance, testing data systems, and understanding how production databases handle large workloads.
preparationSteps: Create the same dataset in two different database designs and benchmark insertion speed, storage use, indexed searches, joins, and aggregation queries under each design.
Build a small application whose database receives repeated queries and create a performance report identifying its slowest queries and the changes you made to improve them.

reasons: This role can help you practice reading database research papers, designing controlled experiments, implementing systems ideas, and producing research results for graduate-level computer science work.
preparationSteps: Choose a SIGMOD or VLDB database paper and reproduce one small experiment or benchmark from it, then write a short comparison between your result and the published result.

By junior year, compare computer science PhD programs with database, distributed systems, or data-management research groups and prioritize strong coursework in algorithms, systems, databases, mathematics, and research.

title: IT Compliance Director
shortDescription: Leads technology compliance programs that ensure financial systems, cloud platforms, access controls, transaction infrastructure, and IT processes satisfy banking, accounting, security, and regulatory requirements.

reasons: This internship can help you practice testing technology controls, reviewing system access, documenting audit evidence, and determining whether important financial systems operate under effective controls.
preparationSteps: Create a mock IT audit for a small financial system covering user access, password controls, software changes, backups, privileged accounts, and separation of duties.
Build an audit workbook listing each control, the risk it prevents, the evidence you would request, your test procedure, and whether the control passed or failed.

reasons: This internship can help you practice identifying technology risks, evaluating controls, tracking remediation, and understanding how regulated companies manage IT systems that process sensitive financial information.
preparationSteps: Create a risk register for a hypothetical online bank containing risks for cloud infrastructure, payment systems, employee access, vendors, software changes, outages, and customer data.
Map each risk to a relevant control framework or requirement such as NIST, PCI DSS, SOX ITGC, or FFIEC and identify the control owner and remediation priority.

reasons: This internship can help you practice maintaining compliance evidence, testing controls, tracking regulatory findings, and coordinating between technology, accounting, cybersecurity, and audit teams.
preparationSteps: Build a mock SOX ITGC matrix covering access management, program changes, computer operations, and privileged access and connect each control to the financial reporting risk it reduces.
Learn the purpose of CISA, CPA, CRISC, CISSP, and related credentials and map which certification best fits the IT audit, technology risk, or cybersecurity path you want to pursue after graduation.

title: Director of Health Informatics
shortDescription: Leads the technology systems that securely store and exchange electronic health information, overseeing EHR platforms, interoperability, clinical data standards, and healthcare system integrations.

reasons: This internship can help you practice working with electronic health systems, clinical data, healthcare workflows, and technology projects that improve how medical information is stored and used.
preparationSteps: Create a mock patient database containing demographics, appointments, diagnoses, medications, laboratory results, and providers and draw how those records would move between a clinic, hospital, laboratory, and pharmacy.
Apply to hospital IT departments, health systems, EHR vendors, digital health companies, or university medical centers offering health informatics or clinical systems internships.

reasons: This internship can help you practice understanding healthcare data standards, connecting clinical systems, validating exchanged records, and supporting secure movement of patient information between organizations.
preparationSteps: Learn the basic structure and purpose of HL7 FHIR and create several sample healthcare resources such as a Patient, Observation, Medication, and Encounter using synthetic information.

Draw an interoperability architecture showing how an EHR could securely exchange patient information with a laboratory, pharmacy, insurer, and another hospital while preserving authentication and audit logging.

reasons: This internship can help you practice translating clinical workflows into technology requirements, documenting EHR processes, testing system changes, and working between healthcare staff and IT teams.
preparationSteps: Choose a healthcare workflow such as medication ordering, laboratory testing, referrals, or discharge and document the clinicians, data fields, systems, decisions, and handoffs involved from start to finish.

By junior year, compare master's programs in health informatics, biomedical informatics, information systems, or healthcare IT and identify programs emphasizing EHRs, interoperability, security, data standards, and healthcare workflows.

title: Global Infrastructure Director
shortDescription: Leads the global deployment and operation of data centers, backbone networks, fiber connectivity, and other physical infrastructure that keeps large digital platforms connected across countries and continents.

reasons: This internship can help you practice configuring networks, monitoring connectivity, documenting infrastructure, and learning how large organizations keep offices, cloud environments, and data centers connected.
preparationSteps: Use Cisco Packet Tracer or another legal network simulator to build a multi-site company network with routers, switches, subnets, redundant links, and separate office and data center networks.
Create a network architecture document showing each site, connection, backup path, expected traffic, and what happens if one major link becomes unavailable.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how servers, network equipment, power, cooling, cabling, monitoring, and redundancy work together inside highly available data centers.
preparationSteps: Design a small hypothetical data center and create a diagram showing server racks, network switches, internet connections, backup power, cooling, monitoring, and redundant components.
Build a spreadsheet calculating the number of servers, rack capacity, estimated power requirements, network capacity, and backup resources needed as the facility grows.

reasons: This internship can help you understand long-distance fiber networks, carrier relationships, network capacity, infrastructure projects, and how international connectivity reaches data centers.
preparationSteps: Choose a real transatlantic or transpacific submarine cable and create a one-page map showing its landing locations, countries served, major connectivity purpose, and possible alternative routes if the cable fails.
Compare three possible fiber or network routes for a hypothetical company using distance, redundancy, capacity, cost, geopolitical exposure, and landing-location risk.

title: Strategic Technology Procurer
shortDescription: Leads strategic purchasing of enterprise software, cloud services, servers, networking equipment, and technology services while negotiating major contracts and managing long-term supplier relationships.

reasons: This internship can help you practice comparing technology vendors, reviewing pricing, preparing sourcing documents, tracking contracts, and supporting purchases of software, hardware, and cloud services.
preparationSteps: Create a mock procurement project where a company needs a new cloud storage or business software platform and compare at least four vendors by price, features, security, contract length, and support.
Build a spreadsheet calculating three-year total cost of ownership for each option, including licenses, implementation, support, training, and expected price increases.

reasons: This internship can help you practice supplier research, RFP analysis, cost comparison, negotiation preparation, and sourcing strategy across high-value business purchases.
preparationSteps: Write a mock RFP for a company purchasing 500 laptops, a SaaS platform, or cloud services and include business requirements, technical requirements, pricing questions, service levels, and evaluation criteria.
Score three mock vendor proposals using a weighted matrix covering cost, technical fit, security, implementation risk, vendor stability, and contract flexibility.

reasons: This internship can help you practice tracking supplier performance, software renewals, contract obligations, technology spending, and risks associated with major third-party vendors.
preparationSteps: Build a mock IT vendor portfolio containing software, cloud, telecom, hardware, and consulting suppliers and track annual spend, renewal dates, contract owners, service levels, and risk ratings.
Create a negotiation brief for one major software renewal showing current spend, usage, alternative vendors, target price, walk-away conditions, and the contract terms you would try to improve.

title: IT Risk Auditor
shortDescription: Evaluates enterprise infrastructure, cloud systems, networks, applications, and technology controls to identify weaknesses that could cause security incidents, financial errors, outages, or major operational failures.

reasons: This internship can help you practice testing technology controls, reviewing system configurations, collecting audit evidence, and documenting whether important IT processes adequately reduce business risk.
preparationSteps: Build a mock IT audit workbook covering user access, privileged accounts, software changes, backups, incident management, network security, and system availability and define evidence you would request for each control.
Choose one hypothetical company system and draw its process and data flow, then mark the control points where unauthorized access, data loss, configuration errors, or outages could occur.

reasons: This internship can help you practice identifying technology risks, evaluating infrastructure and cybersecurity controls, tracking remediation, and explaining technical weaknesses in business terms.
preparationSteps: Create a technology risk register for a hypothetical enterprise containing cloud, network, database, hardware, identity, backup, vendor, and cybersecurity risks with likelihood, impact, controls, and remediation priorities.
Map at least 10 of your identified risks to relevant NIST, COSO, SOX ITGC, or PCI DSS controls so you can practice connecting technical problems to formal risk frameworks.

reasons: This internship can help you practice reviewing security controls, analyzing technical evidence, evaluating vulnerabilities, and determining whether cybersecurity processes operate as intended.
preparationSteps: Build a legal virtual lab and create an audit checklist covering operating-system updates, user permissions, firewall configuration, logging, backups, and authentication controls.
Research the CISA, CIA, CRISC, and CISSP credentials and map which one best fits the IT audit, technology risk, or cybersecurity path you may pursue after graduation.

title: User Experience (UX) Architect
shortDescription: Designs the structural experience of complex digital products by organizing information, workflows, navigation, and interaction patterns so enterprise software remains understandable and efficient for human users.

reasons: This internship can help you practice turning user needs into workflows, wireframes, prototypes, and interface structures while collaborating with product managers and software engineers.
preparationSteps: Choose a complicated campus system such as course registration, advising, club management, or event scheduling and redesign one complete user journey in Figma from the first screen through task completion.
Turn the project into a portfolio case study showing the original problem, user needs, workflow diagram, wireframes, final prototype, and specific design decisions you changed after testing.

reasons: This internship can help you practice studying how people interact with software, identifying usability problems, conducting structured research, and turning behavioral observations into design recommendations.
preparationSteps: Recruit five classmates to complete the same task in an existing website or campus application, record where they hesitate or make errors, and summarize the three strongest usability problems.
Redesign the weakest part of the experience and test the revised prototype with another small group to see whether completion time, errors, or user confusion decreases.

reasons: This internship can help you practice organizing complex information, designing navigation systems, mapping user flows, and creating scalable structures for large digital products.
preparationSteps: Choose a large enterprise application or university website and create a sitemap showing its current pages, hierarchy, navigation paths, duplicate content, and confusing structural relationships.
Redesign the information architecture using a simpler hierarchy and build a clickable low-fidelity prototype demonstrating how users would reach five important tasks.

title: Quantitative Portfolio Manager
shortDescription: Allocates large investment portfolios using statistical models, systematic trading signals, portfolio optimization, and automated risk controls to determine what assets to hold and how much capital to assign to each position.

reasons: This internship can help you practice finding market signals, testing investment hypotheses, analyzing large financial datasets, and evaluating whether quantitative strategies remain useful outside their original sample.
preparationSteps: Build a Python research project testing one market signal such as momentum, volatility, value, or mean reversion across multiple securities and separate your development data from your final test period.
Add transaction costs and basic risk controls to your backtest and report annual return, volatility, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, turnover, and where the strategy performs poorly.

reasons: This internship can help you practice measuring portfolio performance, analyzing sources of risk, optimizing asset weights, and explaining why portfolios gain or lose money.
preparationSteps: Create a portfolio of at least 20 securities and use Python to calculate correlations, volatility, drawdowns, contribution to risk, and several alternative portfolio weightings.

Build a simple optimizer that compares equal weighting, minimum volatility, and another allocation method and explain the tradeoffs rather than selecting a model only because it produced the highest historical return.

reasons: This internship can help you practice translating quantitative signals into systematic trading decisions while considering execution, market behavior, risk limits, and rapidly changing data.
preparationSteps: Build a paper-trading system that reads historical market data, generates predetermined signals, records simulated trades, and produces a daily performance and risk report without using real money.

By junior year, compare quantitative finance, financial engineering, statistics, applied mathematics, and computer science graduate programs if you want deeper training in stochastic modeling, optimization, and advanced quantitative research.

title: Investment Banking Director
shortDescription: Leads major corporate finance transactions including IPOs, equity and debt raises, mergers, and acquisitions while advising executives, managing deal teams, and coordinating complex capital-market execution.

reasons: This internship can help you practice company valuation, financial modeling, transaction research, presentation building, and supporting senior bankers during live capital raising and M&A assignments.
preparationSteps: Choose a public company and build a complete comparable-company analysis and DCF valuation using its filings, then summarize your valuation range and major assumptions on one presentation slide.
Practice reading 10-K and 10-Q filings until you can quickly identify revenue, EBITDA, debt, cash, share count, major business segments, and the factors driving recent financial performance.

reasons: This internship can help you practice analyzing equity markets, evaluating potential offerings, tracking investor demand, and supporting companies preparing to raise capital through public markets.
preparationSteps: Choose a recent IPO and create a five-slide case covering the company, offering size, valuation, comparable companies, use of proceeds, initial pricing, and post-IPO performance.
Build an IPO valuation model that calculates equity value, enterprise value, implied share price, dilution, and valuation multiples under several offering-price scenarios.

reasons: This internship can help you practice financial due diligence, valuation, transaction analysis, and identifying financial issues that affect major corporate deals.
preparationSteps: Create a precedent-transactions table containing at least five acquisitions from one industry and compare transaction value, revenue multiples, EBITDA multiples, premiums, and stated deal rationale.

Recruit for junior-year investment banking internships early and build technical proficiency in accounting, valuation, financial modeling, and behavioral interviews because Director is a senior role reached after progressing through analyst, associate, and vice-president responsibilities.

title: Private Equity Partner
shortDescription: Leads the acquisition of private companies, determines how portfolio businesses can grow or improve profitability, works with management teams to execute those changes, and eventually sells investments to generate returns for investors.

reasons: This internship can help you practice evaluating acquisition targets, analyzing industries, building investment models, conducting due diligence, and writing recommendations about whether a firm should acquire a company.
preparationSteps: Choose a public company and build a basic LBO model containing purchase price, debt financing, operating projections, debt repayment, exit valuation, IRR, and multiple on invested capital.
Write a two-page investment memo covering the company's business model, industry, competitive advantages, major risks, acquisition valuation, value-creation opportunities, and expected return.

reasons: This internship can help you build the valuation, financial modeling, deal process, and due diligence skills commonly used by professionals who later move into private equity investing.
preparationSteps: Become comfortable building DCF, comparable-company, precedent-transaction, and basic LBO models from public financial statements without relying entirely on prebuilt templates.

Recruit seriously for investment banking, transaction advisory, corporate development, or selective undergraduate private equity roles because many traditional buyout professionals enter private equity after gaining prior deal experience.

reasons: This internship can help you practice identifying ways an acquired company can increase revenue, improve margins, reduce costs, strengthen management, and become more valuable during the investment period.
preparationSteps: Choose an underperforming company and build a value-creation plan containing five measurable initiatives across revenue growth, pricing, costs, operations, technology, or organizational improvement.

Create a five-year model comparing the business before and after your proposed improvements and show how changes in revenue growth, margins, debt repayment, and exit valuation affect investor returns.

title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
shortDescription: Leads an organization's financial strategy and oversees accounting, forecasting, budgeting, treasury, risk management, capital allocation, reporting, and financial controls while advising executives and the board.

reasons: This internship can help you practice budgeting, forecasting, financial variance analysis, and preparing management reports used to guide company spending and performance decisions.
preparationSteps: Choose a public company and build a three-year forecast for revenue, expenses, operating income, and cash flow using its historical financial statements.
Create a monthly budget-versus-actual dashboard for a hypothetical company and explain the three largest variances and what management should investigate.

reasons: This internship can help you understand financial statements, closing processes, internal controls, account reconciliations, and the accounting infrastructure CFOs ultimately oversee.
preparationSteps: Take one public company's annual report and trace how revenue, expenses, assets, liabilities, and cash flow connect across its three major financial statements.
Build a mock month-end close checklist containing journal entries, reconciliations, financial statement preparation, variance reviews, and management approval.

reasons: This internship can help you practice monitoring cash, liquidity, debt, banking relationships, and financial risks that become major responsibilities in senior corporate finance leadership.
preparationSteps: Build a 13-week cash forecast for a hypothetical company showing expected collections, payroll, supplier payments, debt service, investments, and minimum cash needs.
Pursue progressive experience across accounting, FP&A, treasury, audit, or corporate finance because CFO is a late-career executive position reached after substantial financial leadership experience.

title: Actuarial Director
shortDescription: Leads actuarial teams that build pricing, reserving, and catastrophe-risk models used to determine how much insurers should charge and how much capital they need to withstand severe losses.

reasons: This internship can help you practice analyzing insurance losses, estimating expected claims, testing pricing assumptions, and supporting actuaries who determine appropriate premiums.
preparationSteps: Build a small insurance pricing project using synthetic claim frequency, claim severity, policy characteristics, and historical loss data to estimate expected loss per policy.
Begin the Society of Actuaries or Casualty Actuarial Society exam pathway during college and target passing at least one actuarial exam before recruiting for actuarial internships.

reasons: This internship can help you practice estimating potential losses from hurricanes, floods, wildfires, and other severe events while learning how insurers model low-frequency, high-severity risks.
preparationSteps: Use public hurricane, flood, wildfire, or property data to build a simple model comparing how expected losses change across geographic regions or event severities.
Create a simulation showing how a portfolio of insured properties performs under normal years, severe-loss years, and an extreme catastrophe scenario.

reasons: This internship can help you practice using statistical programming, insurance datasets, forecasting, and visualization to monitor risk and portfolio profitability.
preparationSteps: Use R or Python to analyze a synthetic insurance portfolio and compare loss ratios, claim frequency, claim severity, and profitability across customer or risk segments.

Keep progressing through actuarial exams while building proficiency in Excel, R, SQL, probability, statistics, and insurance mathematics because director-level roles usually require years of actuarial experience and advanced professional credentials.

title: Hedge Fund Quant Researcher
shortDescription: Searches large financial and alternative datasets for subtle predictive patterns, converts those findings into systematic trading signals, and rigorously tests whether strategies can produce reliable risk-adjusted returns.

reasons: This internship can help you practice generating hypotheses, analyzing large market datasets, developing trading signals, backtesting strategies, and deciding whether patterns are statistically meaningful.
preparationSteps: Build a Python project testing several potential equity signals such as momentum, volatility, earnings changes, or valuation and evaluate them across an out-of-sample period.
Document every hypothesis you test, including unsuccessful ones, and report return, volatility, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, turnover, transaction costs, and signal stability.

reasons: This internship can help you practice evaluating unconventional datasets, engineering predictive features, checking data quality, and determining whether new information adds investment value.
preparationSteps: Find a legal public alternative dataset such as search trends, weather, shipping, employment postings, government records, or news data and test whether it has a measurable relationship with future market or company outcomes.

Create a research notebook documenting data collection, cleaning, feature generation, look-ahead bias checks, model testing, and whether the dataset adds predictive information beyond traditional market variables.

reasons: This internship can help you practice turning statistical research into repeatable trading rules, combining multiple signals, monitoring model behavior, and working with portfolio construction and risk constraints.
preparationSteps: Combine at least three independently researched signals into a simple market-neutral paper portfolio and compare the combined strategy against each signal used alone.

Build strong relationships with mathematics, statistics, economics, physics, or computer science professors and pursue faculty research because the most research-intensive quant roles often favor candidates with substantial mathematical research experience or graduate-level training.

title: High-Frequency Quant Developer
shortDescription: Builds extremely fast trading software that processes live market data, evaluates quantitative signals, and sends orders to exchanges while minimizing latency across software, networking, and computer hardware.

reasons: This internship can help you practice translating quantitative ideas into production software, processing real-time market data, improving code performance, and working alongside traders and quantitative researchers.
preparationSteps: Build a C++ market simulator that reads historical price updates, maintains a simple order book, processes simulated orders, and records execution results without using real money.

Benchmark different implementations of the same program and document runtime, memory use, and throughput so your portfolio shows that you can measure performance rather than simply write functioning code.

reasons: This internship can help you practice C++, concurrency, memory management, networking, profiling, and performance optimization for systems where execution speed and reliability are critical.
preparationSteps: Write a multithreaded C++ program that processes a large stream of generated messages and compare its throughput and latency against a single-threaded implementation.
Use profiling tools on code you wrote yourself to identify one CPU or memory bottleneck, optimize it, and publish before-and-after benchmark results with an explanation of what changed.

reasons: This internship can help you build the operating systems, networking, hardware, and low-level programming knowledge needed to understand where latency occurs inside high-performance trading infrastructure.
preparationSteps: Build a Linux networking project that sends timestamped messages between two programs and measure how message size, concurrency, and system load affect latency.

Strengthen C++, data structures, operating systems, computer architecture, and networking before focusing heavily on finance because current low-latency trading firms explicitly hire strong systems engineers even without prior market experience.

title: Venture Capital Principal
shortDescription: Identifies promising science and technology startups, evaluates their technologies and business models, leads investment due diligence, structures equity investments, and supports founders as their companies grow.

reasons: This internship can help you practice sourcing startups, researching markets, evaluating founders and products, building investment analyses, and supporting due diligence before a venture fund invests.
preparationSteps: Choose five early-stage startups in one technology sector and write one-page investment briefs covering the problem, product, market size, competitors, founders, business model, funding history, risks, and reasons you would or would not invest.
Build a spreadsheet that tracks at least 50 startups in one sector and records funding stage, investors, technology, market, competitors, recent milestones, and your own investment score.

reasons: This internship can help you practice evaluating companies whose value depends on difficult science or engineering, comparing competing technologies, and determining whether technical breakthroughs can become scalable businesses.
preparationSteps: Choose one field such as biotechnology, semiconductors, robotics, energy storage, or AI infrastructure and build a market map containing at least 15 startups grouped by technology approach and development stage.

Select one company from the map and write a technical diligence memo explaining how its technology works, what must be proven for it to succeed, competing approaches, commercialization risks, and potential customers.

reasons: This internship can help you practice market sizing, startup valuation, investment memo writing, financial analysis, and presenting potential investments to senior investors.
preparationSteps: Build a simple venture financing model showing a startup's pre-money valuation, investment amount, post-money valuation, investor ownership, founder dilution, and ownership after a second funding round.

Seek research, engineering, startup, investment banking, consulting, or startup-operating experience alongside finance coursework because principal-level deep-tech investors often need both investment judgment and enough technical fluency to evaluate specialized technologies.

title: REIT Fund Manager
shortDescription: Allocates investment capital across commercial real estate and REIT portfolios, evaluates property sectors and markets, and manages acquisitions, valuations, risk, and portfolio performance to generate returns for investors.

reasons: This internship can help you practice underwriting commercial properties, forecasting cash flows, comparing investment opportunities, and deciding whether properties meet a fund's return requirements.
preparationSteps: Choose a real commercial property listing and build an Excel underwriting model containing acquisition price, rent, vacancy, operating expenses, NOI, debt, cash flow, cap rate, IRR, and exit value.
Repeat the analysis for three different property types such as industrial, office, multifamily, or retail and write a one-page recommendation explaining which asset you would purchase and why.

reasons: This internship can help you practice monitoring property performance, updating valuations and business plans, tracking investment KPIs, and identifying ways to increase the value of existing assets.
preparationSteps: Create a mock portfolio containing 10 commercial properties and track occupancy, rent growth, NOI, debt, property value, capital expenditures, and investment returns in one dashboard.
Select the three weakest properties in your portfolio and create asset-management plans showing how rent changes, renovations, leasing, refinancing, or cost reductions could improve returns.

reasons: This internship can help you practice evaluating entire real estate portfolios, comparing sectors and regions, measuring investment performance, and supporting capital-allocation decisions.
preparationSteps: Build a paper REIT portfolio across at least five property sectors and track returns, volatility, dividend yield, valuation multiples, and sector weights against a real estate benchmark.
Write a quarterly mock investment committee memo recommending which sectors you would overweight or underweight based on valuations, interest rates, property fundamentals, and portfolio risk.

title: International Financial Arbitrator
shortDescription: Serves as a neutral decision maker in major cross-border financial, investment, and commercial disputes by reviewing contracts, financial evidence, international law, and witness arguments before issuing binding arbitral decisions.

reasons: This internship can help you practice researching international disputes, reviewing contracts and procedural rules, preparing legal memoranda, and supporting lawyers working on cross-border arbitration cases.
preparationSteps: Read a publicly available international arbitration award and create a two-page case brief identifying the parties, dispute, governing law, financial claims, major arguments, and tribunal's reasoning.
Compare the basic structure of ICC and ICSID arbitration and create a one-page procedural timeline showing how a dispute can move from filing through tribunal formation, hearings, and final award.

reasons: This internship can help you practice analyzing financial contracts, calculating claimed losses, organizing evidence, and supporting disputes involving banks, investment funds, corporations, or cross-border transactions.
preparationSteps: Choose a public cross-border financial or commercial dispute and build a case file containing the contract issue, jurisdictions involved, claimed damages, important evidence, and each side's legal position.
Create a simple damages model in Excel showing how assumptions about lost revenue, interest, currency conversion, or investment value can change the amount disputed.

reasons: This role can help you develop the legal research, international affairs, writing, and language skills needed before progressing into international arbitration practice and eventually becoming eligible for arbitrator appointments.
preparationSteps: Ask a political science, business law, economics, or international studies professor whether you can assist with research involving investment treaties, international trade, sovereign disputes, foreign investment, or international institutions.

By junior year, plan for law school by researching JD programs with international arbitration, international business law, or dispute resolution offerings and prepare for the LSAT, faculty recommendations, and legal internships; arbitrator appointments normally come only after substantial professional legal experience.

title: Principal Biochemist
shortDescription: Leads biochemical research that engineers proteins, therapeutic molecules, and mRNA-based systems to create new treatments for cancers, rare diseases, and other conditions that are difficult to treat with traditional medicines.

reasons: This internship can help you practice protein expression, biochemical assays, experimental design, and characterization methods used to create and evaluate new therapeutic proteins.
preparationSteps: Ask a biochemistry, chemistry, or biology professor whether you can assist with protein expression, purification, assay preparation, spectroscopy, chromatography, or another active biochemical research project.

Turn one protein from a research paper into a two-page research brief explaining its structure, biological function, therapeutic potential, and the experiments researchers use to measure its activity.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how researchers design RNA constructs, measure protein expression, test therapeutic activity, and optimize delivery or stability for mRNA-based medicines.
preparationSteps: Choose one approved or experimental mRNA therapy and create a pathway diagram showing the encoded RNA, target protein, cellular translation process, intended biological effect, and major delivery challenge.
Ask a genetics, cell biology, or biochemistry researcher whether you can assist with RNA preparation, gene-expression assays, cell culture, quantitative measurements, or literature review work.

reasons: This role can help you build the experimental design, laboratory technique, scientific writing, and faculty research experience expected for advanced biochemical research careers.
preparationSteps: Complete a faculty-supervised biochemical research project and aim to present a poster at an undergraduate research symposium or contribute to a laboratory publication.

By junior year, compare PhD programs in biochemistry, chemical biology, molecular biology, or protein engineering and identify their research expectations, prerequisite courses, faculty labs, and recommendation requirements.

title: Quantum Physicist
shortDescription: Researches and builds quantum computing systems by designing and controlling superconducting qubits, improving gate accuracy, studying sources of quantum errors, and developing methods for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

reasons: This internship can help you practice quantum simulation, experimental analysis, scientific programming, and research methods used to understand and improve quantum computing systems.
preparationSteps: Use Python and a quantum-computing framework to simulate single-qubit and two-qubit circuits, measure how controlled noise changes their outputs, and document the results in a research notebook.

Ask a physics, mathematics, electrical engineering, or computer science professor whether you can assist with quantum information, condensed matter, optics, electronics, or computational physics research.

reasons: This internship can help you practice electronics, measurement, signal analysis, hardware characterization, and experimental techniques relevant to controlling superconducting quantum processors.
preparationSteps: Use an electronics or physics laboratory project to measure signals, noise, resonance, or circuit behavior and write a technical report explaining the experimental setup, uncertainty, and sources of error.
Build familiarity with oscilloscopes, signal generators, basic RF concepts, circuit measurement, and Python data analysis through supervised physics or electrical engineering laboratory work.

reasons: This role can help you practice reading quantum-information research, analyzing error models, implementing simulations, and developing the publication-level research experience expected for quantum scientist positions.
preparationSteps: Implement a small educational simulation comparing an unprotected logical qubit with a basic quantum error-correcting code and measure how error probability changes under controlled noise.

By junior year, identify PhD programs in physics, quantum information, electrical engineering, or quantum computing and prioritize advanced quantum mechanics, linear algebra, research experience, and strong faculty recommendations because current research-scientist roles commonly require a PhD.

title: Molecular Cell Biologist
shortDescription: Studies how genes, proteins, and cellular pathways change during aging and disease, using molecular experiments and functional genomics to identify mutations and biological mechanisms that contribute to tumors and cellular decline.

reasons: This internship can help you practice cell culture, microscopy, experimental measurements, and laboratory methods used to study how cellular pathways change during disease.
preparationSteps: Ask a cell biology, genetics, cancer biology, or biomedical researcher whether you can assist with cell culture, microscopy, sample preparation, assay measurements, or laboratory data organization.
Choose one cellular pathway from a research paper and create a diagram showing the genes, proteins, signaling steps, experimental evidence, and disease outcome associated with the pathway.

reasons: This internship can help you practice studying genetic mutations, tumor cell behavior, signaling pathways, and experimental models used to determine why normal cells become cancerous.
preparationSteps: Choose one cancer type and build a research summary connecting several common mutations to the proteins, signaling pathways, cellular behaviors, and treatment strategies associated with that cancer.
Use a public cancer genomics resource or published dataset to compare the frequency of several mutations across patient samples and visualize which alterations appear most frequently.

reasons: This role can help you practice studying cellular aging, gene regulation, disease-associated cell states, and experimental interventions designed to understand or reverse age-related biological changes.
preparationSteps: Create a literature review comparing three proposed mechanisms of cellular aging and identify the experiments researchers use to distinguish correlation from a causal biological mechanism.

By junior year, compare PhD programs in cell biology, molecular biology, genetics, cancer biology, or aging biology and seek sustained faculty research experience that could produce a thesis, poster, presentation, or strong research recommendation.

title: Materials Genome Scientist
shortDescription: Combines materials science, atomistic simulation, and machine learning to predict the properties of unexplored compounds and identify promising materials before researchers physically synthesize them.
usual_employers: National Institute of Standards and Technology

reasons: This internship can help you practice modeling material structures, analyzing calculated properties, automating simulations, and using computation to narrow down promising materials.
preparationSteps: Download an open materials dataset and build a Python project predicting one property such as band gap, formation energy, or mechanical strength from material composition or structural features.
Ask a materials, physics, chemistry, or engineering professor whether you can assist with computational materials research, simulations, materials databases, or quantitative laboratory data.

reasons: This internship can help you practice training machine learning models on scientific data, comparing predicted material properties, and identifying candidate compounds for further simulation or experimentation.
preparationSteps: Train at least two machine learning models on the same materials dataset and compare their errors, feature importance, and performance on materials excluded from training.
Create a ranked list of hypothetical candidate materials from your model and clearly document why the algorithm considers them promising and where its predictions are uncertain.

reasons: This role can help you connect computational predictions with real material structure, characterization, and experiments while building the research background expected for advanced materials discovery roles.
preparationSteps: Complete a faculty-supervised materials project and aim to contribute a poster, undergraduate presentation, research report, or reproducible computational workflow.

By junior year, compare PhD programs in materials science, computational materials, physics, chemistry, or scientific machine learning because research-scientist roles in novel materials discovery commonly expect advanced graduate training.

title: Forensic DNA Principal
shortDescription: Leads development of highly sensitive forensic genetics methods that recover and interpret DNA profiles from degraded, limited, mixed, or decades-old biological evidence used in criminal investigations.
usual_employers: National Institute of Standards and Technology

reasons: This internship can help you practice evidence documentation, DNA extraction concepts, laboratory quality procedures, genetic analysis, and the strict handling requirements used in forensic laboratories.
preparationSteps: Apply to state crime laboratories, federal forensic programs, medical examiner laboratories, and accredited private forensic laboratories offering student laboratory or research placements.
Create a mock forensic DNA workflow showing evidence intake, biological screening, DNA extraction, quantification, amplification, profiling, interpretation, quality review, and final reporting.

reasons: This internship can help you practice studying degraded DNA, genetic markers, sequencing data, and experimental methods used to improve identification from difficult forensic samples.
preparationSteps: Use NIST's publicly available forensic DNA sequence mixture data to study how DNA quantity, degradation, mixture ratios, or number of contributors changes the complexity of genetic evidence.
Ask a genetics, chemistry, biology, or forensic science professor whether you can assist with DNA extraction, PCR, sequencing, laboratory validation, or genetic data analysis.

reasons: This role can help you build the genetics, molecular laboratory, experimental design, and validation skills required to develop new forensic DNA methods rather than only perform established tests.
preparationSteps: Complete a faculty-supervised genetics project involving DNA amplification, sequencing, genetic variation, or molecular assays and document the controls and validation steps used to establish reliable results.

By junior year, compare master's and PhD programs in forensic science, genetics, molecular biology, or analytical chemistry if you want to lead method-development research rather than remain solely in routine casework.

title: Environmental Toxicologist
shortDescription: Studies how pollutants, industrial chemicals, microplastics, and other environmental exposures affect cells, organs, wildlife, and human health and determines which exposure levels create biological harm.
usual_employers: National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences

reasons: This internship can help you practice studying chemical exposures, measuring biological responses, analyzing dose-response data, and determining how environmental contaminants affect organisms or cells.
preparationSteps: Ask an environmental science, biology, chemistry, or toxicology professor whether you can assist with cell assays, environmental sampling, chemical measurements, microscopy, or toxicity experiments.

Choose one contaminant such as PFAS, lead, pesticides, or microplastics and build a literature table comparing exposure levels, tested organisms or cell types, measured effects, and major findings from at least five studies.

reasons: This internship can help you practice evaluating chemical hazards, organizing experimental evidence, analyzing exposure information, and supporting scientific assessments of potential health risks.
preparationSteps: Build a mock chemical risk profile containing exposure source, dose, affected tissues or organisms, observed biological effects, uncertainty, and the evidence you would need before making a safety conclusion.
Use a public toxicology dataset to graph dose against a measurable biological response and identify where the response begins to differ meaningfully from an untreated comparison group.

reasons: This role can help you practice linking environmental exposures with biological mechanisms while building sustained research experience for advanced toxicology careers.
preparationSteps: Apply to EPA, NIEHS, university environmental health laboratories, or ORISE-style student research programs where undergraduates can contribute to environmental or toxicological science.

By junior year, compare graduate programs in toxicology, environmental health sciences, pharmacology, biochemistry, or molecular biology and seek sustained laboratory experience because research-intensive toxicology careers commonly progress through doctoral or other advanced scientific training.

title: Organic Chemistry Lead
shortDescription: Leads the design and synthesis of novel carbon-based molecules, optimizes their chemical properties, and guides medicinal chemistry teams in developing promising compounds into potential new drugs.

reasons: This internship can help you practice synthesizing and characterizing small molecules, interpreting experimental results, and learning how chemists modify compounds to improve potential drug candidates.
preparationSteps: Ask an organic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, or chemical biology professor whether you can assist with supervised synthesis, purification, chromatography, spectroscopy, or compound characterization in an active laboratory.

Choose one small-molecule drug and create a research brief showing its chemical structure, biological target, major functional groups, and several structural changes medicinal chemists explored during its development.

reasons: This internship can help you practice reaction planning, laboratory synthesis, purification, analytical characterization, and careful experimental documentation with complex organic molecules.
preparationSteps: Use your organic chemistry laboratory work to create a portfolio entry documenting one supervised synthesis through reaction purpose, purification method, analytical results, yield, sources of error, and what you would improve.
Practice interpreting introductory NMR, IR, and mass spectrometry data from coursework or educational datasets and connect each signal to structural features of known organic molecules.

reasons: This role can help you build sustained laboratory experience, experimental design skills, scientific writing, and faculty mentorship needed for advanced drug-discovery research careers.
preparationSteps: Complete a faculty-supervised chemistry research project and aim to produce a poster, undergraduate research presentation, thesis, or contribution to a publication.

By junior year, compare PhD programs in organic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, or chemical biology and identify faculty laboratories, research interests, prerequisite coursework, and recommendation requirements because chemistry-lead roles commonly require advanced research training.

title: Climate Modeler
shortDescription: Builds and analyzes mathematical simulations of the atmosphere, oceans, land, and energy systems to understand climate dynamics and project how temperatures, precipitation, circulation, and extreme events may change over decades.

reasons: This internship can help you practice running climate simulations, analyzing model output, comparing scenarios, and using numerical methods to investigate long-term atmospheric and environmental change.
preparationSteps: Download public climate-model data and use Python to compare temperature or precipitation across two time periods or emissions scenarios, then create maps or charts explaining the strongest changes.
