Create a technical comparison of several lens designs and explain how aberrations, focus, material properties, and geometry affect image quality.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how optics, mechanics, patient safety, testing, and regulated product development come together in medical technology.
preparationSteps: Choose an ophthalmic laser or intraocular lens and create a system diagram showing its optical components, interaction with the eye, major materials, sensors, and critical performance requirements.
Create a mock verification plan containing measurable requirements such as optical power, alignment accuracy, dimensional tolerance, image quality, and device safety.

reasons: This role can help you understand how optical engineering interacts with anatomy, visual perception, biological tissue, and experimental research.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Physics, Biology, or Engineering faculty member about an optics, biomedical imaging, materials, or vision-related project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

Develop the project toward a research poster or technical report and compare graduate programs in optics, biomedical engineering, medical physics, or related fields if you want advanced ophthalmic R&D leadership roles.

title: Trauma Biomechanist
shortDescription: Models how crash forces deform bones, organs, and soft tissues to predict human injury and help engineers design vehicle structures, restraints, and safety systems that better protect occupants.

reasons: This internship can help you practice crash analysis, occupant protection, safety testing, structural simulation, and interpreting engineering data from vehicle impacts.
preparationSteps: Use public crash-test data to compare two vehicles or restraint configurations using measurements such as acceleration, chest deflection, intrusion, or injury metrics.
Create a technical diagram showing how the vehicle structure, seat belt, airbag, seat, and occupant interact during a frontal or side-impact crash.

reasons: This role can help you practice studying human tissue response, injury mechanisms, experimental mechanics, and computational models used in impact biomechanics.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Engineering, Physics, Biology, or Forensic Science faculty member about an impact mechanics, materials failure, human motion, or computational biomechanics project that could become a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.
Use public NHTSA biomechanics data to create a research project comparing how one body region such as the head, chest, spine, or lower extremities responds as crash loading changes.

reasons: This internship can help you practice finite-element modeling, structural dynamics, material models, and simulation techniques that are heavily used in virtual crash testing.
preparationSteps: Build a finite-element model of a simplified structure subjected to an impact or rapidly applied load and examine stress, deformation, energy absorption, and likely failure regions.
Create a portfolio report comparing two structural or material configurations and explain which design reduces transmitted force or deformation and why.

title: Biosensor Array Designer
shortDescription: Designs wearable arrays of chemical sensors, microfluidic channels, and electronics that analyze sweat biomarkers and physiological signals to identify meaningful changes in health, hydration, or metabolic state.

reasons: This internship can help you practice sensor fabrication, calibration, electronics integration, experimental testing, and converting biological measurements into reliable electrical signals.
preparationSteps: Build a safe benchtop sensor project that measures a variable such as pH, conductivity, temperature, or salt concentration and create calibration curves comparing sensor output against known reference values.

Create a system diagram showing how a wearable sensor progresses from sweat collection through chemical sensing, analog electronics, signal processing, wireless transmission, and final health-data visualization.

reasons: This internship can help you practice integrating sensors, flexible materials, electronics, mechanical packaging, and data systems into devices that must operate reliably while worn on the body.
preparationSteps: Design a conceptual sweat-sensing wristband or skin patch showing sensor locations, fluid pathways, electronics, battery, wireless module, skin-contact materials, and the biomarkers being measured.
Create a test plan covering calibration, repeated measurements, temperature effects, motion interference, sensor drift, sweat-rate changes, and differences between users.

reasons: This role can help you build research experience in biomedical signal processing, sensing, chemistry, and experimental validation needed for advanced biosensor development.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Engineering, Chemistry, or Biology faculty member about a biomedical sensing, signal processing, materials, or analytical chemistry project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.
Develop the project toward a research poster containing the sensing principle, experimental setup, calibration procedure, measured data, uncertainty, and limitations of the sensor.

title: Surgical Tool Designer
shortDescription: Designs miniature catheters, guidewires, delivery systems, and precision instruments that allow surgeons and interventional cardiologists to repair heart structures through small incisions or blood vessels instead of open surgery.

reasons: This internship can help you practice CAD, prototyping, mechanical testing, design documentation, and product-development methods used to create minimally invasive surgical tools.
preparationSteps: Design a small grasping, cutting, steering, or delivery mechanism in CAD that could theoretically pass through a narrow tube and document its range of motion, dimensions, materials, and mechanical constraints.
Create a verification plan defining measurable requirements such as maximum diameter, bending radius, tensile strength, deployment force, positional accuracy, and repeated-use performance.

reasons: This internship can help you practice designing small mechanical assemblies, producing engineering drawings, selecting materials, managing tolerances, and iterating prototypes.
preparationSteps: Create a portfolio project containing a miniature mechanical assembly with CAD models, exploded views, tolerances, material choices, manufacturing methods, and several design iterations.
Practice designing components around strict size constraints and explain how reducing diameter or thickness affects strength, flexibility, manufacturability, and reliability.

reasons: This role can help you connect mechanical design with cardiovascular anatomy, experimental testing, biomaterials, and the clinical requirements that determine whether surgical instruments are usable and safe.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Engineering, Physics, Biology, or Materials faculty member about a miniature mechanism, biomaterials, fluid mechanics, assistive-device, or biomedical instrumentation project that could become a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

Study one minimally invasive cardiac procedure and create a high-level engineering workflow showing how the device enters the body, reaches the treatment site, performs its mechanical function, and is safely removed.

title: Principal OS Engineer
shortDescription: Architects core operating-system components and security boundaries that manage memory, processes, hardware access, isolation, and trusted execution while protecting critical systems from low-level attacks.
usual_employers: Operating System and Cloud Infrastructure Companies

reasons: This internship can help you practice low-level programming, operating-system concepts, debugging, memory management, and software that interacts closely with computer hardware.
preparationSteps: Use an educational operating system such as xv6 or another university OS project to study processes, scheduling, virtual memory, and system calls, then document one component you modified or investigated.
Build a C or C++ systems project that manages files, processes, threads, or memory and include tests explaining how the program behaves when resources or inputs fail.

reasons: This internship can help you practice C or C++, hardware-software interaction, debugging, device-level programming, and resource-constrained systems that build strong foundations for kernel engineering.
preparationSteps: Build a small embedded project that reads hardware inputs, controls an output device, and handles timing or interrupts, then document the hardware-software interaction.
Practice using Linux command-line debugging and development tools and create a portfolio note explaining how you diagnosed one memory, process, or concurrency problem.

reasons: This internship can help you learn secure software design, operating-system protections, access controls, isolation, and how engineers harden foundational software.
preparationSteps: Create a defensive Linux hardening project documenting permissions, process isolation, secure configuration, logging, and how each control reduces system exposure.

Build strong experience in operating systems, computer architecture, C or C++, and cybersecurity because principal kernel-security roles are senior positions normally reached after substantial systems-engineering experience.

title: Compiler Research Scientist
shortDescription: Researches compiler techniques that translate high-level programs into highly optimized machine instructions for new CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, and specialized silicon architectures.

reasons: This internship can help you practice parsing programs, transforming intermediate representations, generating machine-oriented code, and measuring how compiler decisions affect performance.
preparationSteps: Build a small compiler or interpreter for a simple language that handles variables, arithmetic, conditional logic, and functions, then document each stage from source code to execution.
Add one optimization such as constant folding or dead-code removal and benchmark several programs before and after the optimization.

reasons: This internship can help you practice profiling programs, identifying performance bottlenecks, understanding hardware behavior, and optimizing code for processors and accelerators.
preparationSteps: Benchmark one computational program under several implementation choices and measure execution time, memory use, and scaling as input size increases.
Inspect generated compiler output or intermediate representation for a few small programs and explain how different optimization settings change the resulting code.

reasons: This role can help you build the algorithms, programming-languages, architecture, experimentation, and publication experience expected for research-oriented compiler careers.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Computer Science or Mathematics faculty member about a programming-languages, algorithms, systems, or performance project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

By junior year, compare master's and PhD programs in computer science focused on compilers, programming languages, computer architecture, or systems because research-scientist positions often value graduate research and published technical work.

title: Distributed Systems Architect
shortDescription: Architects geographically distributed software platforms that process enormous volumes of financial transactions while preserving consistency, availability, security, fault tolerance, and low response times.

reasons: This internship can help you practice developing production services, APIs, databases, testing, and backend systems that form the foundations of large distributed platforms.
preparationSteps: Build a backend application that accepts transactions through an API, stores them in a database, validates duplicate requests, and records transaction status changes.
Write automated tests for failed requests, duplicate transactions, unavailable components, and simultaneous users rather than only demonstrating successful requests.

reasons: This internship can help you practice deploying services, networking applications, monitoring systems, databases, and designing infrastructure that remains available when individual components fail.
preparationSteps: Deploy a small multi-service application using a cloud platform or containers and document how requests move between the client, application service, database, and supporting infrastructure.
Create a controlled failure test where one service becomes unavailable and document what happens to pending requests, stored data, retries, and system recovery.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how software correctness, transaction integrity, auditability, security, and uptime requirements become especially important in financial systems.
preparationSteps: Build a simulated payment-processing system that generates thousands of transaction events and measure throughput, latency, failure rate, and database performance as load increases.

Create an architecture diagram showing redundant application services, a transaction database, event queue, monitoring, and backup or recovery components and explain what happens when one component fails.

title: Graphics Engine Scientist
shortDescription: Researches and develops advanced rendering algorithms that simulate how light interacts with virtual surfaces, enabling realistic real-time graphics for games, film, design, simulation, and other visual computing systems.

reasons: This internship can help you practice implementing rendering algorithms, working with GPUs, manipulating 3D scenes, and optimizing software that produces interactive visual output.
preparationSteps: Build a small 3D renderer that displays meshes, cameras, lighting, textures, and shadows and document how each stage of the rendering pipeline transforms the final image.
Add one advanced feature such as reflections, ray-traced shadows, physically based materials, or anti-aliasing and measure its effect on both image quality and frame time.

reasons: This internship can help you practice real-time rendering, performance optimization, C++, mathematics, and engine architecture used in interactive graphics applications.
preparationSteps: Create a small interactive scene in a graphics API or game engine and profile frame rate, GPU usage, object count, lighting complexity, and rendering bottlenecks.
Create a technical portfolio page explaining the graphics pipeline, performance problem you found, optimization you made, and measurable change in rendering performance.

reasons: This role can help you build the mathematical, experimental, publication, and algorithm-development background expected for scientist-level graphics research.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Computer Science, Mathematics, or Physics faculty member about a rendering, simulation, optimization, or visual-computing project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

By junior year, compare master's and PhD programs in computer graphics, visual computing, computer science, or applied mathematics because research-scientist rendering positions commonly expect graduate research or equivalent advanced experience.

title: AI Ethics Research Director
shortDescription: Leads research that measures and reduces unfair behavior in artificial intelligence systems by developing fairness metrics, model evaluations, mitigation algorithms, interpretability methods, and responsible deployment standards.
usual_employers: National Institute of Standards and Technology

reasons: This internship can help you understand how models are trained, evaluated, compared, and experimentally tested before specializing in fairness and responsible AI.
preparationSteps: Train a classification model on a public dataset and compare accuracy, false-positive rates, and false-negative rates across meaningful subgroups rather than reporting only one overall accuracy number.
Write a short research report explaining where performance differs between groups, possible causes of the disparity, and what additional evidence would be needed before claiming the model is fair.

reasons: This internship can help you practice model evaluation, fairness testing, transparency, documentation, and risk analysis for AI systems used in consequential environments.
preparationSteps: Use a fairness library or your own Python calculations to compare several fairness metrics on the same model and document why optimizing one definition of fairness may not satisfy another.
Create a model card for one machine learning project documenting training data, intended use, limitations, subgroup performance, known risks, and circumstances where the model should not be deployed.

reasons: This role can help you connect technical machine learning evaluation with ethics, governance, human behavior, and the consequences of deploying algorithms in real institutions.
preparationSteps: Choose one high-impact AI use case such as lending, healthcare, hiring, education, or criminal justice and produce a research brief connecting model performance, fairness metrics, affected stakeholders, and possible governance controls.

By junior year, seek sustained faculty research and compare PhD programs in computer science, machine learning, information science, human-computer interaction, or responsible AI because research-director positions generally build on years of advanced research and publication experience.

title: Database Engine Architect
shortDescription: Architects the internal storage, indexing, query-planning, and execution systems of relational databases so enormous operational datasets can be updated and analyzed with extremely low latency.

reasons: This internship can help you practice relational database design, indexing, query performance, transactions, and engineering systems that store and retrieve large quantities of structured data.
preparationSteps: Create a PostgreSQL database with at least several hundred thousand synthetic logistics records and compare query execution plans and runtimes before and after adding different indexes.
Document why each index changes performance, which queries remain slow, and what tradeoffs additional indexes create for storage and write performance.

reasons: This internship can help you practice building applications around relational databases, handling concurrent requests, optimizing queries, and designing reliable data-access patterns.
preparationSteps: Build a logistics API that records shipments, facilities, vehicles, and status events in a relational database and supports several analytical queries such as delayed shipments by region or facility throughput.
Generate increasing amounts of synthetic data and benchmark how API latency and query time change at different dataset sizes before optimizing the schema and queries.

reasons: This role can help you practice query processing, storage structures, algorithms, systems experimentation, and performance analysis used by engineers who develop database engines themselves.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Computer Science faculty member about a database, distributed-systems, algorithms, or performance project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.
Build a small experimental database component such as a B-tree index, buffer cache, query executor, or simplified relational engine and benchmark how its performance changes as data volume grows.

title: Network Protocol Researcher
shortDescription: Researches new wireless networking protocols, routing methods, and communication algorithms that reduce latency, improve efficiency, and help shape future Wi-Fi, cellular, and internet standards.

reasons: This internship can help you understand routing, network traffic, packet behavior, latency, reliability, and the practical systems that communication protocols must operate within.
preparationSteps: Build a small network simulation comparing how latency, packet loss, or throughput changes as traffic volume, routing paths, or network topology changes.

Use Wireshark on traffic from your own controlled network or lab environment and create a technical report explaining several common protocols, packet fields, timing behavior, and request-response sequences.

reasons: This internship can help you practice wireless communications, signal analysis, network testing, simulation, and understanding how software protocols interact with radio systems.
preparationSteps: Create a Python or MATLAB simulation comparing how bandwidth, signal quality, packet size, or retransmissions affect throughput and latency in a simplified wireless link.
Study the architecture of Wi-Fi or 5G and create a diagram explaining how the physical layer, MAC layer, network layer, and applications interact when data moves between two devices.

reasons: This role can help you build the algorithm design, simulation, experimentation, technical writing, and publication experience expected for advanced networking and standards research.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Computer Science, Mathematics, or Engineering faculty member about a networking, algorithms, wireless systems, or distributed-computing project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

By junior year, compare master's and PhD programs in computer science, computer engineering, telecommunications, or networking because standards-oriented research positions commonly value graduate research and published technical contributions.

title: Virtual Reality Principal
shortDescription: Architects the spatial tracking, sensor-fusion, and real-time software that estimates a user's head, eyes, hands, and surroundings while minimizing visual latency and maintaining stable immersive virtual and mixed-reality experiences.

reasons: This internship can help you practice real-time programming, performance optimization, debugging, software architecture, and building reliable systems that respond quickly to continuous input.
preparationSteps: Build an interactive 3D application where camera or object movement responds continuously to keyboard, controller, or sensor input and measure how frame rate changes as scene complexity increases.
Profile the application and document one performance bottleneck, the optimization you made, and the measurable improvement in frame time or responsiveness.

reasons: This internship can help you practice estimating motion and position from cameras and sensors, which is fundamental to headset tracking and spatial computing.
preparationSteps: Build a computer-vision project that tracks a recognizable object, face, hand, or camera movement across video frames and visualize the estimated position over time.
Create a second version that combines visual measurements with simulated or recorded motion-sensor data and compare whether the fused estimate is smoother or more stable.

reasons: This role can help you combine graphics, perception, human-computer interaction, spatial design, and experimental evaluation when developing immersive interfaces.
preparationSteps: Create a small VR or 3D interaction experiment comparing two interface designs and measure task completion time, positioning accuracy, errors, or user comfort instead of evaluating the experience only subjectively.

Talk with a Loyola Computer Science, Mathematics, Psychology, or Theater faculty member about a graphics, spatial interaction, perception, or immersive-media project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

title: Automated Verification Scientist
shortDescription: Develops mathematical verification methods that prove critical software satisfies precisely defined safety and correctness properties before it is deployed in aircraft, autonomous systems, and other high-consequence technology.

reasons: This internship can help you practice requirements analysis, software testing, traceability, debugging, and verification techniques used when software must satisfy strict correctness and safety requirements.
preparationSteps: Build a small C, C++, or Python program with clearly written requirements and create automated tests showing that each requirement is satisfied under normal, boundary, and invalid-input conditions.
Create a requirements-to-tests traceability table showing each software requirement, the test that verifies it, expected behavior, actual result, and any uncovered cases.

reasons: This role can help you practice mathematical specifications, logic, model checking, proof assistants, and research methods used to establish software correctness.
preparationSteps: Learn one accessible formal-methods tool such as Lean, TLA+, or Z3 and use it to specify and verify a small problem such as an algorithm invariant, state machine, or resource-allocation rule.

Talk with a Loyola Computer Science or Mathematics faculty member about a logic, algorithms, programming-languages, or software-verification project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how embedded software, requirements, testing, simulation, and certification interact when software controls safety-critical aerospace systems.
preparationSteps: Create a simplified flight-control state machine with clearly defined allowed states, transitions, safety conditions, and responses to invalid commands, then test every transition.

By junior year, compare master's and PhD programs in computer science, formal methods, programming languages, or software engineering because scientist-level verification research commonly requires advanced mathematical and research training.

title: Bioinformatics Software Lead
shortDescription: Leads development of high-performance software pipelines that process massive DNA sequencing datasets, align reads to genomes, identify genetic variants, and convert raw sequencing output into information researchers and clinicians can analyze.

reasons: This internship can help you practice processing genomic datasets, writing analysis scripts, using sequence-analysis tools, and interpreting biological results computationally.
preparationSteps: Download a small public sequencing dataset and build a documented workflow that performs quality checks, alignment or mapping, and a basic downstream analysis rather than only analyzing a finished spreadsheet.
Create a GitHub portfolio explaining the input files, each pipeline stage, software used, resulting outputs, biological interpretation, and limitations of your analysis.

reasons: This internship can help you practice building reliable software for large scientific datasets, automating workflows, testing code, and improving computational performance.
preparationSteps: Build a Python program that processes thousands of synthetic DNA sequences or genomic records and benchmark execution time and memory usage as the dataset grows.
Refactor the program into separate reusable processing stages with logging, error handling, tests, and configuration files so another researcher could reproduce the workflow.

reasons: This role can help you connect genetics with algorithms, statistics, sequencing technology, and computational research while building experience for advanced bioinformatics positions.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Biology, Computer Science, Statistics, or Data Science faculty member about a genetics, biological-data, algorithmic, or computational research project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

By junior year, compare master's and PhD programs in bioinformatics, computational biology, genomics, computer science, or biostatistics because technical-lead genomics roles often value advanced domain expertise alongside substantial software-engineering experience.

title: Principal Processor Architect
shortDescription: Defines the internal microarchitecture of advanced processor cores, deciding how pipelines, execution units, caches, branch prediction, memory systems, and parallel-compute features should work together for maximum performance and efficiency.

reasons: This internship can help you practice RTL design, digital logic, simulation, verification, and understanding how processor components are implemented in hardware.
preparationSteps: Design a small processor component such as an ALU, register file, cache controller, or pipeline stage in Verilog or another HDL and verify it with a testbench.
Create a portfolio page showing the block diagram, RTL structure, simulation results, design assumptions, and one performance or power tradeoff you considered.

reasons: This internship can help you practice processor performance modeling, benchmarking, cache analysis, and evaluating how architectural decisions affect real workloads.
preparationSteps: Build a small CPU-performance simulation comparing how cache size, pipeline depth, branch-prediction accuracy, or instruction latency affects execution time.
Benchmark several workloads and create a technical report identifying whether each workload is primarily limited by computation, memory, branching, or parallelism.

reasons: This role can help you build the architecture modeling, experimentation, publication, and advanced digital-systems experience expected for principal processor-design careers.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Computer Science, Engineering, or Mathematics faculty member about a processor-performance, digital-systems, parallel-computing, or architecture project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

By junior year, compare master's and PhD programs in computer engineering, electrical engineering, or computer architecture because principal processor architecture roles typically require extensive industry experience and often advanced technical training.

title: Neuromorphic Hardware Engineer
shortDescription: Designs brain-inspired computing chips that use event-driven neurons, synapses, and local memory structures to process information with extremely low power and support spiking or adaptive neural computation directly in hardware.

reasons: This internship can help you practice RTL design, FPGA development, simulation, and building digital circuits that become the foundation for specialized neuromorphic processors.
preparationSteps: Design and simulate a small digital circuit containing registers, arithmetic logic, control states, and memory, then verify its behavior with a testbench.
Implement a simple digital design on an FPGA if university hardware is available and document resource use, clock speed, inputs, outputs, and observed behavior.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how neural-network computations are mapped onto specialized processors and how hardware designers trade accuracy, throughput, memory, and power consumption.
preparationSteps: Train a small neural network and create a hardware-oriented analysis showing the number of operations, memory requirements, input size, and where computation could be parallelized.
Compare a conventional neural network with a simple spiking neural network and document differences in neuron behavior, communication, timing, and potential energy efficiency.

reasons: This role can help you connect computer architecture with neuroscience, machine learning, digital circuits, and experimental research used to create brain-inspired computing systems.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Engineering, Computer Science, Psychology, or Physics faculty member about a neural computation, FPGA, machine learning, digital hardware, or computational-neuroscience project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

By junior year, compare master's and PhD programs in computer engineering, neuromorphic computing, electrical engineering, or computational neuroscience because advanced neuromorphic R&D often requires graduate-level research.

title: Hardware Cryptographic Lead
shortDescription: Leads the design of cryptographic and hardware-security structures built directly into processors and systems, protecting keys, firmware, memory, and sensitive computation against tampering and physical attacks.

reasons: This internship can help you practice RTL, digital logic, embedded hardware, debugging, and understanding how security features ultimately become physical processor logic.
preparationSteps: Build a small FPGA or digital-logic project implementing an access-control or authentication state machine and verify that unauthorized input sequences cannot reach protected states.
Create a block diagram showing a processor, boot ROM, secure memory, cryptographic engine, hardware root of trust, firmware, and external storage and explain which component establishes trust first.

reasons: This internship can help you practice security architecture, cryptography, threat modeling, secure software or firmware, and analyzing how attackers might compromise trusted systems.
preparationSteps: Create a defensive threat model for a hypothetical embedded device covering firmware modification, stolen keys, unauthorized debug access, memory attacks, and physical tampering and map each threat to a hardware or software control.

Build a small cryptography project implementing established library-based hashing, authentication, or encryption and document where keys should be generated, stored, and protected rather than designing your own cryptographic algorithm.

reasons: This role can help you build deeper knowledge of processor architecture, cryptography, digital circuits, secure hardware, and experimental security analysis needed for senior silicon-security positions.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Engineering, Computer Science, or Mathematics faculty member about a cryptography, embedded-systems, digital-design, verification, or hardware-security project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

Build strong foundations in digital logic, computer architecture, cryptography, and embedded systems and compare graduate programs in computer engineering, hardware security, or electrical engineering because lead-level silicon-security roles typically require years of specialized architecture experience.

title: Robotics Firmware Scientist
shortDescription: Develops hard real-time embedded software that reads robot sensors, controls electric actuators, and executes rapid feedback loops so walking and humanoid robots remain stable, responsive, and safe while moving.

reasons: This internship can help you practice low-level C or C++, microcontrollers, timing, interrupts, sensors, communications, and debugging hardware-connected software.
preparationSteps: Build a microcontroller project that reads a sensor and controls a motor or actuator in a timed feedback loop, then measure response time and stability as your control settings change.
Document the hardware, firmware structure, communication interfaces, timing requirements, failure cases, and debugging process in a technical portfolio entry.

reasons: This internship can help you practice integrating sensor measurements, robot models, control logic, and physical hardware into software that must react reliably in real time.
preparationSteps: Build or simulate a two-wheeled balancing robot or inverted-pendulum system and implement a feedback controller that keeps the system near its target orientation.
Graph sensor readings, control commands, error, and recovery behavior after disturbances and explain where latency or noisy measurements reduce stability.

reasons: This role can help you build deeper experience with robot dynamics, controls, embedded computing, sensor fusion, and experimentation relevant to advanced robotics firmware research.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, or Physics faculty member about an embedded systems, controls, robotics, or sensor-fusion project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.
Develop the project into a research poster or technical report containing the robot model, sensors, controller, timing requirements, experiments, failures, and measured performance.

title: Quantum Computing Hardware Lead
shortDescription: Leads development of the electronic control and readout hardware that generates precise digital, analog, and microwave signals used to manipulate, measure, and coordinate quantum bits inside quantum computers.

reasons: This internship can help you practice PCB design, analog and digital electronics, signal measurement, hardware bring-up, and low-noise circuit development used in quantum-control systems.
preparationSteps: Design or simulate a small mixed-signal board containing power regulation, a clock source, analog conditioning, digital control, and external interfaces and explain why each subsystem is needed.
Use an oscilloscope or university lab equipment to measure noise, timing, or signal integrity on a supervised electronics project and document the measurements and design changes.

reasons: This internship can help you practice deterministic digital control, high-speed interfaces, timing, and programmable hardware commonly used to coordinate quantum experiments.
preparationSteps: Implement a digital pulse generator or timing controller in Verilog and create a testbench verifying pulse width, timing sequence, reset behavior, and invalid input handling.
If university FPGA hardware is available, deploy the design and compare its measured timing against your simulation results.

reasons: This role can help you combine quantum physics with electronics, RF systems, FPGA control, measurement, and experimental hardware development.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Physics or Engineering faculty member about quantum devices, electronics, RF measurement, low-temperature physics, or digital control research that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

By junior year, compare master's and PhD programs in computer engineering, electrical engineering, applied physics, or quantum engineering because technical-lead quantum hardware positions often require advanced specialized training.

title: Avionics Hardware Architect
shortDescription: Architects highly reliable flight computers and avionics electronics that integrate processors, programmable logic, sensors, communication buses, power systems, and redundant hardware for commercial and military aircraft.

reasons: This internship can help you practice electronic-system integration, avionics interfaces, requirements, testing, and understanding how aircraft hardware must operate reliably across many subsystems.
preparationSteps: Create an architecture diagram for a simplified flight computer showing processors, memory, sensors, communication buses, power supplies, redundant channels, cockpit systems, and actuator interfaces.
Create a failure table showing what should happen if one processor, sensor, communication link, or power source becomes unavailable and identify which functions require redundancy.

reasons: This internship can help you practice FPGA or ASIC logic, circuit-card design, verification, interfaces, and hardware development methods used inside modern flight computers.
preparationSteps: Design an FPGA state machine representing a simplified aircraft subsystem and build a testbench covering normal operation, sensor errors, invalid commands, and reset behavior.
Create a technical portfolio entry documenting requirements, block diagrams, interfaces, RTL logic, verification results, and how you prevented one failure from creating an unsafe system state.

reasons: This internship can help you practice processor interfaces, real-time hardware, firmware interaction, communications, and system-level debugging relevant to avionics computers.
preparationSteps: Build a microcontroller or FPGA-based system that reads multiple sensors and communicates their values over a digital bus, then add fault handling for missing or invalid measurements.

Learn the high-level purpose of DO-254, DO-178C, redundancy, built-in test, and deterministic communication because senior avionics architecture roles require rigorous certification and safety engineering in addition to hardware design.

title: Mixed-Signal IC Designer
shortDescription: Designs analog and digital circuits inside semiconductor chips that amplify, filter, sample, and convert real-world radio or electrical signals into clean digital information that processors can use.

reasons: This internship can help you practice transistor-level circuit design, simulation, measurement, and understanding how analog signals are conditioned before digital processing.
preparationSteps: Use SPICE or another circuit simulator to design an amplifier or filter and measure gain, bandwidth, noise, power use, and behavior as component values change.
Create a portfolio page containing the schematic, design equations, simulation plots, assumptions, measured specifications, and the tradeoffs you made between performance and power.

reasons: This internship can help you understand CMOS design, simulation, silicon development, verification, and how analog and digital blocks are combined inside integrated circuits.
preparationSteps: Create a block diagram of a wireless receiver containing an antenna, RF amplifier, mixer, filter, ADC, digital signal-processing block, and processor and explain how the signal changes at each stage.
Compare several ADC architectures at a high level by resolution, speed, power consumption, complexity, and common applications and explain which architecture you would choose for one wireless system.

reasons: This role can help you build deeper circuit-analysis, semiconductor, measurement, and research experience needed for advanced analog and mixed-signal IC design.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Engineering or Physics faculty member about an electronics, signal-processing, semiconductor, or circuit-design project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

By junior year, compare master's and PhD programs in electrical engineering, computer engineering, microelectronics, or integrated-circuit design because advanced mixed-signal design roles commonly value graduate-level circuit specialization.

title: Silicon Verification Lead
shortDescription: Leads pre-silicon testing of complex processor and SoC designs by building automated verification environments that expose logic errors, protocol violations, and overlooked hardware behaviors before chips enter manufacturing.

reasons: This internship can help you practice writing automated hardware tests, debugging RTL, measuring functional coverage, and checking whether digital designs behave correctly across many operating conditions.
preparationSteps: Design a small digital module such as an ALU, FIFO, arbiter, or cache controller in Verilog or SystemVerilog and build a testbench containing normal, boundary, invalid, and randomized test cases.
Create a verification checklist showing each required behavior, stimulus used to test it, expected output, actual result, discovered bugs, and whether every requirement has been covered.

reasons: This internship can help you understand RTL architecture from the designer's perspective, making it easier to identify incorrect behavior and create effective verification strategies.
preparationSteps: Implement a state machine or processor component in HDL and intentionally introduce several controlled logic errors, then create tests that reliably expose each defect.
Use waveform-debugging tools to trace one failing simulation from incorrect output back through internal signals to the RTL statement responsible for the problem.

reasons: This internship can help you practice systematic test development, scripting, debugging, data collection, and checking whether complex hardware satisfies its specifications.
preparationSteps: Write Python scripts that automatically generate test inputs, run simulations, record pass or fail results, and summarize failures for a small digital-hardware project.

Talk with a Loyola Engineering or Computer Science faculty member about a digital systems, FPGA, computer architecture, testing, or verification project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

title: Edge AI Hardware Designer
shortDescription: Designs compact, low-power AI accelerator hardware that processes speech, audio, sensor, and other neural-network workloads directly inside smartphones and embedded devices without relying on cloud computing.

reasons: This internship can help you practice RTL design, digital circuits, simulation, and hardware optimization that form the foundation of neural-processing accelerators.
preparationSteps: Design a small matrix-multiplication or multiply-accumulate block in Verilog or another HDL and verify its behavior with a testbench.
Compare two versions of your design using measurements such as clock speed, resource usage, estimated power, or circuit size and explain which architecture is better for a constrained device.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how neural networks are optimized for limited memory, compute, battery power, and real-time requirements on edge devices.
preparationSteps: Train a small speech-command classifier and deploy or simulate it on a resource-constrained platform, recording its model size, inference time, memory use, and accuracy.
Quantize the model and compare the original and compressed versions to show how reducing numerical precision changes memory requirements, execution speed, and recognition accuracy.

reasons: This role can help you combine computer architecture, signal processing, machine learning, and experimental performance analysis for specialized edge-computing hardware.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Engineering, Computer Science, or Speech-Language-Hearing Sciences faculty member about an embedded AI, speech processing, digital hardware, or signal-processing project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

Build a portfolio experiment comparing how the same speech or audio model performs under different bit widths, memory limits, or hardware configurations and document the accuracy, latency, and efficiency tradeoffs.

title: Optical Computing Lead
shortDescription: Leads development of silicon-photonic circuits, switches, and interconnect architectures that route laser light between processors and computing components to move data with extremely high bandwidth and low energy consumption.

reasons: This internship can help you practice designing, simulating, measuring, and characterizing optical components that guide or manipulate light inside integrated systems.
preparationSteps: Model a simple optical waveguide, coupler, or resonator and investigate how geometry or wavelength changes transmission through the device.
Create a technical portfolio entry containing the device geometry, physical assumptions, simulation results, optical behavior, and one design change that improves performance.

reasons: This internship can help you practice photonic circuit design, chip layout, optical simulation, and integrating optical devices with semiconductor computing hardware.
preparationSteps: Create a simplified photonic circuit containing an input laser, waveguides, splitter or switch, modulator, and photodetectors and explain how information moves through the system.

Compare several routing or switching configurations by insertion loss, number of optical paths, footprint, and scalability and document which architecture you would choose for a small compute interconnect.

reasons: This role can help you connect optics, semiconductor devices, computer architecture, and experimental research used to develop next-generation photonic computing systems.
preparationSteps: Talk with a Loyola Physics, Engineering, or Computer Science faculty member about an optics, electromagnetics, semiconductor, communications, or computing project that could be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

By junior year, compare master's and PhD programs in electrical engineering, computer engineering, photonics, or applied physics because lead-level optical-computing R&D commonly requires substantial photonics specialization and advanced research experience.

title: Central Bank Economist
shortDescription: Builds macroeconomic models and forecasts that help central banks understand inflation, employment, growth, financial conditions, and how interest-rate decisions may affect the wider economy.

reasons: This internship can help you practice cleaning economic data, estimating statistical models, reviewing research, and producing evidence used in macroeconomic and policy analysis.
preparationSteps: Use FRED data to build a Python, R, or Stata project tracking inflation, unemployment, GDP growth, and interest rates over time and explain how the variables move around major economic shocks.
Estimate a simple forecasting model for inflation or unemployment and compare its predictions against actual outcomes using clearly reported forecast errors.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how quantitative economic evidence is translated into policy recommendations for government, monetary, and financial institutions.
preparationSteps: Choose one recent Federal Reserve policy decision and write a short policy memo using inflation, labor-market, and growth data to explain the arguments for holding, raising, or lowering rates.
Create a simple Taylor-rule style project comparing a model-implied policy rate with the actual federal funds rate over several years and explain where the two diverge.

reasons: This role can help you build econometrics, forecasting, literature-review, and faculty research experience that is especially important for doctoral economics admissions.
preparationSteps: Ask an economics professor whether you can assist with data cleaning, literature reviews, econometric analysis, forecasting, or macroeconomic research and aim to produce a poster, paper, or replication project.

By junior year, compare PhD programs in economics and strengthen calculus, linear algebra, probability, econometrics, and research experience because professional central-bank economist positions commonly recruit candidates with economics PhDs.

title: Antitrust Economic Expert
shortDescription: Uses microeconomics, econometrics, and market data to determine whether mergers or business practices reduce competition and may ultimately present economic findings as expert evidence in major antitrust litigation.
usual_employers: U.S. Department of Justice Antitrust Division

reasons: This internship can help you practice using economic theory, statistical analysis, and large datasets to answer questions arising in mergers, litigation, regulation, and competition disputes.
preparationSteps: Choose a completed merger and build a short economic analysis covering the relevant products, major competitors, market shares, concentration, likely substitutes, and arguments for and against competitive harm.
Use public market data to calculate concentration measures before and after the transaction and explain why concentration alone does or does not establish that a merger is anticompetitive.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how economists and government agencies evaluate monopolization, mergers, pricing behavior, and potential harm to consumers.
preparationSteps: Read a public DOJ or FTC merger complaint and create a case brief identifying the proposed market, theory of competitive harm, economic evidence, defendants' likely counterarguments, and final outcome.
Build a small price-and-demand analysis using public or simulated data to estimate whether customers switch toward competing products when prices change.

reasons: This internship can help you practice converting complex datasets into defensible quantitative conclusions and communicating those findings clearly to nontechnical decision-makers.
preparationSteps: Create an econometric project testing a competition-related question such as whether prices vary with market concentration while clearly separating correlation from causal claims.

By junior year, compare PhD programs in economics with strengths in industrial organization, econometrics, or applied microeconomics because economists who independently provide high-stakes expert testimony commonly have doctoral training and extensive consulting or enforcement experience.

title: Chief Development Economist
shortDescription: Leads economic analysis that shapes large international development programs, advising on growth, sovereign debt, structural reforms, poverty reduction, and the policy frameworks attached to multilateral financing for developing countries.
usual_employers: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development

reasons: This internship can help you practice analyzing poverty, growth, employment, trade, inequality, and public-policy data across developing economies.
preparationSteps: Use World Bank Development Indicators to compare two developing countries across GDP growth, poverty, investment, debt, employment, education, and another development measure over at least 10 years.
Turn the analysis into a short policy report identifying one structural constraint on development and support your recommendation with data rather than general observations.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how governments and multilateral institutions combine economic analysis, financing, reforms, and risk assessment when supporting major development programs.
preparationSteps: Study one World Bank Development Policy Financing operation and create a financing brief covering the country's economic problem, financing amount, policy reforms, macroeconomic conditions, expected results, and major risks.

Create a simplified sovereign-debt dashboard containing government debt, debt-to-GDP, fiscal balance, interest costs, growth, and foreign-exchange exposure and explain which trends would make additional borrowing more difficult.

reasons: This role can help you build the quantitative research, policy writing, and international economic experience expected for senior positions at multilateral development institutions.
preparationSteps: Ask an economics professor whether you can assist with development, international economics, sovereign debt, trade, growth, or public-policy research and aim to produce a substantial empirical paper or faculty-supported research project.

By junior year, compare PhD programs in economics and quantitatively rigorous graduate programs in development economics or public policy because chief-economist positions at major development institutions generally follow years of advanced economic research and international policy experience.

title: Behavioral Game Theorist
shortDescription: Designs and tests auction rules for high-value markets such as wireless spectrum, using game theory, behavioral evidence, and simulations to predict bidder strategies and create efficient, competitive outcomes.

reasons: This internship can help you practice applying microeconomics, quantitative analysis, and strategic reasoning to competition, regulation, pricing, and market-design problems.
preparationSteps: Build a Python simulation of a simple auction with several bidders and compare how outcomes change under first-price, second-price, or ascending auction rules.
Write a short analysis explaining how reserve prices, bidder information, budget constraints, or strategic bidding change revenue and allocation efficiency.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how government agencies use economic models and market rules when allocating scarce public resources and regulating industries.
preparationSteps: Study one completed FCC spectrum auction and create a brief covering the licenses sold, auction format, major bidders, revenue, competition concerns, and why regulators selected that auction structure.
Compare two possible auction formats for the same hypothetical spectrum allocation and write a recommendation based on efficiency, competition, strategic behavior, and implementation complexity.

reasons: This role can help you build the mathematical economics, experimentation, econometrics, and research experience expected for advanced market-design and game-theory careers.
preparationSteps: Ask an economics professor whether you can assist with game theory, industrial organization, behavioral economics, experimental economics, or applied microeconomic research and aim to contribute to a paper or substantial research project.

By junior year, compare PhD programs in economics with strengths in market design, game theory, behavioral economics, or industrial organization because research-heavy auction-design careers frequently require doctoral training.

title: Quantitative Macro Researcher
shortDescription: Builds quantitative models of global capital flows, exchange rates, interest rates, debt, and financial conditions to estimate macroeconomic risks and identify economies vulnerable to sharp currency depreciation or financial stress.

reasons: This internship can help you practice forecasting economic variables, analyzing international datasets, and studying how monetary and financial conditions interact across countries.
preparationSteps: Use IMF, World Bank, or FRED data to build a country dashboard containing exchange rates, inflation, interest rates, reserves, external debt, current-account balance, and capital flows over time.
Choose one historical currency crisis and graph how these variables changed during the several years before and after the depreciation.

reasons: This internship can help you practice measuring market and macroeconomic risks and understanding how currencies, interest rates, and international financial conditions affect portfolios and institutions.
preparationSteps: Build a Python project tracking several major currencies and calculate returns, volatility, correlations, maximum drawdowns, and periods of unusually severe depreciation.
Add macroeconomic variables to the project and test whether changes in inflation, interest differentials, foreign reserves, or global risk conditions historically preceded major currency moves.

reasons: This internship can help you understand balance-of-payments dynamics, sovereign risk, international capital movements, and how economic shocks transmit across countries.
preparationSteps: Create a comparative research report on three emerging economies covering foreign reserves, external debt, portfolio flows, current accounts, exchange-rate regimes, and vulnerability to external shocks.

By junior year, seek faculty econometrics or macroeconomic research and compare master's or PhD programs in economics, financial economics, or quantitative macroeconomics if you want research-intensive macro careers.

title: Labor Market Economist
shortDescription: Uses worker, occupation, wage, and industry data to measure how automation and artificial intelligence change employment, job tasks, productivity, skill demand, wages, and workforce structure across the economy.

reasons: This internship can help you practice analyzing employment, wages, occupations, workforce characteristics, and policy questions using real labor-market datasets.
preparationSteps: Use BLS data to compare employment and wage changes across several industries over the past decade and identify occupations that expanded, contracted, or changed substantially.
Create a research report testing whether industries with greater exposure to automation experienced different employment or wage trends while clearly distinguishing correlation from causation.

reasons: This internship can help you practice analyzing employee, occupation, skill, and workforce data while learning how organizations measure structural changes in labor demand.
preparationSteps: Create a dataset linking occupations to tasks and classify which tasks appear most exposed to automation, augmentation, or minimal technological change.
Build a dashboard comparing employment, wages, education requirements, and automation exposure across several occupation groups and explain which patterns deserve further investigation.

reasons: This internship can help you connect quantitative labor-market evidence with workforce policy, education, training, inequality, and technological change.
preparationSteps: Choose one industry undergoing significant automation and create a policy brief covering affected occupations, changing tasks, potential productivity gains, displacement risks, and realistic worker-transition options.

Ask an economics or sociology professor whether you can assist with labor, inequality, technology, demographic, or public-policy research and aim to complete a substantial empirical paper before graduate-school applications.

title: Health Economics Researcher
shortDescription: Uses economic models and healthcare data to measure treatment costs, patient access, utilization, reimbursement, and health outcomes so hospitals, governments, and healthcare organizations can improve care while using limited resources efficiently.

reasons: This internship can help you practice analyzing healthcare costs, utilization, patient outcomes, and access using quantitative economic methods.
preparationSteps: Use public hospital pricing or Medicare data to compare the cost of the same procedure across several hospitals and investigate whether measurable hospital or market characteristics explain some of the variation.
Turn the analysis into a short research report containing your question, dataset, descriptive statistics, economic model, results, limitations, and implications for healthcare access.

reasons: This internship can help you practice working with healthcare datasets, measuring costs and outcomes, and presenting evidence that hospitals or insurers can use when making resource decisions.
preparationSteps: Build a dashboard using public healthcare data that compares hospitals by measures such as utilization, readmissions, cost, patient outcomes, or payer mix.
Choose one hospital-performance metric and use regression or another statistical method to test which measurable factors are most strongly associated with differences between hospitals.

reasons: This role can help you connect economic evidence with reimbursement, insurance, hospital policy, public spending, and decisions about who can access medical care.
preparationSteps: Choose one healthcare policy such as Medicare reimbursement, hospital price transparency, prescription-drug pricing, or insurance subsidies and write a policy memo evaluating its likely effects on cost, access, providers, and patients.

Seek sustained research with an economics or health-policy professor and compare master's or PhD programs in health economics, economics, public policy, or health services research because researcher-level HEOR careers commonly value advanced quantitative training.

title: Trade Policy Director
shortDescription: Leads quantitative and strategic analysis of tariffs, trade agreements, market-access rules, and supply-chain policies to understand how international policy changes affect companies, industries, sourcing networks, and cross-border commerce.
usual_employers: Office of the U.S. Trade Representative

reasons: This internship can help you practice analyzing imports, exports, tariffs, market access, and policy changes affecting companies operating across national borders.
preparationSteps: Use Census, Commerce Department, or USITC trade data to identify the largest import sources for one U.S. industry and calculate how a hypothetical tariff would change the direct landed cost of those imports.
Create a short trade brief explaining which products, countries, companies, and consumers would likely be most exposed and which alternative suppliers could potentially replace affected imports.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how tariffs and trade restrictions affect sourcing, transportation, inventory, supplier selection, and the cost of global production networks.
preparationSteps: Build a spreadsheet or Python model for a hypothetical multinational supply chain and compare total costs before and after tariffs are imposed on one major sourcing country.
Create alternative sourcing scenarios and measure changes in product cost, transportation distance, supplier concentration, lead time, and exposure to additional trade restrictions.

reasons: This role can help you practice quantitative trade research, policy writing, and evaluating how government decisions propagate through industries and the broader economy.
preparationSteps: Choose one major tariff change and build a before-and-after analysis covering import volumes, prices, affected industries, sourcing shifts, and possible retaliation using public economic data.

Ask an economics or international-business professor whether you can assist with trade, globalization, supply chains, international economics, or policy research and aim to complete a substantial empirical paper or faculty-supported project.

title: Environmental Economist
shortDescription: Uses economic models to estimate how carbon prices, environmental taxes, regulations, and climate investments can reduce pollution while managing impacts on economic growth, households, government revenue, and industry competitiveness.

reasons: This internship can help you practice analyzing environmental policy, emissions data, economic costs, and incentives using quantitative economic methods.
preparationSteps: Use public emissions and economic data to compare carbon emissions, GDP, energy use, and carbon prices across several countries and investigate how those variables changed after major climate policies.
Build a simple carbon-tax model estimating emissions reductions, government revenue, and industry costs under several possible prices per ton of carbon dioxide.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how governments compare carbon taxes, emissions trading, subsidies, regulations, and other policies when pursuing climate targets.
preparationSteps: Choose one existing carbon tax or emissions-trading program and create a policy brief covering its carbon price, industries covered, emissions trend, revenue use, and major economic tradeoffs.

Compare three ways carbon-pricing revenue could be used, such as household rebates, lower taxes, or clean-energy investment, and explain how each option changes the distributional and economic effects of the policy.

reasons: This role can help you build econometrics, environmental-policy modeling, academic research, and technical writing skills used in advanced environmental economics.
preparationSteps: Ask an economics professor whether you can assist with environmental economics, energy markets, public policy, climate, taxation, or applied econometric research and aim to produce a substantial empirical paper.

By junior year, strengthen calculus, linear algebra, econometrics, and research experience and compare PhD programs in economics with environmental, energy, or public-economics concentrations because research economist positions frequently require doctoral training.

title: Urban Development Economist
shortDescription: Analyzes how zoning, housing construction, transportation access, and urban development policies affect real estate values, rents, housing supply, displacement, affordability, and broader risks of housing instability and homelessness.
usual_employers: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
City Planning and Economic Development Agencies

reasons: This internship can help you practice analyzing housing, zoning, transportation, demographics, and development policies affecting cities and neighborhoods.
preparationSteps: Choose one city zoning reform and create a before-and-after dataset tracking permits, housing units, rents, property values, population, and other available neighborhood indicators.
Write a short policy memo explaining which outcomes changed after the reform while clearly identifying which changes can and cannot confidently be attributed to zoning.

reasons: This internship can help you practice analyzing property values, rents, development feasibility, neighborhood demand, and the economics behind new housing construction.
preparationSteps: Use public real estate or Census data to model housing prices or rents across neighborhoods using variables such as location, density, income, transit access, and housing characteristics.
Build a simple development model comparing whether the same parcel is financially viable under several zoning scenarios with different allowable unit counts or building sizes.

reasons: This role can help you study housing supply, affordability, homelessness, displacement, and neighborhood change using economic and demographic data.
preparationSteps: Use Census, HUD, and local housing data to compare rent burden, vacancy rates, housing construction, income, and homelessness across several cities and investigate which housing-market variables move together.

Ask an economics, sociology, or public-policy professor whether you can assist with housing, urban economics, inequality, real estate, or demographic research and aim to complete a rigorous empirical project before graduate-school applications.

title: ESG Investment Director
shortDescription: Leads investment analysis that combines financial performance with environmental and sustainability risks, helping private equity and asset management firms decide which companies to invest in and how portfolio companies can improve environmental performance.

reasons: This internship can help you build the financial analysis, company research, Excel, and investment-writing skills you need before adding sustainability factors to investment decisions.
preparationSteps: Pick one public company and use its latest annual report to make a one-page investment summary covering revenue growth, profitability, debt, major risks, and why you would or would not invest.

Build a simple Excel valuation using public company data and practice calculating revenue growth, margins, valuation multiples, and a basic investment return instead of trying to start with a complicated private equity model.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how investors compare traditional financial information with environmental risks, emissions, resource use, and sustainability opportunities.
preparationSteps: Take the same company you analyzed financially and read its sustainability report, then add five environmental items to your investment note such as emissions, energy use, water use, waste, and climate-related risks.
Compare two companies in the same industry and make a one-page scorecard showing both their financial performance and a few clearly measurable environmental indicators.

reasons: This internship can help you practice collecting environmental data, checking whether goals are being met, and presenting sustainability information clearly to decision-makers.
preparationSteps: Check Loyola's Office of Sustainability student opportunities and apply for or ask about helping with an existing campus project involving waste, composting, climate action, or sustainability data.
Turn one campus or public sustainability dataset into a simple Excel or Power BI dashboard tracking a few measures such as waste, electricity, emissions, or recycling over time.

title: Environmental Law Counsel
shortDescription: Represents governments, organizations, communities, or companies in major legal disputes involving pollution, hazardous waste, environmental permits, cleanup responsibility, and compliance with federal environmental laws.

reasons: This internship can help you practice researching laws, reading cases, organizing evidence, writing clearly, and seeing how attorneys prepare legal arguments.
preparationSteps: Meet with Loyola's pre-law advisor by junior year and use the Pre-Law Program to map out your law-school timeline, courses, LSAT preparation, and application requirements.
Read one recent DOJ or EPA environmental enforcement case and write a one-page summary covering what happened, which law was involved, what evidence mattered, and how the case ended.

reasons: This internship can help you learn the laws and regulations behind environmental disputes before you are expected to understand courtroom litigation.
preparationSteps: Choose one issue such as water pollution, hazardous waste, air pollution, or PFAS and make a two-page briefing explaining the environmental problem, the main federal law that applies, and which government agency enforces it.
Attend one public environmental hearing, city meeting, agency webinar, or policy event and take notes on the different arguments being made by government, businesses, and community members.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how agencies investigate violations, write regulations, build enforcement cases, and work with attorneys.
preparationSteps: Search EPA, state environmental agencies, attorney general offices, local government, and environmental nonprofits for undergraduate internships rather than limiting your search to positions labeled specifically as environmental litigation.

Plan for a J.D. after college if you want to personally litigate cases: during junior year, begin structured LSAT preparation and identify two professors who know your writing and analytical work well enough to eventually provide recommendations.

title: Circular Economy Architect
shortDescription: Redesigns packaging and material systems so companies use less virgin material, reuse packaging where possible, increase recycled content, and keep discarded packaging in recycling or recovery loops instead of sending it to landfill.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how companies choose packaging materials, test new designs, reduce material use, and balance sustainability with cost, durability, and customer needs.
preparationSteps: Collect 10 everyday packages from groceries, toiletries, or deliveries and make a spreadsheet listing the material, number of separate pieces, whether each piece is reusable or recyclable locally, and one realistic redesign idea.

Pick one of those packages and make a simple before-and-after concept showing how you could remove a component, use less material, make it easier to recycle, or replace single-use packaging with a reusable option.

reasons: This internship can help you practice waste reduction, recycling, sustainability communication, and working on environmental improvements within an organization.
preparationSteps: Contact Loyola's Office of Sustainability about its student internship or volunteer opportunities and ask specifically whether you can help with waste management, composting, reusable dining programs, or a small waste-reduction project.

Do a simple one-day or one-week packaging audit in a dorm, club, event, or other accessible setting by counting the most common disposable items and identifying the three easiest items to reduce or replace.

reasons: This internship can help you understand where packaging comes from, how it moves through companies and customers, and why reuse or recycling systems have to work across the entire supply chain.
preparationSteps: Choose one familiar product and draw its packaging journey from material supplier to manufacturer, store or delivery, customer use, and final disposal or recycling.

Identify one point in that journey where packaging becomes waste and write three practical options for reducing it, such as reusable shipping containers, lighter packaging, recycled material, or a take-back system.

title: Renewable Energy Asset Lead
shortDescription: Leads the development and grid connection of large wind-energy portfolios, coordinating engineering, utilities, permitting, transmission, financing, construction, and operations across multiple projects and regions.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how wind and other renewable projects move from an early idea through permitting, engineering, construction, and operation.
preparationSteps: Choose one operating wind farm and make a one-page project profile covering its location, number of turbines, approximate capacity, utility or grid region, owner, and when it began operating.

Search wind developers, utilities, energy companies, and engineering firms for general renewable-energy internships instead of limiting yourself to positions specifically labeled wind asset management.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how new wind generation connects to transmission networks and what utilities evaluate before allowing a project onto the grid.
preparationSteps: Learn which regional grid operator serves one wind project, such as PJM, MISO, ERCOT, or NYISO, and draw a simple diagram showing the wind farm, substation, transmission lines, and wider grid connection.

Talk with a Loyola Engineering or Physics professor about a renewable-energy, electrical-grid, or energy-systems project you could assist with during the school year or potentially develop for a future Hauber Summer Research Fellowship proposal.

reasons: This internship can help you practice coordinating schedules, permits, budgets, land issues, engineering work, and outside stakeholders across large infrastructure projects.
preparationSteps: Make a simple Excel tracker for a hypothetical wind project with columns for site selection, land agreements, environmental review, permitting, grid connection, financing, construction, and completion status.
Use one class, club, campus event, or personal project to practice managing deadlines and multiple contributors, then keep a short record of what you organized and what changed because of your work.

title: Industrial Carbon Auditor
shortDescription: Measures and verifies greenhouse-gas emissions from manufacturing operations, tracing energy, fuels, materials, and industrial processes to identify where companies can reduce their carbon footprints.

reasons: This internship can help you practice collecting energy and emissions data, checking environmental metrics, and identifying practical opportunities to reduce an organization's footprint.
preparationSteps: Choose one familiar organization or campus activity and make a simple emissions spreadsheet covering electricity, fuel, transportation, and waste using publicly available conversion factors.
Check Loyola sustainability opportunities or local organizations for a project involving energy, waste, emissions, or environmental data where you can help collect or organize real measurements.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how industrial equipment, fuels, chemicals, energy use, and production processes create environmental impacts.
