preparationSteps: Pick a simple manufacturing process such as producing glass, plastic, steel, food, or chemicals and draw the major steps, including where electricity, heat, fuel, and raw materials enter the process.
Identify three places in that process where emissions might be reduced through lower energy use, different materials, recycling, or cleaner equipment and explain each idea in plain language.

reasons: This internship can help you practice checking whether reported numbers are accurate, tracing data back to evidence, documenting inconsistencies, and working carefully with spreadsheets.
preparationSteps: Choose a company's sustainability report and pick five reported environmental numbers, then make a spreadsheet listing the metric, reporting year, units, stated methodology, and whether the company explains where the number came from.
Take an accounting, statistics, or data-analysis class project and practice keeping your calculations organized enough that another student could follow your inputs and reproduce your final number.

title: Conservation Geneticist
shortDescription: Uses DNA and genomic data to measure genetic diversity, relatedness, inbreeding, and population history so conservation teams can protect endangered species and make healthier breeding and population-management decisions.

reasons: This internship can help you practice DNA work, biological data collection, laboratory methods, and research documentation before specializing in endangered-species genetics.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Biology professor whether you can help with a genetics, ecology, evolution, molecular biology, or environmental biology project during the semester, even if the project is not specifically about endangered animals.

If the project becomes a good fit, talk with the professor about developing it into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle so you can gain sustained faculty-mentored research experience.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how population monitoring, field observations, habitat conditions, and species-management decisions connect with genetic information.
preparationSteps: Apply to zoos, wildlife agencies, conservation nonprofits, parks, and environmental organizations for general conservation or wildlife internships instead of waiting for an internship labeled specifically as conservation genetics.

Choose one endangered species and make a one-page profile covering current population size, major threats, geographic range, known genetic concerns, and what conservation organizations are currently doing to protect it.

reasons: This internship can help you practice using code and statistics to analyze biological data, which is increasingly important in conservation genomics.
preparationSteps: Use a small public genetics dataset and practice loading it into R or Python, cleaning the data, calculating simple summary statistics, and creating a few clear visualizations.
Keep the project on GitHub or in a simple portfolio folder with a short explanation of the biological question, where the data came from, what you calculated, and what the results appear to show.

title: Sustainable Urban Planner
shortDescription: Plans neighborhoods, public spaces, transit networks, walking and biking infrastructure, and land-use policies that help cities reduce transportation emissions while remaining accessible, safe, and practical for residents.

reasons: This internship can help you practice reviewing development plans, mapping neighborhoods, researching policies, and seeing how cities decide what gets built and where.
preparationSteps: Choose one Baltimore neighborhood and use Google Maps, city GIS data, or another mapping tool to mark housing, parks, schools, transit stops, major roads, sidewalks, and vacant or underused land.

Write a one-page recommendation for one realistic improvement such as a safer crossing, bus-stop upgrade, bike connection, small public space, or better pedestrian route and support it with what you observed.

reasons: This internship can help you practice transit, walking, biking, traffic, and accessibility analysis while learning how transportation projects affect sustainability and daily life.
preparationSteps: Pick one trip you regularly make and compare driving, transit, biking, and walking by travel time, approximate cost, convenience, and environmental impact.

Look for internships with city transportation departments, transit agencies, metropolitan planning organizations, and consulting firms using broad searches rather than searching only for sustainable urban planning.

reasons: This internship can help you connect climate goals with practical city projects involving transportation, public spaces, land use, waste, and community programs.
preparationSteps: Check Loyola's sustainability, student government, or campus planning opportunities and volunteer for one project involving transportation, public space, waste, energy, or campus accessibility where you can help collect information or organize a real improvement.

Create a small portfolio page showing the problem, what you observed or measured, the improvement you suggested, and any map, chart, photo, or result that makes the project easy for an employer to understand.

title: Partner, Forensic Accounting
shortDescription: Leads complex investigations into fraud, money laundering, corruption, accounting misconduct, and suspicious financial transactions, helping companies, attorneys, regulators, and law-enforcement agencies understand where money moved and what financial evidence shows.

reasons: This internship can help you practice reviewing financial records, spotting inconsistencies, organizing evidence, and tracing transactions during fraud or misconduct investigations.
preparationSteps: Choose a completed public fraud or accounting-enforcement case from the SEC or DOJ and make a one-page case summary showing what happened, which financial records revealed the problem, and how investigators reached their conclusion.
Create a simple Excel exercise with fictional bank transactions and practice sorting payments by date, amount, sender, recipient, and category so you can clearly explain where money moved.

reasons: This internship can help you learn financial statements, internal controls, evidence gathering, documentation, and how accountants verify whether reported information is reliable.
preparationSteps: Take one company annual report and practice connecting the income statement, balance sheet, and cash-flow statement, then write down three places where an auditor would want supporting evidence.

Apply broadly to public accounting firms, corporate accounting departments, government audit offices, and consulting firms instead of waiting for an internship labeled specifically as forensic accounting.

reasons: This internship can help you understand financial controls, suspicious activity, regulatory requirements, and how organizations prevent financial misconduct before an investigation is needed.
preparationSteps: Read one public money-laundering enforcement case and create a short timeline showing the organizations involved, suspicious financial activity, red flags identified by investigators, and final enforcement action.
During college, work toward the accounting coursework needed for CPA eligibility in the state where you expect to work and learn what the CFE credential requires for later in your career.

title: International Tax Counsel
shortDescription: Advises multinational companies on the legal tax consequences of cross-border investments, acquisitions, financing, intellectual property, and corporate structures so international business is organized efficiently and complies with tax laws across jurisdictions.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how businesses calculate taxes, organize supporting information, research tax rules, and handle transactions with different tax consequences.
preparationSteps: Pick one multinational public company and read the income-tax section of its latest annual report, then make a one-page note explaining its effective tax rate, foreign operations, and any major tax issues mentioned.
Apply broadly to accounting firms, corporate tax departments, and tax-advisory teams for undergraduate tax internships so you can learn the accounting side before law school.

reasons: This internship can help you practice legal research, writing, document review, and understanding how attorneys advise businesses.
preparationSteps: Meet with Loyola's pre-law advising resources and make a simple timeline for LSAT preparation, law-school applications, recommendation letters, and graduation because becoming tax counsel requires earning a J.D.

Choose one international tax topic such as tax treaties, foreign tax credits, transfer pricing, or the global minimum tax and write a two-page beginner-friendly summary using IRS, OECD, or law-firm resources.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how multinational companies organize operations, suppliers, subsidiaries, financing, and transactions across countries before you specialize in their tax treatment.
preparationSteps: Choose one multinational company and draw a simple map showing its headquarters, major international markets, manufacturing locations, and important subsidiaries using only publicly available information.

Take an international business, accounting, or finance class project and focus it on one real cross-border transaction so you can practice connecting business decisions with financial and legal considerations.

title: Chief Audit Executive (CAE)
shortDescription: Leads an organization's independent internal audit function, reviewing financial reporting, operations, controls, compliance, technology, and enterprise risks and reporting major findings to executive leadership and the board.

reasons: This internship can help you practice reviewing business processes, testing controls, documenting problems, and explaining practical improvements to managers.
preparationSteps: Choose a simple process you already understand, such as a student organization collecting dues or purchasing supplies, and draw the steps from receiving money through recording, approving, and spending it.
Identify three basic controls that would reduce mistakes or misuse, such as requiring receipts, separating approval from payment, or reconciling the account each month.

reasons: This internship can help you build strong accounting fundamentals, evidence-testing skills, financial statement knowledge, and professional documentation habits.
preparationSteps: Use one public company's annual report to find its auditor's report and internal-control discussion, then write a short explanation of what management is responsible for versus what the external auditor checks.
Apply to public accounting firms of different sizes, including regional firms, because a broad audit internship is a realistic first step toward later internal-audit and leadership roles.

reasons: This internship can help you see how financial, operational, regulatory, and technology risks are identified and monitored across an organization.
preparationSteps: Create a simple risk register for a campus club, small business, or class case with columns for the risk, likelihood, possible impact, current control, and one improvement you would recommend.

During college, learn the CPA and CIA pathways and prioritize strong internships in accounting, audit, risk, or compliance; CAE is a late-career role, so your immediate goal is building solid audit fundamentals rather than trying to prepare for executive responsibilities now.

title: SEC Financial Reporting Lead
shortDescription: Leads the preparation and review of a public company's SEC filings, financial statements, disclosures, and reporting controls so investors receive accurate information that follows U.S. GAAP and federal reporting requirements.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how accountants check financial statements, gather supporting evidence, test controls, and document whether reported information is reliable.
preparationSteps: Pick one public company and read its latest 10-K, focusing first on the income statement, balance sheet, cash-flow statement, footnotes, and independent auditor's report.
Apply broadly to public accounting firms and corporate accounting departments for audit or assurance internships instead of waiting for an internship specifically labeled SEC reporting.

reasons: This internship can help you practice preparing financial schedules, checking account balances, supporting quarterly reporting, and organizing information used in external financial statements.
preparationSteps: Use two consecutive annual reports from the same company and make a simple spreadsheet comparing revenue, operating income, cash flow, debt, and several important footnote disclosures year over year.
Practice writing a one-page explanation of the largest changes you found so that someone without an accounting background could understand what changed and why it matters.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how day-to-day accounting records eventually become the financial statements and disclosures filed by public companies.
preparationSteps: Take a class accounting exercise and practice tracing several transactions from journal entries through account balances and into the final financial statements.

During college, check the CPA education requirements for the state where you expect to work and plan your accounting coursework early because senior SEC-reporting roles frequently prefer or require CPA-level expertise.

title: Corporate Valuation Principal
shortDescription: Leads financial analysis used to estimate what companies, business units, and complex assets are worth during mergers, acquisitions, financial reporting, and other major corporate transactions.

reasons: This internship can help you practice analyzing businesses, building financial models, comparing companies, and explaining why a company may be worth more or less than its current market price.
preparationSteps: Choose one public company and build a basic Excel valuation using its revenue, operating profit, cash flow, debt, and a few comparable companies from the same industry.
Write a one-page conclusion giving a reasonable valuation range and explain which two or three assumptions have the biggest effect on your answer.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how financial statements, company forecasts, due diligence, and valuation are used when businesses are bought or sold.
preparationSteps: Choose one recently announced merger and make a short deal summary covering the buyer, target, purchase price, target revenue, reason for the acquisition, and how the purchase price compares with the target's prior market value.
Read the valuation section of a public merger filing or fairness opinion and make a simple list of the methods the financial advisor used, such as DCF, comparable companies, or prior transactions.

reasons: This internship can help you build the financial-statement, forecasting, Excel, and business-analysis skills that valuation professionals use every day.
preparationSteps: Take one finance or accounting class project and turn it into a clean portfolio piece with a company overview, financial analysis, charts, assumptions, and a short recommendation.
Apply broadly to corporate finance, FP&A, investment banking, accounting advisory, and valuation internships because each can build useful valuation experience before you specialize.

title: ESG Accounting Specialist
shortDescription: Builds reporting controls and assurance procedures that help companies prove environmental and sustainability metrics such as greenhouse-gas emissions, energy use, waste, and other disclosures are complete, consistent, and supported by evidence.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how accountants test evidence, document controls, verify reported numbers, and decide whether information can be relied upon.
preparationSteps: Take one company's sustainability report and choose five environmental numbers such as emissions, electricity, water, or waste, then make a spreadsheet showing the reported value, unit, reporting year, and any explanation of how the company calculated it.
For each number, write down what evidence you would want to see before trusting it, such as utility bills, fuel records, meter readings, invoices, or calculation worksheets.

reasons: This internship can help you practice gathering sustainability information, checking calculations, and turning environmental data into organized company reporting.
preparationSteps: Find a sustainability report from a company you recognize and make a one-page summary of its largest environmental goals, current progress, and which metrics appear easiest or hardest to verify.

Look for a campus, nonprofit, or internship opportunity where you can help track real data such as electricity, waste, recycling, transportation, or emissions and practice keeping the source documents organized.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how organizations design checks that prevent reporting errors and make data easier for auditors to verify later.
preparationSteps: Create a simple reporting process for one environmental metric showing who collects the number, where it comes from, who reviews it, what evidence is saved, and what happens if the number looks unusual.
Practice explaining your process to a classmate and ask them to reproduce the final number using only your instructions and saved evidence; fix anything they cannot follow.

title: Bankruptcy Restructuring Lead
shortDescription: Leads financial analysis for distressed companies, estimating cash needs, asset values, debt obligations, and creditor recoveries to help businesses and lenders make decisions during major restructurings and bankruptcies.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how analysts review struggling businesses, cash flow, debt, assets, and possible turnaround or bankruptcy options.
preparationSteps: Choose one well-known company that filed for Chapter 11 and make a one-page timeline covering what caused its financial trouble, how much debt it had, what happened during bankruptcy, and whether the company reorganized or sold major assets.
Open the company's final annual report before bankruptcy and make a simple Excel sheet tracking cash, total debt, revenue, operating income, and operating cash flow for the previous three years.

reasons: This internship can help you build financial-statement, valuation, due-diligence, and Excel skills that transfer directly into restructuring work.
preparationSteps: Pick one public company and write a short financial health check covering profitability, debt, available cash, and whether its cash flow appears strong enough to support its obligations.
Apply broadly to accounting firms and consulting firms for transaction advisory, deals, valuation, or financial due-diligence internships rather than searching only for bankruptcy positions.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how lenders and investors value assets, evaluate debt, and decide what to do when a property or borrower is financially stressed.
preparationSteps: Choose one commercial property listing and make a basic spreadsheet showing the asking price, estimated annual income if available, financing assumptions, and how much value would remain after paying off hypothetical debt.
Search banks, commercial real estate firms, lenders, valuation firms, and advisory companies for general real estate finance internships to gain experience working with assets and debt.

title: Accounting Information Architect
shortDescription: Designs the cloud systems that move financial transactions from business activities into accounting records, connecting ledgers, approvals, databases, integrations, and security controls across large organizations.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how business processes are translated into software workflows, databases, approvals, and system requirements.
preparationSteps: Choose a simple process such as a student organization buying supplies and draw the steps from purchase request to approval, payment, accounting record, and final account balance.
Turn that process into a clean flowchart using Draw.io, Lucidchart, or another diagramming tool and label where information enters the system, who approves it, and where the final record is stored.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how accounting rules and software work together to record transactions accurately across a company.
preparationSteps: Create a small Excel or database example containing sales, purchases, transaction dates, account names, and amounts, then show how the individual transactions add up to summary account balances.
Use Loyola accounting and information-systems coursework to build one portfolio example that shows both sides of the field: the accounting process and the system or database that supports it.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how companies protect financial systems, restrict access, test controls, and prevent one person from having too much control over a transaction.
preparationSteps: Take the process flow you created and mark which person should be allowed to request, approve, pay, and record a transaction, making sure one person does not control every step.
Apply broadly to IT audit, technology risk, accounting systems, and information-systems internships at accounting firms, banks, consulting firms, and large companies.

title: Public Finance Director
shortDescription: Leads financial planning for major cities and public agencies, helping manage tax and other revenues, budgets, capital projects, municipal bonds, debt obligations, and long-term funding decisions.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how cities collect revenue, build budgets, pay for public services, and keep track of taxpayer money.
preparationSteps: Download the current budget for Baltimore or another city and make a one-page summary showing its largest revenue sources, largest spending categories, and major capital projects.
Search city, county, state, transit-agency, and other government websites for general finance, budget, accounting, or analyst internships instead of looking only for positions labeled public finance.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how cities and public agencies borrow money for infrastructure and how analysts evaluate municipal finances before bonds are issued.
preparationSteps: Find one recent municipal bond issue for a city, school system, transit agency, or utility and write down how much was borrowed, what the money will fund, when the debt matures, and how repayment is expected to occur.
Create a simple Excel sheet comparing two cities using population, annual revenue, outstanding debt, and debt per resident so you can practice explaining why their borrowing situations may differ.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how government accounting, financial reporting, tax revenues, and spending records support larger public-finance decisions.
preparationSteps: Open one city's annual financial report and identify its major funds, revenue sources, debt balance, and capital assets, then write a short explanation of what each section tells residents about the city's finances.
Use an accounting or economics class assignment to analyze a real local-government budget or financial report so you have one public-sector project to discuss during internship interviews.

title: Financial Fraud Expert Witness
shortDescription: Uses forensic accounting to reconstruct suspicious transactions, trace money through companies and accounts, measure financial losses, and explain complex fraud evidence clearly in legal disputes and court proceedings.

reasons: This internship can help you practice reviewing financial records, identifying suspicious transactions, organizing evidence, and understanding how accountants investigate possible fraud.
preparationSteps: Choose a completed SEC, DOJ, or state fraud case and make a one-page timeline showing how the scheme worked, where the money moved, how investigators discovered it, and what evidence supported the case.
Create a small fictional transaction dataset in Excel and practice filtering payments by person, company, date, and amount until you can clearly show the path money took through several accounts.

reasons: This internship can help you build the financial-statement, evidence-testing, documentation, and internal-control skills that forensic accountants rely on during investigations.
preparationSteps: Take one public company's financial statements and identify several balances that would need outside evidence to verify, such as cash, inventory, revenue, or accounts receivable.
Apply broadly to audit and assurance internships at national, regional, and local accounting firms because traditional audit experience is a strong starting point for later forensic work.

reasons: This internship can help you practice organizing financial evidence and explaining complicated numerical findings in a way attorneys, clients, and eventually courts can understand.
preparationSteps: Take one fraud case you studied and explain it in a short presentation without accounting jargon, using a simple timeline or transaction diagram that someone outside accounting could follow.

During college, build toward CPA eligibility and learn about later credentials such as the CFE or CFF, but focus first on strong accounting coursework, internships, and clear written communication rather than expert-witness credentials.

title: Quantum Cryptographic Researcher
shortDescription: Designs and analyzes post-quantum cryptographic algorithms intended to protect digital information against attacks from both classical computers and future quantum computers.
usual_employers: National Institute of Standards and Technology

reasons: This internship can help you practice mathematical reasoning, implementing cryptographic algorithms, testing assumptions, and reading technical security research.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Mathematics, Computer Science, or Engineering professor whether you can help with a project involving number theory, algorithms, cybersecurity, discrete mathematics, or cryptography that could potentially become a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

Implement one established post-quantum algorithm or simplified cryptographic example from a reputable educational source and write a short explanation of what mathematical problem provides its security.

reasons: This internship can help you build proof-writing, abstract mathematics, computational experimentation, and faculty research experience needed for graduate cryptography research.
preparationSteps: Look through Loyola's Hauber, NSF REU, and NIST SURF opportunities and identify programs involving algebra, number theory, algorithms, discrete mathematics, or cybersecurity that you could realistically apply to next cycle.

During junior year, compare Ph.D. programs in mathematics and computer science with cryptography faculty and make a checklist of their expected coursework, research experience, recommendation letters, and application deadlines.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how cryptographic ideas are implemented inside real software and where mathematical security can fail because of poor implementation.
preparationSteps: Build a small program using a standard cryptography library to encrypt, decrypt, sign, and verify sample data, then document what the library handles for you instead of trying to invent your own encryption.

Strengthen linear algebra, number theory, algorithms, and proof-based mathematics and aim to build relationships with two quantitative faculty members who could later speak about your research ability in graduate-school recommendations.

title: Principal Biostatistician
shortDescription: Leads the statistical design and analysis of clinical studies, creating rigorous methods to determine whether new treatments such as genetic and gene therapies are safe, effective, and supported by reliable evidence.

reasons: This internship can help you practice applying statistics to real biological or health questions and interpreting results instead of only completing textbook exercises.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Mathematics, Statistics, or Biology professor whether you can assist with a health, genetics, biology, or statistics research project and discuss whether it could be developed for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

Use a public health or biology dataset to answer one clear question in R or Python, producing a few statistical tests or models, visualizations, and a short explanation of what the results do and do not prove.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how patient data, study protocols, treatment groups, endpoints, and research documentation come together in clinical trials.
preparationSteps: Find one published clinical trial involving a genetic or advanced therapy and make a one-page summary of the treatment groups, sample size, primary endpoint, statistical result, and major limitation.

Search hospitals, universities, biotechnology companies, and research centers for broad clinical research or data internships instead of waiting for a position specifically labeled gene-therapy biostatistics.

reasons: This role can help you build the statistical theory, coding, research writing, and faculty mentorship expected before entering graduate biostatistics programs.
preparationSteps: Explore Loyola's SIBS, REU, Hauber, and other summer quantitative research options and aim to complete at least one sustained statistics or health-data research experience before graduation.

By junior year, compare M.S. and Ph.D. programs in biostatistics and statistics, checking prerequisites such as calculus, linear algebra, probability, mathematical statistics, programming, and research experience so you can fill any gaps before applying.

title: High-Frequency Quant Developer
shortDescription: Builds and optimizes automated trading systems that process market data, evaluate quantitative strategies, and send orders to financial exchanges with extremely low latency.

reasons: This internship can help you build strong programming, debugging, algorithms, and systems skills before specializing in ultra-fast trading software.
preparationSteps: Build one C++ project where speed actually matters, such as processing a large file or stream of simulated messages, and compare how long two different implementations take to run.
Apply broadly to software engineering, systems engineering, and quantitative-development internships rather than limiting yourself to internships specifically labeled high-frequency trading.

reasons: This internship can help you connect programming and probability with market data, trading strategies, execution, and financial decision-making.
preparationSteps: Use historical market data to build a simple event-driven trading simulation that reads prices, generates a basic rule-based signal, records trades, and calculates returns without trying to create a profitable HFT strategy.
Learn basic order-book concepts such as bids, asks, spreads, market orders, limit orders, and fills so you can explain what your code would actually be interacting with in an electronic market.

reasons: This internship can help you study operating systems, processors, networking, algorithms, and performance measurement at the deeper level needed for advanced low-latency engineering.
preparationSteps: Ask a Computer Science, Mathematics, or Engineering professor about research involving algorithms, systems, networking, optimization, or high-performance computing and try to produce a substantial project, poster, or research result before graduate-school applications.

Compare master's and Ph.D. programs in computer science, computer engineering, applied mathematics, or quantitative finance and note which programs offer systems, algorithms, optimization, probability, and high-performance computing courses relevant to advanced quant development.

title: Actuarial Director
shortDescription: Leads advanced pricing and risk models for commercial and specialty insurance, combining historical losses, catastrophe models, exposure data, and financial assumptions to determine sustainable prices for large and uncertain risks.

reasons: This internship can help you practice probability, insurance pricing, loss analysis, Excel, and communicating quantitative findings to insurance teams.
preparationSteps: Use a small insurance-style dataset to calculate claim frequency, average claim size, expected annual losses, and how the estimated price changes when the assumed loss rate changes.

After completing enough probability coursework, review the current actuarial Exam P and Exam FM pathways and choose one realistic first exam to prepare for rather than trying to study the entire credential sequence at once.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how insurers estimate losses from hurricanes, floods, earthquakes, wildfires, and other rare but financially severe events.
preparationSteps: Choose one recent hurricane or other major disaster and make a simple spreadsheet comparing insured losses, affected locations, property exposure, and the different estimates reported before and after the event.

Ask a Loyola Mathematics or Statistics professor about a probability, risk, simulation, or extreme-events research project that could build toward faculty research or the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

reasons: This internship can help you build the statistics, coding, forecasting, and data-analysis skills used in actuarial pricing and portfolio risk work.
preparationSteps: Build a small Python or Excel project that groups fictional insurance policies by characteristics such as location or coverage amount and compares average losses across those groups.

During junior year, compare M.S. programs in actuarial science, statistics, applied mathematics, or risk management if you want deeper catastrophe-modeling training, while keeping ACAS and eventually FCAS credential progress as the main professional pathway.

title: Operations Research Scientist
shortDescription: Builds mathematical optimization models that help large organizations move products across warehouses, factories, ports, and countries faster while balancing shipping cost, capacity, inventory, and delivery constraints.

reasons: This internship can help you practice turning real scheduling, routing, capacity, and resource problems into mathematical models.
preparationSteps: Create a small shipping problem with three warehouses and several destinations, then use Excel Solver or Python to find the cheapest way to meet every destination's demand without exceeding warehouse capacity.
Save the model, assumptions, final solution, and one simple chart in a portfolio folder and explain in plain language what decision the optimization model improved.

reasons: This internship can help you understand the real shipping costs, inventory limits, delivery requirements, and operational constraints that optimization models eventually need to represent.
preparationSteps: Choose a familiar product and map a simple path from supplier to warehouse to customer, then list where delays, extra shipping costs, or capacity limits could occur.

Build a spreadsheet comparing two or three shipping plans by total cost, average delivery time, and number of shipments so you can practice explaining tradeoffs before using more advanced optimization.

reasons: This role can help you build the mathematical modeling, programming, faculty research, and technical-writing experience expected by graduate Operations Research programs.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, or Information Systems professor whether you can help with an optimization, scheduling, simulation, logistics, or decision-modeling project and discuss whether it could grow into a future Hauber proposal.

By junior year, compare M.S. and Ph.D. programs in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, or Applied Mathematics and make a short checklist of their prerequisites in calculus, linear algebra, probability, programming, and optimization.

title: Algorithmic Topologist
shortDescription: Uses computational topology and topological data analysis to extract meaningful shapes and structural patterns from complex datasets such as MRI, CT, and other medical images.
usual_employers: University of Utah Scientific Computing and Imaging Institute

reasons: This internship can help you build proof-based mathematics, computational experimentation, and faculty research experience before specializing in topology.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Mathematics professor about research involving geometry, topology, data analysis, computational mathematics, or another proof-based area and ask whether there is a small part of an existing project you could help with.
If the faculty project is a good fit, work with the professor toward a poster or project that could potentially be developed for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

reasons: This internship can help you learn what MRI and CT data look like in practice and how mathematical or computational methods can extract useful information from images.
preparationSteps: Download a small public medical-imaging dataset and write a basic Python notebook that loads several images, displays them, and summarizes simple properties such as image dimensions and pixel values.

After you are comfortable handling the images, follow one beginner tutorial for a TDA library such as GUDHI or giotto-tda and generate a simple persistence diagram from sample data rather than trying to reproduce a research paper immediately.

reasons: This role can help you combine mathematics and programming while preparing for graduate research in topological data analysis, computational geometry, or mathematical data science.
preparationSteps: Take one geometry, linear algebra, or computational mathematics class project and extend it into a small Python project with a clear question, visual output, and short explanation of the mathematics involved.

By junior year, identify M.S. and Ph.D. programs in applied mathematics, statistics, computer science, or data science with faculty working in topology, geometry, scientific computing, or medical imaging, and note the courses and research experience they expect before admission.

title: Mathematical Epidemiologist
shortDescription: Builds mathematical and statistical models of infectious diseases to understand how outbreaks spread, how interventions change transmission, and how new pathogen variants may affect future epidemic patterns.
usual_employers: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

reasons: This internship can help you practice working with disease data, interpreting outbreak patterns, and connecting quantitative results with real public-health questions.
preparationSteps: Choose one infectious disease and use public CDC data to graph cases over time, then write a short explanation of when cases rose or fell and what factors may have contributed.

Search universities, hospitals, health departments, and research institutes for broad epidemiology, public health, or quantitative research internships rather than only positions labeled mathematical epidemiology.

reasons: This internship can help you practice turning biological questions into equations and simulations while building research experience for graduate school.
preparationSteps: Build a basic SIR or SEIR disease model in Python and change one input such as transmission rate or recovery time to see how the outbreak curve changes.

Ask a Loyola Mathematics, Statistics, Biology, or Computer Science professor about a mathematical biology, differential equations, simulation, or health-data project that could potentially grow into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

reasons: This internship can help you practice cleaning, visualizing, and analyzing the kinds of surveillance and genomic data used in modern epidemic modeling.
preparationSteps: Use a public dataset containing disease cases or variant frequencies and make a small Python or R project showing how the dominant strain or case pattern changed over time.

By junior year, compare M.S. and Ph.D. programs in applied mathematics, epidemiology, biostatistics, or mathematical biology and note their prerequisites in calculus, differential equations, probability, statistics, programming, and biology.

title: Machine Learning Mathematician
shortDescription: Develops mathematical theory explaining why machine-learning systems work, proving results about neural-network optimization, convergence, stability, geometry, and the ability of trained models to generalize beyond their training data.

reasons: This internship can help you move beyond simply training models and start asking why algorithms behave the way they do.
preparationSteps: Train a small neural network in Python and run one controlled experiment changing something simple such as learning rate, network depth, or training-set size, then graph how the change affects training and test performance.

Read one beginner-accessible machine-learning theory paper with a professor or student research group and write down the main question, assumptions, result, and mathematical tools used without trying to understand every proof immediately.

reasons: This internship can help you develop proof-writing, analysis, probability, and mathematical maturity needed for theoretical machine-learning research.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Mathematics, Statistics, or Computer Science professor about research involving optimization, probability, analysis, numerical methods, algorithms, or machine learning and ask whether there is a small part of an existing project you could contribute to.
If the project develops well, work with the professor toward a poster or research result that could potentially become a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

reasons: This role can help you build the combination of mathematics, programming, paper reading, and faculty mentorship expected for graduate study in machine-learning theory.
preparationSteps: Prioritize strong grades in linear algebra, probability, real analysis, algorithms, and machine learning and keep one or two substantial research or technical projects that show you can work through difficult quantitative problems.

By junior year, identify Ph.D. programs in mathematics, statistics, computer science, or applied mathematics with faculty working in learning theory, optimization, deep-learning theory, or statistical learning, and track their prerequisites, research expectations, recommendation letters, and application deadlines.

title: Econometrician
shortDescription: Develops and applies advanced statistical models to measure how economic forces such as interest rates, financial conditions, and policy changes affect markets, businesses, households, and economies around the world.

reasons: This internship can help you practice cleaning economic data, estimating statistical relationships, interpreting results, and supporting professional economists with research.
preparationSteps: Use FRED data to study a simple question such as how interest-rate changes relate to inflation, unemployment, housing activity, or business investment, and present the results with a few clear graphs and regressions.

Apply broadly to Federal Reserve Banks, government agencies, research institutes, and economic consulting firms for economics or research internships rather than searching only for positions titled econometrician.

reasons: This internship can help you build the programming, statistics, data-cleaning, and visualization skills needed before working with more advanced econometric models.
preparationSteps: Take one economics class question and answer it with a real public dataset in R, Python, or Stata, keeping your code, graphs, statistical output, and written interpretation together as one portfolio project.
Practice explaining the difference between correlation and causation in your project and clearly state what your analysis can and cannot conclude from the available data.

reasons: This role can help you build the faculty mentorship, econometrics, mathematical preparation, and research writing experience expected by graduate economics programs.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Economics, Mathematics, or Statistics professor whether you can help with data collection, econometric analysis, literature review, or replication work on an existing research project and aim to produce a substantial paper or research presentation.

By junior year, compare Ph.D. programs in economics, econometrics, or statistics and make a checklist of their expectations in calculus, linear algebra, probability, econometrics, programming, research experience, and faculty recommendation letters.

title: Fluid Dynamics Theoretical Lead
shortDescription: Leads mathematical and computational research on how water flows around underwater vehicles, using fluid dynamics and simulation to reduce drag, improve stability, and guide the design of efficient submarine hull geometries.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how engineers use mathematics, physics, simulation, and testing to improve the performance of real mechanical systems.
preparationSteps: Build a simple project comparing two streamlined shapes and explain which geometric features you expect to create more or less fluid resistance using concepts from physics or fluid mechanics.
Apply broadly to mechanical, aerospace, naval, and engineering-analysis internships instead of waiting for an undergraduate role specifically involving submarine hydrodynamics.

reasons: This internship can help you practice using numerical models to visualize flow, pressure, velocity, and drag around physical objects.
preparationSteps: Follow a beginner CFD tutorial in an accessible tool and simulate flow around a simple object such as a cylinder or streamlined body, then save images showing velocity and pressure around the object.

Ask a Loyola Engineering, Mathematics, or Physics professor about a project involving fluids, differential equations, numerical simulation, mechanics, or computational physics that could potentially develop into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

reasons: This role can help you build the differential-equation, numerical-analysis, programming, and research experience needed for graduate work in theoretical or computational fluid dynamics.
preparationSteps: Work with a mathematics, physics, or engineering professor on a sustained research project and aim to leave college with at least one substantial paper, poster, simulation project, or faculty-supervised research result.

By junior year, compare M.S. and Ph.D. programs in applied mathematics, mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or computational science with faculty working in fluid dynamics, and check their expectations in calculus, differential equations, numerical methods, mechanics, programming, and undergraduate research.

title: Semiconductor Device Physicist
shortDescription: Develops new semiconductor materials, thin films, and nanoscale device structures that help future computer chips become faster, smaller, and more energy efficient as traditional silicon scaling reaches physical limits.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how chip materials, fabrication steps, measurements, and device performance connect inside real semiconductor development.
preparationSteps: Choose one modern transistor technology and make a one-page visual explaining its basic layers, semiconductor material, gate, contacts, and why shrinking or changing those materials can improve performance.

Search semiconductor manufacturers, equipment companies, government labs, and university labs for broad materials, electrical engineering, physics, or semiconductor internships rather than waiting for a position titled device physicist.

reasons: This internship can help you build laboratory, characterization, experimental-design, and research skills needed before specializing in nanoscale electronic materials.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Physics or Engineering professor whether you can assist with a materials, electronics, nanotechnology, solid-state physics, or experimental project and discuss whether it could develop into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

Look at undergraduate research programs such as NSF REUs, NIST SURF, and university summer materials programs where you could gain hands-on experience with microscopy, thin films, electronic materials, or device fabrication.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how deposition, etching, cleaning, lithography, and measurement steps are combined to manufacture semiconductor devices.
preparationSteps: Learn the basic purpose of deposition methods such as ALD, CVD, PVD, and epitaxy and make a simple comparison sheet showing what each method deposits and why engineers choose one over another.

By junior year, identify M.S. and Ph.D. programs in Materials Science, Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, or Nanotechnology with semiconductor-device faculty and track their expectations in physics, materials science, laboratory research, mathematics, and recommendation letters.

title: Biomaterial Implant Scientist
shortDescription: Develops and tests implant materials and porous structures that encourage bone to grow onto or into orthopedic devices, improving the long-term stability and biological compatibility of replacements such as hip implants.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how researchers test whether metals, polymers, ceramics, and coatings are strong enough and biologically suitable for medical use.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Biology, Engineering, Chemistry, or Physics professor whether you can help with a materials, cell biology, biomechanics, or biomedical research project and discuss whether it could grow into a future Hauber Summer Research Fellowship proposal.

Choose one implant material such as titanium, stainless steel, ceramic, or polymer and make a short comparison covering strength, stiffness, corrosion resistance, biocompatibility, and why it is used inside the body.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how implant ideas move through design, testing, manufacturing, quality checks, and eventual clinical use.
preparationSteps: Pick one commercial hip implant and make a one-page breakdown of its materials, shape, porous or coated surfaces, fixation method, and what each design feature is meant to accomplish.

Apply broadly to orthopedic companies, medical-device manufacturers, engineering firms, and research hospitals for engineering or R&D internships instead of limiting your search to biomaterials scientist positions.

reasons: This internship can help you connect materials science with bone biology, biomechanics, implant testing, and the clinical problems orthopedic devices are designed to solve.
preparationSteps: Read one beginner-accessible research paper comparing porous and solid titanium implants and make a one-page summary of the research question, experiment, main result, and limitation.

By junior year, compare M.S. and Ph.D. programs in Materials Science, Biomedical Engineering, Bioengineering, or Biomaterials and identify programs where faculty specifically study implants, additive manufacturing, tissue-material interactions, or orthopedic biomechanics.

title: Aerospace Composites Director
shortDescription: Leads the development of lightweight composite materials and structures for spacecraft and advanced aerospace systems, balancing strength, mass, temperature resistance, durability, manufacturing, and mission requirements.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how engineers compare materials, perform mechanical tests, investigate failures, and select materials for demanding aerospace applications.
preparationSteps: Choose aluminum, titanium, and carbon-fiber composite and make a simple spreadsheet comparing density, strength, stiffness, temperature limits, and one aerospace use for each material.

Apply broadly to aerospace companies, government laboratories, materials manufacturers, and engineering firms for general materials or engineering internships instead of searching only for space-composites positions.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how fibers, resins, layer direction, manufacturing methods, and defects determine the performance of composite structures.
preparationSteps: Make a simple composite sample or use a classroom materials project to compare how changing fiber or layer direction changes stiffness and strength, documenting what you changed and what happened.
Learn the basic difference between carbon fiber, fiberglass, carbon-carbon, and ceramic-matrix composites and create a one-page reference showing where each is useful in aerospace.

reasons: This role can help you build the experimental research, mechanics, simulation, and faculty mentorship needed for advanced materials leadership and graduate research.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Engineering, Physics, or Chemistry professor about research involving materials, mechanics, polymers, structural testing, or thermal behavior and see whether a manageable project could develop into the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

By junior year, compare M.S. and Ph.D. programs in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, or Aerospace Engineering with faculty working on composites, lightweight structures, extreme-environment materials, or spacecraft structures and track their prerequisite and research expectations.

title: Solid-State Battery Principal
shortDescription: Leads research on solid electrolytes and battery materials that could make electric-vehicle batteries safer, more energy dense, faster charging, and capable of longer driving ranges.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how researchers compare battery materials, measure cell performance, organize experimental data, and investigate why batteries lose performance over time.
preparationSteps: Choose three battery technologies such as conventional lithium-ion, solid-state lithium-metal, and lithium iron phosphate and make a one-page comparison of energy density, safety, charging, materials, and major technical challenges using reputable sources.

Search battery companies, automotive companies, national laboratories, universities, and materials companies for broad battery, materials, chemistry, or engineering internships rather than only positions labeled solid-state battery research.

reasons: This internship can help you build laboratory, experimental-design, characterization, and research-writing experience before specializing in battery materials.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Chemistry, Physics, or Engineering professor whether you can assist with a materials, electrochemistry, energy, ceramics, or experimental research project and discuss whether it could develop into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

Keep a simple research portfolio containing your research question, methods you learned, graphs or measurements you helped produce, and a short explanation of what you found rather than only listing the lab on your resume.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how battery chemistry, materials, testing, manufacturing, and electric-vehicle requirements connect outside a university laboratory.
preparationSteps: Read one recent solid-state battery research paper and make a beginner-friendly summary of the electrolyte used, what problem the researchers were trying to solve, what they tested, and the main limitation that remains.

By junior year, compare M.S. and Ph.D. programs in Materials Science, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or Electrochemistry with battery faculty and track their prerequisites, undergraduate research expectations, recommendation letters, and application deadlines.

title: Metallurgical Failure Consultant
shortDescription: Investigates broken or damaged metal components to determine whether failures came from fatigue, corrosion, manufacturing defects, excessive loads, welding problems, or other material and mechanical causes.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how engineers measure material strength, examine damaged components, document observations, and compare test results with expected material behavior.
preparationSteps: Take a broken everyday metal item or use photographs from a published engineering case and make a short observation sheet describing where it failed, what the fracture looks like, what loads it likely experienced, and what additional tests you would want before claiming a cause.

Search materials laboratories, aerospace companies, manufacturers, testing companies, and engineering consultancies for general materials testing or engineering internships instead of limiting yourself to forensic failure-analysis titles.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how metal composition, heat treatment, manufacturing, microstructure, and loading affect whether components perform safely.
preparationSteps: Choose one metal commonly used in aircraft or pipelines and create a one-page profile covering its basic composition, strength, corrosion concerns, common applications, and two ways that component can fail.

If you have access through a supervised course or research lab, learn how basic microscopy, hardness testing, tensile testing, or metallography is used and keep examples of the resulting graphs or images for your portfolio.

reasons: This role can help you build the materials characterization, mechanics, experimental research, and technical-writing background commonly expected in advanced failure-analysis consulting.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Engineering or Physics professor about a project involving materials, mechanics, fracture, corrosion, structural testing, or experimental methods and see whether a manageable research question could develop into a future Hauber proposal.

By junior year, compare M.S. and Ph.D. programs in Materials Science, Metallurgical Engineering, or Mechanical Engineering and identify programs with faculty studying fracture, fatigue, corrosion, or failure analysis.

title: Nanotechnology Catalyst Lead
shortDescription: Leads research on nanoscale catalyst materials whose surface structure, composition, and active sites help hydrogen-producing electrochemical reactions occur faster, more efficiently, and with less expensive materials.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how researchers create, characterize, and compare small-scale materials whose surface properties strongly affect chemical reactions.
preparationSteps: Choose one nanomaterial used in energy research and create a short profile explaining what it is made from, what makes its surface useful, how researchers measure it, and what energy application it supports.

Ask a Loyola Chemistry, Physics, or Engineering professor whether you can assist with a materials, chemistry, surface-science, or energy project and discuss whether it could grow into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how electrical energy and chemical reactions interact in batteries, fuel cells, electrolyzers, and hydrogen-production systems.
preparationSteps: Read one beginner-accessible paper or review on water electrolysis and make a one-page diagram showing the anode, cathode, electrolyte, hydrogen production step, and where catalysts improve the process.

Search universities, national laboratories, chemical companies, energy companies, and materials firms for chemistry, materials, electrochemistry, or energy research internships rather than waiting for a nanocatalyst-specific opening.

reasons: This role can help you build the sustained laboratory research, data analysis, scientific writing, and faculty recommendations needed for graduate study in advanced catalyst materials.
preparationSteps: Work toward one sustained undergraduate research experience where you regularly collect or analyze experimental data and aim to finish with a poster, presentation, or faculty-supervised research report.

By junior year, compare Ph.D. programs in Materials Science, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or Applied Physics with faculty working in catalysis, electrochemistry, nanomaterials, or hydrogen and note their coursework and research expectations before applying.

title: Electronic Ceramics Researcher
shortDescription: Develops piezoelectric ceramic and crystal materials that efficiently convert electrical energy into ultrasound and back again, helping improve the sensitivity, resolution, and performance of advanced medical ultrasound transducers.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how researchers prepare materials, measure their properties, organize experimental results, and determine whether a material performs as expected.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Engineering, Physics, or Chemistry professor whether you can help with a materials, ceramics, electronics, acoustics, or experimental project and discuss whether it could eventually become a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

Choose three piezoelectric materials, such as PZT, a lead-free ceramic, and a piezoelectric single crystal, and make a simple comparison of their major properties and why each might be useful in an ultrasound device.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how advanced materials are turned into real diagnostic devices and tested for reliable medical use.
preparationSteps: Choose one medical ultrasound probe and make a one-page visual explaining the basic purpose of the piezoelectric element, backing material, matching layers, electronics, and outer housing without trying to reproduce the full engineering design.

Search medical-device companies, ultrasound manufacturers, materials suppliers, and engineering firms for broad medical-device, materials, or R&D internships rather than only positions involving piezoelectric ceramics.

reasons: This role can help you combine materials science with electricity, physics, experimentation, and device performance while preparing for graduate research.
preparationSteps: Use one class or faculty project to practice plotting an electrical or materials measurement, writing a short interpretation, and explaining what the result says about the material rather than only submitting the calculation for a grade.

By junior year, compare M.S. and Ph.D. programs in Materials Science, Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, or Ceramics with faculty researching piezoelectric, ferroelectric, acoustic, or electronic materials and track their coursework and undergraduate research expectations.

title: Smart Fabrics Material Scientist
shortDescription: Develops conductive fibers, polymers, coatings, and flexible electronic materials that allow clothing and protective equipment to sense biometric signals, movement, temperature, or environmental conditions without relying on bulky external devices.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how conductive polymers, fibers, coatings, and flexible materials are made, tested, and compared for use in wearable devices.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Engineering, Chemistry, or Physics professor whether you can assist with a polymers, electronics, sensors, materials, or conductivity project and discuss whether it could develop into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

Choose three ways to make fabric electrically conductive, such as conductive thread, a polymer coating, or printed conductive material, and make a simple comparison of flexibility, conductivity, durability, and likely wearable uses.

reasons: This internship can help you connect materials with sensors, circuits, biometric measurements, and the practical challenges of putting electronics into clothing.
preparationSteps: Build or document one simple wearable-sensor project using accessible components, such as conductive fabric or thread connected to a basic pressure, stretch, temperature, or movement measurement, and record what happens when the fabric bends or moves.
Create a one-page project summary showing the material used, what the sensor measures, how the signal is collected, what worked, and what would need to improve for the device to survive everyday use.

reasons: This role can help you understand how wearable materials and sensors are evaluated for demanding applications such as health monitoring, protective equipment, communication, and field use.
preparationSteps: Choose one realistic military wearable use, such as monitoring heart rate, body temperature, hydration risk, or movement, and make a simple diagram showing what would be measured, where the sensor could sit in the garment, and what information the wearer would receive.

By junior year, compare M.S. and Ph.D. programs in Materials Science, Electrical Engineering, Polymer Science, or Biomedical Engineering with faculty researching smart textiles, flexible electronics, sensors, or wearable materials and note their prerequisite courses and research expectations.

title: Optical Glass Research Lead
shortDescription: Leads research on specialized glass compositions and optical-fiber structures that minimize light loss, control refractive properties, and improve the transmission of laser and data signals through fiber systems.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how researchers change material compositions, measure physical properties, compare samples, and document experimental results.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Physics, Chemistry, or Engineering professor whether you can assist with a glass, optics, materials, spectroscopy, or experimental-physics project and discuss whether it could develop into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

Choose three optical-glass types such as pure silica, doped silica, and multicomponent glass and make a one-page comparison of refractive index, light transmission, common applications, and why their compositions differ.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how lasers, lenses, fibers, detectors, and optical measurements interact in real photonics systems.
preparationSteps: Build a simple diagram explaining how an optical fiber's core and cladding keep light inside the fiber, then identify absorption, scattering, and bending as three ways signal strength can be lost.

Search photonics companies, fiber manufacturers, telecommunications companies, national laboratories, and university labs for broad optics, photonics, physics, or engineering internships rather than only glass-research positions.

reasons: This role can help you combine materials science, physics, laboratory measurements, and research writing while preparing for advanced optical-materials research.
preparationSteps: Use one physics or materials class project to practice plotting experimental measurements and explaining how a material property affects an optical outcome such as transmission, reflection, or refractive behavior.

By junior year, compare M.S. and Ph.D. programs in Materials Science, Optics, Applied Physics, or Electrical Engineering with faculty studying glass, photonics, fiber optics, or optical materials and track their prerequisite courses, research expectations, and recommendation-letter requirements.

title: Corrosion Mitigator
shortDescription: Develops and tests coatings, surface treatments, and corrosion-control systems that protect offshore wind foundations and other marine metal structures from seawater, salt, oxygen, and long-term environmental degradation.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how metals and coatings are tested, how environmental exposure damages materials, and how engineers select materials for long service lives.
preparationSteps: Choose carbon steel, stainless steel, and one corrosion-resistant alloy and make a simple comparison of how each behaves in saltwater, approximate cost differences, and where each might be used offshore.

Search materials laboratories, offshore-energy companies, coating manufacturers, engineering consultancies, and testing companies for general materials or engineering internships rather than waiting for a corrosion-specific opening.

reasons: This internship can help you practice inspecting coatings, measuring corrosion, comparing protective systems, and understanding why some coatings survive harsh environments better than others.
preparationSteps: Take several small pieces of information from reputable corrosion sources and make a one-page comparison of paint or barrier coatings, galvanizing, sacrificial-anode protection, and impressed-current cathodic protection, including when each method is useful.

If you have access to a supervised chemistry or materials lab, ask whether you can help with a simple corrosion or coating experiment and document the samples, exposure conditions, measurements, photos, and results.

reasons: This role can help you build the chemistry, materials testing, experimental research, and faculty mentorship useful for advanced corrosion and protective-coatings work.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Chemistry, Physics, or Engineering professor about a project involving metals, coatings, electrochemistry, materials degradation, or environmental exposure and see whether a manageable research question could develop into a future Hauber proposal.

By junior year, compare M.S. and Ph.D. programs in Materials Science, Corrosion Science, Chemical Engineering, or Mechanical Engineering with faculty studying coatings, electrochemistry, marine materials, or corrosion and note their coursework and undergraduate research expectations.

title: Tenured University Professor
shortDescription: Conducts original research, publishes scholarly work, teaches university students, mentors future researchers, and contributes to the long-term academic work of a college or university.

reasons: This role can help you learn how academic research actually works while building the faculty relationships and research experience that graduate programs value.
preparationSteps: Ask a professor in the subject you may eventually study in graduate school whether you can help with a manageable part of their research, such as finding sources, organizing citations, reviewing archival material, transcribing information, or checking a bibliography.

Keep the strongest work you produce in one folder and aim to turn at least one class or faculty project into a polished research paper, conference presentation, poster, or other sample you can later discuss in graduate-school applications.

reasons: This experience can help you determine whether you enjoy explaining difficult ideas, answering student questions, and supporting other people's learning before committing to an academic career.
preparationSteps: Tutor students in a subject you already know well, lead a study group, or look for peer-mentor opportunities where you regularly explain course material rather than only helping once.
After several sessions, write down which explanations worked, which confused students, and how you changed your approach so you begin developing actual teaching experience.

reasons: This internship can help you practice close reading, archival research, writing, source evaluation, and other skills useful for graduate study in fields such as history, philosophy, or music.
preparationSteps: Look for internships or volunteer work with museums, archives, libraries, historical organizations, arts organizations, or university research centers where you can work with real sources and produce something you can describe on a CV.

By junior year, identify several Ph.D. programs in your intended academic field and compare faculty research areas, writing-sample expectations, language requirements if applicable, funding, recommendation letters, and application deadlines.

title: Superintendent of Schools
shortDescription: Leads an entire public school system, setting district priorities and overseeing instruction, staffing, budgets, operations, facilities, policy implementation, and long-term improvements across many schools.

reasons: This internship can help you understand what teachers and students experience every day before eventually making decisions that affect an entire school district.
preparationSteps: Tutor, mentor, coach, or assist in a K-12 classroom or youth education program consistently enough that you can observe how instruction, student support, discipline, and school routines actually work.
Talk with a teacher, counselor, or school administrator about their career path and ask what problems at the school level are hardest for district leadership to solve.

reasons: This internship can help you see the budgeting, staffing, transportation, facilities, purchasing, and administrative work required to operate a school system.
preparationSteps: Download a nearby school district's public budget and make a one-page breakdown of where its money comes from and its largest spending categories, such as instruction, salaries, transportation, facilities, and student services.

Attend or watch one public school-board meeting and take notes on one budget, staffing, curriculum, or facilities decision and the different concerns raised by administrators, board members, employees, and families.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how principals and district administrators coordinate people, programs, budgets, and student outcomes.
preparationSteps: During college, investigate the teacher or school-specialist licensure route you would use after graduation because superintendent pathways normally require substantial real PreK-12 experience before district-level administration.

Later, after gaining school experience, plan for a master's degree in educational leadership or administration and state administrator credentials; if superintendent leadership remains your goal, compare Ed.D. or superintendent-certification programs and their experience requirements.

title: Educational Neuroscientist
shortDescription: Studies how children's brains develop during learning and how differences such as dyslexia affect reading and cognition, using behavioral and neuroscience evidence to improve assessment, instruction, and learning technologies.

reasons: This internship can help you practice working with children, collecting behavioral data, running research studies, and understanding how learning changes across development.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Psychology, Education, Biology, or related faculty member whether you can assist with a child development, cognition, learning, language, or psychology research project through tasks such as literature review, participant work, data entry, or basic analysis.
If you find a suitable faculty project, discuss whether a focused research question could eventually be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

reasons: This internship can help you understand dyslexia and other learning differences through real educational assessment, literacy research, and work with children.
preparationSteps: Volunteer or work in a tutoring, literacy, special-education, or youth-learning setting so you gain direct experience supporting children with different learning needs before trying to design educational interventions.

Read two or three research papers on dyslexia and make a short comparison of what each study measured, which children participated, what the researchers found, and what the study still could not answer.

reasons: This internship can help you combine psychology, neuroscience, statistics, and education while preparing for doctoral research.
preparationSteps: Look for university labs where undergraduate assistants can help with EEG, behavioral testing, psychometric assessments, participant recruitment, or data analysis, and apply broadly to developmental neuroscience and cognitive psychology labs rather than only jobs titled educational neuroscience.

By junior year, compare Ph.D. programs in cognitive neuroscience, developmental psychology, educational neuroscience, learning sciences, or education and identify faculty studying dyslexia, literacy, child development, or learning technology; track their statistics, research-methods, programming, and prior-lab-experience expectations.

title: Curriculum Transformation Director
shortDescription: Leads large-scale curriculum and instructional improvement efforts, designing standards, learning frameworks, assessments, and teacher resources that can be implemented across school districts, states, or other major education systems.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how learning goals, lessons, assessments, and teaching materials are organized into a larger curriculum.
preparationSteps: Choose one Maryland academic standard and compare how two different lesson plans teach that same standard, noting what students are expected to learn, what activity they complete, and how their learning is checked.
Ask a teacher or education professor whether you can help organize lessons, review instructional materials, create student activities, or assist with another real curriculum-related task.

reasons: This internship can help you see how curriculum decisions are influenced by state standards, regulations, assessments, funding, and public education policy.
preparationSteps: Read one recent Maryland State Board of Education curriculum or standards decision and make a one-page summary of what changed, who the change affects, and what schools would need to do differently.

Attend or watch one school-board or state-board meeting involving curriculum, testing, literacy, mathematics, or instructional policy and write down the major arguments raised by educators, officials, and community members.

reasons: This role can help you build research, program-evaluation, and faculty mentorship experience while preparing for advanced curriculum leadership.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Education, Psychology, or Sociology professor whether you can help with research involving teaching, curriculum, student outcomes, equity, assessment, or school improvement and aim to contribute to a paper, poster, or substantial project.

After gaining classroom or education experience, compare master's and Ed.D. or Ph.D. programs in curriculum and instruction, educational leadership, or education policy and track their teaching-experience, research, recommendation, and licensure expectations.

title: Dean of Admissions
shortDescription: Leads a university's admissions operation, directing student recruitment, application review, enrollment strategy, marketing, data analysis, and coordination with financial-aid teams to build incoming classes.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how colleges communicate with prospective students, organize applications, host visits, and move students from initial interest to enrollment.
