preparationSteps: Ask Loyola Admissions whether there are student ambassador, tour guide, open-house, calling, or office-support opportunities where you can work directly with prospective students and families.
Keep track of the events, tours, or student interactions you support and note what questions prospective students ask most often so you begin understanding how students make enrollment decisions.

reasons: This internship can help you practice the outreach, messaging, event promotion, and audience analysis that universities use to recruit students.
preparationSteps: Choose three universities and compare how their admissions websites communicate academics, cost, student life, outcomes, and campus culture to prospective students.
Use a marketing class, campus club, or student organization to help promote one real event and track a simple measure such as registrations, attendance, email responses, or social engagement.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how admissions leaders use application, acceptance, enrollment, demographic, and financial data when planning an incoming class.
preparationSteps: Use publicly available university admissions data to build a simple Excel or Power BI dashboard comparing applications, admission rates, enrollment, and other available measures across several years.

By junior or senior year, learn about master's programs in higher education administration, enrollment management, education leadership, or business; graduate school is not always required immediately, but it can become valuable as you move toward senior admissions leadership.

title: Chief Instructional Designer
shortDescription: Leads the design of large-scale corporate learning experiences, combining instructional science, interactive media, simulations, and emerging technologies such as virtual reality to help employees practice complex skills safely and effectively.

reasons: This internship can help you practice turning information into clear lessons, activities, assessments, and digital learning experiences.
preparationSteps: Choose something you already know how to do and create a short five-to-ten-minute digital lesson with a learning objective, explanation, practice activity, and small knowledge check using PowerPoint, Canva, Articulate, or another accessible tool.
Ask a Loyola professor, campus office, club, or student organization whether they have a short training or orientation topic you could turn into a clearer digital learning resource for real users.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how learning-management systems, interactive media, videos, simulations, and other technologies are used to deliver training.
preparationSteps: Build one small interactive learning project with branching choices, such as a customer-service, safety, or workplace decision scenario, where each learner choice leads to different feedback.
Keep screenshots, your storyboard, the final activity, and a short explanation of why you designed it that way in a portfolio because instructional-design employers commonly want to see actual work.

reasons: This internship can help you explore how simulations, 3D environments, and VR can let employees practice tasks that are expensive, dangerous, or difficult to recreate in a classroom.
preparationSteps: Choose one training problem where VR could genuinely help, such as equipment safety or emergency response, and storyboard a simple simulation showing what the learner sees, what decisions they make, and what feedback they receive.

By junior year, compare master's programs in instructional design, learning technologies, educational technology, or human-computer interaction and identify programs with coursework in learning science, interactive media, simulation, or XR if you want to lead advanced immersive-learning teams later.

title: Education Policy Researcher
shortDescription: Uses student, school, and demographic data to evaluate education policies such as vouchers, school choice, funding, accountability, and academic interventions and translates the evidence into recommendations for policymakers.

reasons: This internship can help you practice working with student and school data, reviewing research, and evaluating whether education programs are actually improving outcomes.
preparationSteps: Use a public education dataset such as NCES or the Urban Institute Education Data Portal to compare a few school or district measures over several years and turn the results into two or three clear charts.

Ask a Loyola Education, Political Science, Sociology, Economics, or Statistics professor whether you can help with data collection, literature review, survey work, or analysis on an existing education or public-policy research project.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how research findings are turned into legislation, agency decisions, funding priorities, and recommendations for schools.
preparationSteps: Choose one current education policy such as vouchers, school funding, teacher pay, or standardized testing and write a two-page policy brief summarizing the proposal, evidence supporting it, evidence questioning it, and what additional information policymakers would need.
Attend or watch one Maryland State Board of Education, local school-board, or legislative hearing and take notes on what evidence different speakers use to support their positions.

reasons: This internship can help you build the statistics, programming, data-cleaning, and visualization skills used in large education-policy evaluations.
preparationSteps: Build one R or Python project that follows an education measure such as test scores, graduation rates, attendance, or college enrollment across several years and clearly document where the data came from and what each calculation means.

By junior year, compare MPP, education-policy master's, Ed.D., and Ph.D. programs and note which ones emphasize econometrics, causal inference, statistics, and research experience so you can choose the graduate pathway that matches how research-focused you want your career to be.

title: Speech-Language Pathologist
shortDescription: Evaluates and treats children with speech, language, literacy, social-communication, and cognitive-communication difficulties so they can communicate more effectively and participate successfully in school and everyday life.

reasons: This experience can help you see what speech-language assessment and therapy actually look like before committing to graduate clinical training.
preparationSteps: Ask Loyola faculty or local speech-language clinics, schools, hospitals, and pediatric therapy centers whether they allow undergraduate observation, volunteering, or supervised exposure to speech-language services.
Keep a simple observation log describing the age group, general communication goal, type of activity used, and what you learned about the SLP's role without recording any private patient information.

reasons: This internship can help you become comfortable working with children and understand how communication, learning, behavior, and development interact.
preparationSteps: Tutor, mentor, coach, or work consistently with children through a school, literacy program, youth organization, or disability-support program so you gain real experience communicating with different learners.
Choose one childhood communication disorder and make a one-page beginner-friendly summary of common signs, how an SLP assesses it, and examples of treatment goals using ASHA resources.

reasons: This internship can help you build research, data, and faculty experience while preparing for competitive graduate programs in speech-language pathology.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Communication Sciences and Disorders, Psychology, Education, or related faculty member whether you can help with research involving language development, speech, literacy, hearing, cognition, or child communication.

Before senior year, compare CAA-accredited master's programs in speech-language pathology and make a checklist of each program's prerequisite courses, observation or clinical expectations, recommendation letters, application deadlines, and any undergraduate courses you still need.

title: Clinical Child Psychologist
shortDescription: Evaluates and treats children and adolescents experiencing emotional, behavioral, developmental, or mental-health challenges, working with young people, families, schools, and other healthcare professionals to improve daily functioning and development.

reasons: This internship can help you practice participant work, literature review, behavioral data collection, and research methods while building experience that clinical psychology doctoral programs value.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Psychology professor whether you can help with a child development, mental health, learning, cognition, or behavioral research project through manageable tasks such as literature review, participant scheduling, data entry, or basic analysis.
If you find a strong faculty research fit, ask whether a focused part of the project could eventually be developed into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

reasons: This experience can help you become comfortable working with children and adolescents in settings where emotional, behavioral, and developmental needs are supported.
preparationSteps: Volunteer or work consistently with children through a youth program, school, mentoring organization, behavioral-health program, or disability-support organization so you gain real experience communicating with different developmental needs.

Choose one childhood condition such as ADHD, anxiety, autism, or depression and make a one-page summary of common signs, evidence-based treatment approaches, and the role a psychologist may play using APA or children's-hospital resources.

reasons: This role can help you build the sustained research, statistics, faculty mentorship, and writing experience expected by competitive clinical psychology doctoral programs.
preparationSteps: Aim to complete at least one sustained research experience before graduation and keep track of the research question, your responsibilities, methods you learned, and any poster, presentation, or paper that resulted.

By junior year, compare APA-accredited Ph.D. and Psy.D. programs in clinical psychology with strong child or adolescent training and make a checklist of their research expectations, prerequisite courses, recommendation letters, clinical opportunities, internship outcomes, and application deadlines.

title: Bilingual Program Director
shortDescription: Leads bilingual and dual-language programs across schools, coordinating curriculum, teacher training, language-development goals, student assessment, family engagement, and program improvement so students can build strong academic skills in two languages.

reasons: This internship can help you see how teachers balance academic content and language development inside bilingual or immersion classrooms.
preparationSteps: Volunteer, observe, tutor, or assist in a Spanish-English, French-English, or other multilingual classroom or youth program so you can see how students actually learn academic material in two languages.
After several sessions, write down two teaching strategies that helped students understand difficult material and one challenge teachers faced when working across both languages.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how districts coordinate language programs, student support, family outreach, curriculum, and teacher resources across multiple schools.
preparationSteps: Choose one school district with a dual-language program and make a one-page overview showing which languages are offered, which grades participate, how much instructional time occurs in each language, and how the program expands across grade levels.

Search school districts, education nonprofits, language organizations, and community programs for broad education, multilingual, language, or student-support internships instead of waiting for a director-level bilingual program opening.

reasons: This experience can help you build real teaching and language-use experience before pursuing leadership positions that supervise bilingual teachers and curriculum.
preparationSteps: Use your strongest second language regularly through tutoring, conversation groups, language clubs, community programs, or classroom assistance and work toward advanced speaking, reading, and writing ability rather than relying only on course completion.

Plan first for classroom teaching or another school-based role after college, then compare master's programs in bilingual education, curriculum and instruction, or educational leadership and the teaching or administrator credentials required in the state where you want to work.

title: Investigative Journalist
shortDescription: Conducts deep reporting into corruption, political influence, abuse of power, and other hidden systems by combining interviews, public records, financial documents, data, and careful fact-checking into evidence-based stories.

reasons: This internship can help you practice interviewing people, verifying information, meeting deadlines, and turning research into publishable journalism.
preparationSteps: Report and publish two or three stories through a campus publication, local outlet, class project, or independent portfolio where you interview real people and verify information instead of writing only opinion pieces.

Attend one Loyola, Baltimore, or Maryland public meeting such as a school-board, city-council, planning, or government hearing and write a short news story explaining what happened and why it matters.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how reporters move beyond daily news by using documents, databases, interviews, and timelines to investigate one issue over a longer period.
preparationSteps: Choose one manageable local question, such as how a public program spends money or whether a promised project was completed, and collect public documents, meeting records, budgets, and interviews before writing your conclusion.
Learn how to submit a basic Maryland Public Information Act or federal FOIA request and practice by requesting a narrow, clearly defined set of nonprivate public records.

reasons: This internship can help you use spreadsheets, public datasets, and visualization to find patterns that can become stronger investigative stories.
preparationSteps: Download one public Baltimore, Maryland, or federal dataset and use Excel, Python, or another familiar tool to find one interesting pattern, then create a chart and explain what additional reporting would be needed before publishing a claim.

Build a small journalism portfolio that includes at least one reported article, one document-based investigation, and one data-based story so internship editors can see several kinds of reporting ability.

title: Editor-in-Chief
shortDescription: Sets the editorial direction of a major publication, deciding coverage priorities and standards while leading editors, reporters, publishing workflows, investigations, and the overall voice of the newsroom.

reasons: This internship can help you practice editing drafts, checking facts, writing headlines, organizing publishing schedules, and improving other writers' work.
preparationSteps: Join a Loyola student publication or another campus media organization and volunteer for editing responsibilities where you regularly review another writer's draft before publication.
Take three pieces of your own or a classmate's writing and create before-and-after editing samples showing what you changed for clarity, structure, accuracy, grammar, or unnecessary wording.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how reporters, editors, photographers, designers, and audience teams coordinate to publish reliable journalism on deadline.
preparationSteps: Take responsibility for one small recurring section, newsletter, beat, or content series in a campus organization and practice planning what gets published over several weeks rather than producing only one article.
After each issue or publishing cycle, note what was late, what required major editing, what readers responded to, and one change you would make to improve the next cycle.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how writing, editing, production, audience development, and publication planning fit together behind a finished media product.
preparationSteps: Create a small publication project with classmates or independently, such as a newsletter or digital magazine containing several pieces, and set simple standards for tone, sourcing, editing, deadlines, and formatting.

If senior editorial leadership remains your goal, focus first on building years of reporting and editing experience; consider a journalism, history, political science, or media master's degree later only if it provides specialized reporting skills, strong industry access, or deeper subject expertise.

title: Lead Medical Writer
shortDescription: Leads the preparation of clear and accurate clinical and regulatory documents that explain drug-study methods, efficacy results, safety findings, and supporting scientific evidence to health authorities.

reasons: This internship can help you practice turning technical biological or clinical information into accurate writing that scientists, healthcare professionals, or regulators can understand.
preparationSteps: Choose one published clinical trial and write a one-page summary explaining the research question, patient group, treatment, primary outcome, major safety findings, and limitations without copying the paper's abstract.

Create two versions of the same trial summary: one written for a scientific audience and one written for a general audience so your portfolio demonstrates that you can adjust technical depth without changing the facts.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how clinical data are generated before medical writers are responsible for explaining those data in regulatory documents.
preparationSteps: Search hospitals, universities, pharmaceutical companies, biotechnology companies, and research organizations for broad clinical research or research-assistant opportunities where you can work with study documentation or data.

Read one clinical-trial protocol or ClinicalTrials.gov study record and make a short reference sheet identifying the study population, intervention, control group, endpoints, timeline, and safety measures.

reasons: This internship can help you combine scientific understanding with writing, editing, literature review, and communication before specializing in pharmaceutical regulatory writing.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Biology, Chemistry, Psychology, or health-related professor whether you can help turn research from their lab or field into a poster, literature summary, research abstract, or other scientific communication that gives you a real writing sample.

By junior or senior year, compare master's or Ph.D. programs in biomedical science, pharmacology, public health, or another relevant life-science field if you want stronger scientific credentials for senior regulatory writing, while also looking for programs or professional training specifically in medical and regulatory writing.

title: White House Speechwriter
shortDescription: Researches and writes major speeches that translate a president's policies, priorities, and personal voice into clear and persuasive addresses for national and international audiences.

reasons: This internship can help you practice writing messages quickly, researching policy, preparing public remarks, and communicating complicated issues clearly.
preparationSteps: Choose one real policy proposal and write a three-minute speech explaining it to a general audience, then revise the speech after asking a professor or classmate which parts were unclear or unconvincing.

Use a student government campaign, campus organization, nonprofit, or local political organization to practice writing real event remarks, talking points, emails, or short public statements for someone other than yourself.

reasons: This internship can help you understand policy well enough to explain it accurately rather than treating speechwriting as purely creative writing.
preparationSteps: Attend or watch one congressional hearing, state legislative hearing, or major policy speech and write a one-page brief covering the issue, major arguments, and three facts a speechwriter would need to verify before using them.
Apply broadly to congressional offices, state government, public-affairs organizations, campaigns, and policy nonprofits for communications, legislative, research, or government internships.

reasons: This experience can help you practice researching facts, matching another person's speaking style, and producing polished drafts under deadlines.
preparationSteps: Build a small portfolio containing three different speeches, such as a policy address, ceremonial speech, and crisis-response statement, and include a short note explaining the intended audience and tone for each.

Study several speeches by the same political leader and mark repeated vocabulary, sentence length, humor, storytelling, and argument style, then rewrite one short paragraph in that speaker's general voice without copying their wording.

title: Principal Technical Writer
shortDescription: Leads documentation for complex software and cloud platforms, turning architecture, APIs, infrastructure, deployment procedures, and engineering concepts into accurate guides that developers and technical teams can actually use.

reasons: This internship can help you practice learning unfamiliar technology, interviewing engineers, and turning technical details into clear instructions and explanations.
preparationSteps: Take one Python, JavaScript, or other coding project you already understand and write a clean README explaining what it does, how to install it, how to run it, what inputs it expects, and common errors a new user might encounter.
Ask a classmate to follow your instructions without your help and revise every section where they become confused or need to ask you a question.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how developer guides, API references, setup instructions, examples, and troubleshooting documentation support real software products.
preparationSteps: Create one small GitHub documentation project containing an installation guide, quick-start tutorial, example commands, and troubleshooting section for a simple application or open-source tool.
Learn basic Git and command-line navigation well enough to clone a repository, create a branch, edit documentation files, and commit your changes.

reasons: This internship can help you build enough hands-on technical knowledge to write accurately about infrastructure instead of relying entirely on engineers to explain every concept.
preparationSteps: Deploy one small application using an accessible cloud platform and make a simple architecture diagram showing the user, application, database or storage, and any major service involved.

Keep technical writing and software projects together in a portfolio; graduate school is optional for this field, so prioritize strong documentation samples, technical coursework, internships, and progressively more complex writing responsibilities.

title: Literary Agent / Editor
shortDescription: Discovers promising books and authors, helps strengthen manuscripts, evaluates their commercial potential, and works with publishers and rights partners to bring books to readers in domestic and international markets.

reasons: This internship can help you practice reading submissions, editing manuscripts, preparing book materials, and understanding how a manuscript moves from acquisition to publication.
preparationSteps: Join a campus literary magazine, journal, or publication and volunteer to read submissions or edit other people's work so you gain experience making editorial decisions rather than only writing your own material.

With permission from the writer, edit one short story, essay, or chapter and write a one-page editorial letter explaining what works, what needs improvement, and two or three specific revision suggestions.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how agents evaluate submissions, identify marketable projects, research publishers, and support authors before and after a book deal.
preparationSteps: Read three recently published books in one genre you might want to work with and write a short reader report for each covering the audience, strengths, weaknesses, comparable titles, and why you think a publisher might or might not acquire it.
Practice writing a short pitch for one book you enjoyed that explains the premise, target reader, and what makes it different without simply summarizing the entire plot.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how one book can generate separate publishing opportunities through translation, audio, film, television, and other rights.
preparationSteps: Choose one internationally successful book and make a simple rights map showing its original publisher, translated editions you can find, audiobook, and any film or television adaptation rights that were publicly announced.

Apply broadly to publishers, literary agencies, university presses, book nonprofits, and rights departments; graduate school is usually not necessary, so prioritize internships, editorial experience, strong reading habits, and a clear understanding of the publishing market.

title: Global Communications Director
shortDescription: Leads communication strategy across countries and regions, coordinating media relations, executive messaging, campaigns, crisis responses, and brand standards while adapting messages for different international audiences.

reasons: This internship can help you practice writing announcements, preparing content, supporting media outreach, and keeping an organization's messaging consistent across different channels.
preparationSteps: Use a Loyola club, campus office, nonprofit, or community organization to help write real newsletters, event announcements, social posts, or press materials and save two or three strong examples for a portfolio.

Choose one organization with an international audience and compare how its website or social media communicates the same major initiative in two different countries, noting what wording, examples, or priorities change.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how organizations communicate across cultures, languages, political environments, and regional media markets.
preparationSteps: Choose one global issue or company announcement and write two short versions for audiences in different countries, changing examples and context while keeping the core facts consistent.

Search international nonprofits, multinational companies, universities, development organizations, and public-affairs firms for broad communications or public-relations internships rather than only positions labeled global communications.

reasons: This internship can help you practice communicating about complicated public issues while learning how media coverage, policy, reputation, and organizational priorities interact.
preparationSteps: Pick one multinational organization facing a recent public controversy and make a one-page communications review showing what happened, who the main audiences were, what the organization said, and one thing you would have communicated differently.

Build experience with a second language, study abroad, international student organizations, or globally focused coursework when possible so you gain direct experience communicating with people whose cultural assumptions differ from your own.

title: Foreign Bureau Chief
shortDescription: Leads a news organization's reporting from a foreign country or region, managing correspondents and editors while directing coverage of politics, conflict, economics, diplomacy, and other major international events.

reasons: This internship can help you build the interviewing, sourcing, deadline writing, fact-checking, and story judgment required before taking on international reporting assignments.
preparationSteps: Report several real stories for a Loyola or local publication and make sure at least one requires multiple interviews, document research, and independent fact-checking rather than relying mainly on press releases.
Choose one international event each week for a month and write a short news brief using several reputable sources, separating confirmed facts from claims that remain uncertain.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how international newsrooms follow fast-moving political events, verify information from abroad, and explain unfamiliar regional context to wider audiences.
preparationSteps: Choose one country or region you want to understand deeply and follow its politics, economy, major institutions, and news outlets for an entire semester, keeping a simple running notebook of major people, organizations, and events.

Apply broadly to international news organizations, foreign-affairs publications, public radio, wire services, and globally focused media organizations instead of waiting for an internship specifically labeled foreign correspondent.

reasons: This internship can help you combine journalism with stronger knowledge of diplomacy, conflict, international institutions, and regional politics.
preparationSteps: Build a portfolio containing at least one internationally focused reported story, one breaking-news style article, and one deeper explanatory piece that shows you can add context instead of only summarizing events.

Continue developing a useful second language and seek study-abroad, international reporting, or overseas internship opportunities when feasible; graduate school in journalism or international affairs can help later, but strong reporting experience, regional expertise, and language ability are usually more important than the degree alone.

title: Biographer / Historical Consultant
shortDescription: Researches people, institutions, and historical events through archives, interviews, and primary sources, then turns that evidence into authoritative biographies, historical reports, books, and other narratives for public audiences.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how historians find, organize, describe, verify, and interpret original documents and artifacts.
preparationSteps: Choose one historical leader you are interested in and create a source folder containing at least five primary sources and several reliable secondary sources, with a short note explaining what each source contributes.
Apply broadly to museums, archives, libraries, historical societies, presidential libraries, and cultural organizations for history, collections, archives, or research internships.

reasons: This role can help you build deeper primary-source research, citation, writing, and faculty mentorship experience before pursuing professional historical work.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola History professor whether you can help with source collection, archival research, transcription, bibliography work, or another manageable part of an existing research project.

Turn one strong history paper into a polished writing sample of roughly 10 to 20 pages with careful citations and primary-source evidence that you could later use when applying for internships or graduate programs.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how researched nonfiction moves from manuscript development through editing, fact-checking, production, and publication.
preparationSteps: Write a short biographical profile of one historical figure using both primary and secondary sources, then make a separate fact-check sheet showing the source supporting each major factual claim.

By junior year, compare M.A. programs in History or Public History and Ph.D. programs if you want a research-intensive scholarly career, focusing on faculty specialties, archival opportunities, funding, writing-sample requirements, and placement outcomes.

title: IP Entertainment Attorney
shortDescription: Advises authors, publishers, filmmakers, producers, performers, and media companies on copyrights, trademarks, licensing, contracts, and disputes involving creative works and entertainment brands.

reasons: This internship can help you practice legal research, writing, document review, and understanding how attorneys turn facts and laws into advice for clients.
preparationSteps: Meet with Loyola's pre-law advisor by junior year and map out your LSAT preparation, law-school application timeline, recommendation letters, and courses that strengthen analytical reading and writing.

Choose one well-known copyright case involving a book, film, song, or other creative work and write a one-page case brief explaining what each side argued, what legal question the court considered, and the result.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how scripts, books, brands, licenses, talent agreements, and other creative assets move through the entertainment business before you advise clients about them as an attorney.
preparationSteps: Choose one book, film, or television adaptation and make a simple rights map showing the original creator, publisher or producer, adaptation, and any publicly reported licensing or distribution relationships.

Apply to publishers, production companies, theaters, media companies, literary agencies, and entertainment organizations for general business, legal, production, or rights internships so you learn how the industry works from inside.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how copyrights, trademarks, registrations, licenses, and ownership records are used to protect creative work.
preparationSteps: Use U.S. Copyright Office resources to learn what copyright protects for books, scripts, films, and other creative works, then make a one-page reference sheet distinguishing copyright from trademark and explaining what copyright does not protect.

Create a rights-clearance checklist for a hypothetical short film or play covering the script, music, photographs, artwork, logos, and other third-party material you would want permission to use before release.

title: United States Diplomat
shortDescription: Represents the United States abroad, working with foreign governments and communities to advance American political, economic, security, humanitarian, and diplomatic interests.
usual_employers: Foreign Service Economic and Public Diplomacy Sections

reasons: This internship can help you understand how governments research international issues, prepare briefings, communicate policy positions, and support diplomatic relationships.
preparationSteps: Choose one country you care about and keep a one-semester briefing notebook covering its political system, current leaders, economy, relationship with the United States, major security issues, and two or three reliable local news sources.

Apply broadly to the State Department, congressional offices, foreign-policy nonprofits, international organizations, and globally focused government programs rather than waiting for an internship specifically labeled diplomat.

reasons: This internship can help you build cross-cultural communication, program coordination, writing, and research experience in an international setting.
preparationSteps: Use study abroad, a language club, international student programming, or another campus opportunity to regularly work with people from different countries instead of relying only on classroom knowledge of international affairs.

Continue developing French, Spanish, or another useful language beyond basic coursework by practicing conversation, reading international news in that language, and aiming for advanced functional proficiency.

reasons: This pathway can help you prepare specifically for the competitive Foreign Service selection process while deciding whether graduate study would strengthen your international-affairs background.
preparationSteps: Read the State Department's five Foreign Service Officer career tracks and choose the one or two that currently fit you best, then use the official FSOT practice materials to learn the format instead of studying blindly.

During junior or senior year, review the Rangel and Pickering fellowship requirements and compare master's programs in international affairs or public policy; graduate school is optional for the Foreign Service, so pursue it only if it adds useful expertise, funding, or a fellowship pathway.

title: Chief Policy Analyst
shortDescription: Leads quantitative and policy analysis of proposed laws, estimating how changes such as environmental taxes could affect federal revenue, businesses, households, economic activity, and environmental outcomes before lawmakers act.

reasons: This internship can help you practice researching proposed policies, using evidence from multiple sources, and writing concise analysis for decision-makers.
preparationSteps: Choose one proposed environmental tax, credit, or regulation and write a two-page policy brief explaining who would pay or benefit, the intended environmental goal, likely economic effects, and which claims remain uncertain.
Attend or watch one congressional, Maryland legislative, or public-agency hearing related to taxes, energy, or environmental policy and compare the evidence used by different witnesses.

reasons: This internship can help you build the statistics, economics, Excel or programming, and data interpretation skills used to estimate how legislation affects the economy.
preparationSteps: Use public CBO, EPA, BEA, or Census data to build a simple spreadsheet or Python analysis showing how one environmental industry measure, tax variable, or economic outcome has changed over time.
Write a short interpretation beneath each chart explaining what the data show and what they do not prove so your project demonstrates both quantitative ability and policy judgment.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how research, committee work, legislative drafting, constituent concerns, and fiscal analysis fit into the policymaking process.
preparationSteps: Apply broadly to congressional offices, committees, CBO-style research organizations, think tanks, and state legislative offices for policy, legislative, economics, or research internships.

By junior year, compare MPP, MPA, economics master's, and Ph.D. programs and identify which route fits your goal: an MPP or MPA for applied policy leadership, or a quantitatively rigorous economics Ph.D. for advanced economic modeling and research positions such as those at JCT.

title: Urban Planning Director
shortDescription: Leads long-range planning for cities and metropolitan areas, guiding zoning, land use, housing growth, neighborhood development, and coordination of major transportation and infrastructure investments.
usual_employers: New York City Department of City Planning

reasons: This internship can help you practice reviewing development proposals, researching zoning, mapping neighborhoods, and understanding how city plans turn into real land-use decisions.
preparationSteps: Choose one Baltimore neighborhood and use public maps or GIS tools to mark its zoning, housing, commercial areas, parks, major roads, and transit stops, then identify one planning issue you notice.

Attend or watch one Baltimore Planning Commission, zoning, or development hearing and write a one-page summary of the proposal, who supported or opposed it, and what planning rules shaped the decision.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how transit routes, population patterns, land use, walking and biking networks, and capital investment decisions interact.
preparationSteps: Choose one Baltimore-area transit corridor and make a simple map showing major stops, nearby housing, jobs, schools, and undeveloped or underused land, then identify one place where better land-use and transit coordination might help.

Search city agencies, MDOT MTA, metropolitan planning organizations, engineering firms, and planning consultancies for broad transportation, GIS, or planning internships rather than only director-track positions.

reasons: This internship can help you see how zoning and long-range plans affect housing, businesses, neighborhoods, public investment, and residents in practice.
preparationSteps: Volunteer or intern with a local community-development organization, housing group, planning office, or neighborhood nonprofit and help with a real task such as mapping, survey work, meeting notes, property research, or community outreach.

By junior year, compare PAB-accredited graduate programs such as master's degrees in urban, city, regional, or community planning and check their GIS, statistics, planning-studio, internship, and application requirements; a professional planning master's is a strong preparation route for eventual director-level leadership.

title: Political Pollster / Methodologist
shortDescription: Designs and improves political surveys, sampling plans, weighting systems, and likely-voter models that help campaigns, researchers, and news organizations estimate public opinion and understand how different groups may vote.
usual_employers: NORC at the University of Chicago
Political Polling and Survey Research Firms

reasons: This internship can help you practice writing survey questions, organizing responses, analyzing samples, and understanding why survey results may not perfectly represent the wider population.
preparationSteps: Create a short anonymous survey about a campus issue, collect responses from a manageable group, and compare the demographics of your respondents with the larger student population before interpreting the results.
Use Excel, R, or Python to make a simple version of the results where underrepresented groups receive slightly more weight, then explain how the adjusted results differ from the unweighted results.

reasons: This internship can help you connect elections and political behavior with statistics, voter data, polling, and quantitative communication.
preparationSteps: Download public election results for several Maryland counties or precincts and create a few charts showing turnout and vote-share differences across places or election years.

Choose one public poll and read its methodology section, then make a one-page note explaining who was surveyed, how respondents were contacted, how the poll was weighted, its sample size, and its margin of error.

reasons: This role can help you build the statistics, research design, programming, and faculty mentorship useful for advanced polling and survey-methodology careers.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Sociology, Political Science, Statistics, Psychology, or Marketing professor whether you can help with survey design, data cleaning, questionnaire testing, sampling, or quantitative analysis on an existing research project.

By junior year, compare master's and Ph.D. programs in survey methodology, statistics, political science, sociology, or quantitative social science and note their expectations in statistics, research methods, programming, and undergraduate research.

title: Lobbyist / Government Relations Lead
shortDescription: Represents technology companies or industry groups before government, explaining how proposed laws and regulations affect the sector and building support for policy positions through research, meetings, testimony, coalitions, and legislative advocacy.
usual_employers: Government Affairs and Public Policy Firms

reasons: This internship can help you learn how organizations track legislation, prepare policy materials, meet with government officials, and advocate for specific policy positions.
preparationSteps: Choose one technology bill involving AI, privacy, cybersecurity, social media, or another issue and make a one-page tracker showing what the bill would change, who supports it, who opposes it, and where it currently sits in the legislative process.

Apply to trade associations, companies, nonprofits, public-affairs firms, and professional associations for broad government affairs, policy, or public-affairs internships instead of only searching for lobbying internships.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how lawmakers and staff actually research bills, communicate with stakeholders, prepare hearings, and move legislation through government.
preparationSteps: Apply to congressional, Maryland General Assembly, county, or city legislative offices and look for opportunities involving policy research, constituent correspondence, committee work, or legislative tracking.

Attend or watch one technology-related legislative hearing and write down the arguments made by lawmakers, industry representatives, advocates, and technical experts, including which evidence each side uses.

reasons: This internship can help you build enough technical understanding to discuss technology policy accurately while developing research and advocacy skills.
preparationSteps: Pick one technology issue such as AI regulation, data privacy, semiconductor policy, cybersecurity, or app-store rules and write a two-page brief explaining the technology first and the policy disagreement second.

If you want senior government-relations leadership later, consider an MPP, MPA, J.D., MBA, or technology-policy graduate program after gaining some practical experience; graduate school can help, but strong legislative, government, or industry experience is usually just as important.

title: Demographic Researcher
shortDescription: Analyzes population, migration, age, housing, employment, and household trends over time to help governments and planning organizations understand how communities are changing and prepare housing, zoning, infrastructure, and public services accordingly.
usual_employers: King County Department of Local Services

reasons: This internship can help you practice using Census and population data to understand how communities change across time and place.
preparationSteps: Choose two Baltimore-area neighborhoods or census tracts and use Census or American Community Survey data to compare population, age, household size, income, housing, and another measure across available years.
Turn the comparison into a short report with three or four charts and explain which changes seem most important for housing, schools, transportation, or other local services.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how population and housing data are used alongside maps and zoning information in real planning decisions.
preparationSteps: Use a simple GIS project to map population growth, housing density, age, or another demographic measure across several neighborhoods and compare the pattern with transit stops or zoning areas.
Apply broadly to city and county planning departments, metropolitan planning organizations, housing agencies, and community-development organizations for planning, GIS, research, or data internships.

reasons: This role can help you build the statistical modeling, research, GIS, and faculty mentorship useful for advanced demographic forecasting and policy research.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Sociology, Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, or Political Science professor whether you can assist with research involving population change, migration, housing, inequality, neighborhoods, or public policy and aim to contribute to a substantial empirical project.

By junior year, compare master's and Ph.D. programs in demography, sociology, statistics, urban planning, or public policy and identify programs with strong population methods, GIS, forecasting, or quantitative social-science training.

title: Political Pollster / Methodologist
shortDescription: Designs political surveys, develops weighting and voter models, and analyzes sample data to estimate public opinion and voting behavior.

reasons: This internship can help you practice survey design, questionnaire testing, data cleaning, weighting, and communicating polling results.
preparationSteps: Find a publicly available political survey dataset and reproduce several published percentages in Excel, R, or Python, then compare the unweighted and weighted results.
Create a short five-to-ten-question campus opinion survey, document how you selected respondents, and write a one-page explanation of the survey's limitations and possible sources of bias.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how voter data, polling, turnout information, and political trends are analyzed during real campaigns.
preparationSteps: Use public election results and Census demographic data to compare turnout or vote-share patterns across several counties and present the findings in a simple dashboard or written brief.
Apply to campaign, political consulting, and advocacy organizations for roles involving polling, voter data, research, or analytics rather than searching only for jobs titled 'pollster.'

reasons: This pathway can build the deeper research and statistical background often useful for advanced survey-methodologist positions.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola statistics, sociology, political science, or communication professor whether you can assist with a project involving surveys, sampling, public opinion, or quantitative social research.

If you want to specialize in methodology, compare graduate programs in survey methodology, statistics, political science, or data science and make a checklist of their statistics, research, programming, and recommendation requirements.

title: Lobbyist / Government Relations Lead
shortDescription: Represents an organization before lawmakers and regulators, analyzes policy proposals, builds coalitions, and advocates for legislative or regulatory outcomes affecting its industry.
usual_employers: Government Affairs Firms and Trade Associations

reasons: This internship can help you learn how organizations monitor legislation, prepare policy materials, and communicate with government officials.
preparationSteps: Choose one active Maryland or federal bill related to technology, privacy, cybersecurity, or artificial intelligence and create a one-page brief explaining what the bill would change, who supports it, and who could be affected.
Apply broadly to government affairs teams at companies, associations, nonprofits, and advocacy organizations rather than limiting your search to internships specifically labeled 'lobbying.'

reasons: This internship can provide firsthand exposure to how legislation is researched, negotiated, amended, and communicated to constituents and outside organizations.
preparationSteps: Attend or watch a Maryland General Assembly or congressional committee hearing and write a short summary of the competing arguments, stakeholders, and proposed policy changes.
Practice legislative research by following one bill from introduction through committee activity and recording its sponsors, amendments, hearings, votes, and current status.

reasons: This internship can help you combine technical knowledge with policy analysis in areas such as AI, cybersecurity, privacy, digital platforms, and emerging technology regulation.
preparationSteps: Pick one technology-policy issue such as AI regulation, data privacy, or cybersecurity requirements and write a two-page memo explaining the technical issue, current policy debate, and arguments from at least two stakeholder groups.

Build enough technical literacy to explain a technology issue accurately to a nontechnical audience while developing experience through policy organizations, government offices, trade associations, or corporate public-policy teams.

title: Demographic Researcher
shortDescription: Analyzes population data and develops demographic estimates or projections that help governments and organizations plan for changes in housing, services, infrastructure, and communities.

reasons: This internship can help you analyze population trends, migration, age structure, household change, and other demographic patterns using real datasets.
preparationSteps: Download Census population data for several Maryland counties and compare changes in population size, age structure, and migration over time using Excel, Python, or another statistical tool.
Turn the analysis into a short research brief with two or three charts explaining what the demographic changes could mean for schools, housing, transportation, or public services.

reasons: This internship can show you how demographic and geographic data are used by local governments when evaluating development, infrastructure, land use, and long-range plans.
preparationSteps: Use Census data and a basic GIS tool to map population growth, age distribution, or household change across several neighborhoods or census tracts.
Attend a local planning commission or zoning hearing and identify where population, housing, transportation, or neighborhood data are used to support competing planning arguments.

reasons: This pathway can build the research experience and quantitative preparation useful for advanced demography and population-science careers.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola sociology, economics, mathematics, statistics, or public-policy professor about assisting with research involving migration, population change, inequality, neighborhoods, or longitudinal social data.

By junior year, compare master's and Ph.D. programs in demography, sociology, population studies, statistics, or related fields and make a checklist of quantitative coursework, research experience, writing samples, recommendations, and application deadlines.

title: Campaign Strategist
shortDescription: Develops political campaign strategy by coordinating voter targeting, messaging, media, research, and mobilization efforts to persuade supporters and achieve electoral goals.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how campaigns recruit volunteers, contact voters, track outreach goals, and organize communities around an election.
preparationSteps: Volunteer for a local, state, or congressional campaign and complete several shifts involving canvassing, phone banking, voter registration, or volunteer recruitment.

Track your campaign's voter-contact activities for several weeks and create a simple spreadsheet showing contacts attempted, conversations completed, volunteer participation, and other available campaign metrics.

reasons: This internship can help you practice political messaging, social media, press research, advertising, and rapid-response communication.
preparationSteps: Choose a recent political issue and create a small communications portfolio containing a press release, social media post, short video script, and one sample digital advertisement aimed at the same audience.

Compare how two campaigns communicate about the same issue across speeches, advertisements, email, and social media, then write a one-page analysis of how their audiences and messaging strategies differ.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how voter data, polling, turnout information, and campaign metrics influence targeting and resource decisions.
preparationSteps: Download public election results for several Maryland counties or precincts and use Excel, Power BI, or Python to compare turnout and vote-share patterns across elections.
Create a one-page campaign targeting brief identifying several areas where turnout increased or decreased and explain what additional voter information you would want before recommending outreach.

title: Non-Profit Executive Director
shortDescription: Leads a nonprofit organization by overseeing strategy, finances, fundraising, staff, community programs, partnerships, and the responsible use of grants and donor funding.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how nonprofit organizations design, operate, and evaluate programs serving communities.
preparationSteps: Volunteer or intern with a local nonprofit and ask to assist with one specific program involving participant registration, event coordination, outreach, data tracking, or service delivery.
Create a one-page program summary showing the nonprofit's goal, target population, major activities, estimated resources, and two or three measures that could be used to evaluate its results.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how nonprofits find funding, communicate with donors, prepare grant materials, and track restricted funds.
preparationSteps: Choose a local nonprofit and identify three foundations or grant programs that appear relevant to its mission, then record each funder's priorities, eligibility rules, award size, and deadline.
Practice grant writing by creating a short mock funding request describing a community problem, proposed program, basic budget, expected outcome, and method for measuring success.

reasons: This pathway can build the financial, operational, and leadership experience normally accumulated before moving into Executive Director positions.
preparationSteps: Ask a nonprofit staff member if you can observe or assist with a small budgeting, volunteer-management, program-planning, or performance-tracking task so you can see how administrative work supports the organization's mission.

Before graduation, compare early-career nonprofit roles such as program coordinator, development associate, grants assistant, operations coordinator, and community engagement coordinator, since Executive Director is normally reached after progressive management experience rather than directly from college.

title: Corporate Litigator
shortDescription: Represents companies in complex commercial disputes, class actions, securities cases, and other high-stakes litigation through investigation, motions, trial, and appeal.

reasons: This internship can help you observe how attorneys research business disputes, organize evidence, prepare filings, and manage litigation matters.
preparationSteps: Read a publicly available commercial lawsuit complaint and one response or court opinion, then write a one-page summary identifying the parties, disputed issue, requested remedy, and major arguments.
Apply to law firms for undergraduate legal assistant, litigation support, paralegal intern, or general legal internship positions rather than searching only for attorney-level litigation roles.

reasons: This internship can show you how litigation risk connects with contracts, financial decisions, regulation, and corporate operations.
preparationSteps: Choose a public company involved in a recent lawsuit and use its annual report to identify the litigation disclosure, financial risks, and business areas affected by the dispute.
Create a short memo explaining the lawsuit in plain language and how a major judgment or settlement could affect the company's finances or operations.

reasons: Corporate litigators must complete law school and obtain the required bar admission before practicing as attorneys.
preparationSteps: Meet with Loyola pre-law advising to map your J.D. timeline, LSAT preparation, recommendation letters, application deadlines, and opportunities to strengthen your legal research and writing experience.

Before applying to law school, build at least one substantial legal writing sample by researching a business-law dispute and writing a structured argument supported by cases, statutes, or other legal authorities.

title: Constitutional Law Scholar
shortDescription: Researches and teaches constitutional law while publishing legal scholarship that contributes to debates about constitutional interpretation, rights, government power, and judicial decisions.

reasons: This pathway can help you learn how scholars develop research questions, locate legal authorities, evaluate arguments, and produce academic writing.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola political science, history, philosophy, or law-related professor whether you can assist with research involving courts, constitutional history, civil liberties, judicial politics, or legal institutions.
Choose one Supreme Court case and trace several earlier cases cited in the majority and dissent, then write a short paper explaining how each side interprets constitutional precedent differently.

reasons: This internship can expose you to real disputes involving civil liberties, constitutional rights, appellate litigation, and public-interest law.
preparationSteps: Follow one active constitutional case through its complaint, major briefs, and court decisions and maintain a short case timeline explaining the constitutional question at each stage.
Apply to civil liberties organizations, legal advocacy groups, government legal offices, and policy institutes for undergraduate research or legal-support positions.

reasons: Constitutional law scholarship is normally pursued after a J.D. and often additional research, clerkship, fellowship, practice, or graduate experience.
preparationSteps: Meet with Loyola pre-law advising to plan your J.D. applications, LSAT preparation, recommendation letters, writing experience, and undergraduate courses in constitutional law, history, politics, and philosophy.

Research several constitutional-law professors whose work interests you and compare their paths after law school, including judicial clerkships, legal practice, academic fellowships, graduate degrees, and early publications.

title: Criminal Defense Attorney
shortDescription: Represents people accused of crimes by investigating evidence, challenging the government's case, negotiating resolutions, filing motions, and advocating for clients at trial and sentencing.
usual_employers: Maryland Office of the Public Defender

reasons: This internship can expose you to client representation, criminal court proceedings, case preparation, investigations, and the realities of indigent defense.
preparationSteps: Observe several publicly accessible criminal court proceedings and keep notes on arraignments, motions, plea discussions, witness testimony, and the different responsibilities of prosecutors and defense attorneys.
Apply to state and federal public defender offices for undergraduate internships, investigative internships, legal-support positions, or other student opportunities available before law school.

reasons: This internship can help you see how private attorneys investigate allegations, review evidence, communicate with clients, research legal issues, and prepare cases.
preparationSteps: Take a publicly available criminal appellate opinion and write a one-page case brief identifying the facts, legal question, ruling, and reasoning used by the court.

Search local criminal-defense and white-collar firms for undergraduate legal assistant, administrative, investigative, research, or internship opportunities rather than limiting yourself to positions titled 'criminal defense intern.'

reasons: Practicing criminal defense requires completing a J.D. and obtaining the appropriate bar admission, with serious trial work normally developing through later supervised experience.
preparationSteps: Meet with Loyola pre-law advising to plan LSAT preparation, J.D. applications, recommendation letters, and undergraduate experiences involving legal research, writing, criminal justice, psychology, or forensic evidence.

Before law school, build a legal writing sample by analyzing a criminal-procedure issue such as searches, interrogations, eyewitness evidence, or defendants' constitutional rights using several court decisions.

title: Patent Attorney
shortDescription: Protects inventions by obtaining, analyzing, licensing, and enforcing patent rights involving technologies such as biotechnology, electronics, software, and semiconductor systems.
usual_employers: Technology and Semiconductor Company Legal Departments

reasons: This internship can help you observe how attorneys research patents, evaluate inventions, organize technical evidence, and support intellectual property matters.
preparationSteps: Choose a familiar technology and find several related patents using the USPTO patent-search tools, then write a one-page comparison of what each patent claims to protect.

Apply to intellectual property firms and corporate legal departments for undergraduate legal, patent, research, or administrative internships rather than limiting your search to attorney-level positions.

reasons: This pathway can help you build the technical literacy patent attorneys need to understand inventions and communicate with scientists or engineers.
preparationSteps: Choose either a biological or engineering technology you understand from coursework and create a short explanation of how it works, what problem it solves, and which features might distinguish it from competing designs.
Ask a science or engineering professor about assisting with laboratory, design, or technical research so you develop firsthand experience interpreting scientific or engineering work.

patent_law_school_pathway.internshipTitle: Patent Law School and USPTO Pathway
reasons: Patent attorneys generally combine a J.D. and bar admission with qualifying scientific or technical preparation, and practitioners representing patent applicants before the USPTO must satisfy USPTO registration requirements.
preparationSteps: Meet with Loyola pre-law advising to map your LSAT preparation, J.D. applications, recommendation letters, legal writing experience, and law-school timeline.

Review the current USPTO General Requirements Bulletin before graduation and compare your degree and coursework with its scientific and technical eligibility routes so you know whether additional technical coursework may be necessary.

title: Environmental General Counsel
shortDescription: Leads legal strategy for a clean-energy or environmental company, advising on energy regulation, permitting, grid interconnection, contracts, compliance, transactions, and organizational legal risk.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how environmental and energy rules affect projects, utilities, businesses, and government approval processes.
preparationSteps: Choose one proposed energy or environmental regulation and write a one-page brief explaining the rule, responsible agency, organizations affected, and major compliance questions.
Attend or watch a public utility, environmental, zoning, or energy regulatory hearing and summarize the legal and policy arguments presented by the major stakeholders.

reasons: This internship can expose you to contracts, permitting, compliance, project development, and other legal issues involved in building energy infrastructure.
preparationSteps: Choose a solar, wind, battery, transmission, or other energy project and identify the major government approvals, environmental reviews, contracts, and stakeholders involved in bringing it online.
Apply to renewable-energy companies, utilities, environmental organizations, government agencies, and law firms for broad legal, compliance, regulatory, or policy internships.

reasons: General Counsel is normally reached after law school, bar admission, and years of progressively responsible legal work rather than directly after graduation.
preparationSteps: Meet with Loyola pre-law advising to plan LSAT preparation, J.D. applications, recommendation letters, legal writing experience, and coursework involving environmental regulation, economics, and public policy.

Research attorneys working in energy regulation and clean-energy companies and compare common early-career routes such as law-firm associate, regulatory attorney, government counsel, and in-house counsel before advancement into senior legal leadership.

title: Appellate Court Judge
shortDescription: Reviews lower-court records, written briefs, oral arguments, and legal precedent to determine whether significant legal or procedural errors occurred and to issue appellate decisions.

reasons: This internship can help you observe how judges and court staff analyze cases, conduct hearings, research legal questions, and prepare judicial decisions.
preparationSteps: Attend several publicly accessible trial and appellate proceedings and keep notes on how judges question attorneys, identify legal issues, and distinguish factual disputes from questions of law.
Apply to local, state, and federal courts for undergraduate judicial, courthouse, administrative, or legal-support internships that are open to students before law school.

reasons: This pathway can help you practice the close reading of cases and precedent that becomes central to appellate advocacy and judicial decision-making.
preparationSteps: Choose one published appellate decision and create a case brief identifying the procedural history, legal question, standard of review, precedent used, holding, and reasoning.
Read both a majority opinion and dissent from the same appellate case and write a two-page comparison explaining where the judges disagree about law, precedent, or interpretation.

reasons: Appellate judgeships normally follow a J.D., bar admission, and a substantial legal career that may include litigation, appellate practice, judicial clerkships, government service, or prior judicial experience.
preparationSteps: Meet with Loyola pre-law advising to plan LSAT preparation, J.D. applications, recommendation letters, legal writing development, and undergraduate experiences involving courts and constitutional law.

Research several current appellate judges in your state and federal circuit and map their careers from law school through clerkships, legal practice, government service, or earlier judgeships to understand how varied and experience-intensive the path is.

title: International Trade Lawyer
shortDescription: Advises companies and governments on tariffs, customs, trade agreements, market access, and trade remedies while representing clients in major cross-border trade disputes.
usual_employers: Office of the U.S. Trade Representative

reasons: This internship can help you understand how governments analyze tariffs, trade agreements, market-access barriers, and international economic policy.
preparationSteps: Choose a current U.S. tariff or trade dispute and create a one-page brief explaining the products involved, countries affected, legal basis for the measure, and arguments made by each side.
Apply to federal agencies, congressional offices, trade associations, and policy organizations for internships involving international trade, economics, commerce, or regulatory policy.

reasons: This internship can expose you to tariffs, customs classifications, import regulations, trade remedies, and legal issues affecting companies that operate across borders.
preparationSteps: Select an imported product and use public government resources to identify its tariff classification, applicable duty rate, country of origin, and any major import restrictions or special trade measures.
Read a publicly available trade-remedy or customs decision and write a short case brief identifying the dispute, governing rule, arguments, and outcome.

reasons: Practicing international trade law generally requires a J.D. and bar admission, followed by experience in trade regulation, government, litigation, or international economic law.
preparationSteps: Meet with Loyola pre-law advising to plan LSAT preparation, J.D. applications, recommendation letters, legal writing experience, and undergraduate coursework involving international politics, economics, and business law.

Compare law schools with strong international trade, international economic law, customs, or WTO offerings and identify clinics, journals, moot courts, and government externships that could provide trade-law experience.

title: M&A Legal Architect
shortDescription: Structures major mergers and acquisitions by negotiating and drafting transaction agreements that define ownership, price, obligations, risk allocation, approvals, and closing conditions.

reasons: This internship can help you observe how attorneys review contracts, perform due diligence, research corporate-law issues, and support business transactions.
preparationSteps: Choose a recently announced acquisition involving two public companies and create a one-page deal summary covering the buyer, target, transaction value, payment method, expected closing date, and major regulatory approvals.
Apply to corporate law firms and company legal departments for undergraduate legal, corporate, transactional, or general law-firm internships rather than searching only for M&A-specific positions.

reasons: This pathway can help you understand the financial and business logic behind transactions before learning the legal documents used to execute them.
preparationSteps: Pick a completed public-company acquisition and compare the buyer and target's revenue, earnings, debt, and market value before the announcement using their public financial statements.

Read the publicly filed merger agreement for the same transaction and identify several major sections such as purchase price, representations, closing conditions, termination rights, and regulatory obligations.

reasons: Practicing as an M&A attorney requires a J.D. and bar admission, with transactional expertise developing through corporate-law coursework, summer associate work, and supervised deal experience.
preparationSteps: Meet with Loyola pre-law advising to plan LSAT preparation, J.D. applications, recommendation letters, legal writing experience, and coursework that strengthens both legal reasoning and financial literacy.

Before applying to law school, learn to read basic balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements so you can understand the business information that corporate attorneys encounter during transactions and due diligence.

title: Jury Consultant Principal
shortDescription: Leads behavioral research on potential jurors and uses mock trials, surveys, focus groups, and jury-selection analysis to help legal teams refine trial strategy and understand juror reactions.

reasons: This pathway can help you learn how psychologists and social scientists design studies, analyze human decision-making, and turn behavioral data into defensible conclusions.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola psychology or sociology professor about assisting with research involving judgment, persuasion, social attitudes, decision-making, bias, or group behavior.

Use a public survey dataset to test whether several attitudes or demographic variables are associated with different responses, then summarize the results without claiming that correlation proves individual behavior.

reasons: This internship can expose you to mock trials, jury research, case strategy, witness preparation, and the research methods used by professional trial consultants.
preparationSteps: Read several publicly available court opinions from the same type of case and create a short list of factual, emotional, or credibility issues that different jurors might interpret differently.

Search jury-consulting, trial-consulting, litigation-support, and legal-research firms for undergraduate research or analyst internships rather than limiting yourself to positions titled 'jury consultant.'

reasons: Senior jury consultants often develop substantial expertise in psychology, sociology, communication, law, or quantitative research, and many hold advanced degrees even though no single graduate credential is universally required.
preparationSteps: Build strong undergraduate preparation in statistics and research methods and complete at least one substantial research paper or faculty-supported project involving human attitudes or decision-making.

Compare graduate programs in social psychology, legal psychology, behavioral science, communication, or related fields and note their research-methods prerequisites, faculty interests, recommendation requirements, and career outcomes before deciding whether graduate study fits your path.

title: Entertainment Counsel
shortDescription: Negotiates and drafts contracts governing actors, creators, production, intellectual property, and the licensing and distribution of film, television, and streaming content.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how studios and production companies organize deals involving performers, writers, producers, directors, and intellectual property.
preparationSteps: Choose a film or television production and identify the major groups whose rights or services would require agreements, such as actors, writers, directors, producers, music owners, and distributors.
Apply to studios, production companies, networks, streaming companies, and talent organizations for undergraduate business affairs, legal, rights-management, or contract-administration internships.

reasons: This internship can expose you to how entertainment companies license content, track rights, and distribute programming across theaters, television networks, streaming services, and international markets.
preparationSteps: Choose one movie or television series and research where it is currently available, then create a simple map of the studio, producer, distributor, streamer, and other companies involved in bringing it to viewers.

Practice rights analysis by creating a one-page fictional deal sheet identifying the content, territory, platform, license period, exclusivity, and payment terms that a distribution agreement would need to address.

reasons: Practicing as entertainment counsel requires a J.D. and appropriate bar admission, followed by experience in transactional law, intellectual property, entertainment business affairs, or related legal work.
preparationSteps: Meet with Loyola pre-law advising to plan LSAT preparation, J.D. applications, recommendation letters, legal writing experience, and undergraduate exposure to media, theater, business, and intellectual property issues.

Compare law schools with entertainment-law or intellectual-property offerings and identify entertainment law journals, clinics, externships, and summer opportunities with studios, agencies, production companies, or media law firms.

title: Foreign Service Officer
shortDescription: Represents U.S. interests abroad by analyzing foreign developments, engaging government officials, communicating policy positions, supporting negotiations, and advancing diplomatic priorities.
usual_employers: U.S. Mission to the United Nations

reasons: This internship can expose you to diplomacy, foreign policy, government writing, embassy operations, and the work performed by Foreign Service and Civil Service professionals.
preparationSteps: Review the five Foreign Service Officer career tracks and write a one-page comparison identifying which track best matches your interests and what experiences could demonstrate its relevant skills.

Apply to U.S. Department of State student programs and other federal international-affairs opportunities while building examples of writing, leadership, teamwork, analysis, and cross-cultural experience.

reasons: This internship can help you practice researching foreign developments and turning complex political events into concise recommendations or briefing materials.
preparationSteps: Choose one country and produce a two-page monthly political brief covering its government, major political actors, relationship with the United States, and one current foreign-policy issue.
Apply to think tanks, congressional foreign-policy offices, international organizations, and research institutes for positions involving international affairs, regional research, or policy analysis.
