reasons: This internship can expose you to fabric performance, material selection, supplier capabilities, quality testing, sustainability considerations, and textile innovation.
preparationSteps: Compare several fabrics or textile materials on properties such as weight, strength, stretch, durability, texture, cost, and intended garment use, then explain why each fits different products.

Ask a Loyola engineering or materials professor about a small project involving textiles, polymers, coatings, fibers, or material testing and discuss whether it could develop into a proposal for the next Hauber Summer Research Fellowship cycle.

reasons: Director-level fashion product and production roles generally follow years of experience in product development, materials, sourcing, manufacturing, merchandising, or supply chain.
preparationSteps: Compare early-career roles such as product-development coordinator, materials assistant, production coordinator, sourcing analyst, technical designer, and supply-chain analyst to decide which side of fashion operations fits you best.

Map one apparel collection from design concept through material sourcing, samples, manufacturing, freight, distribution, and retail, then identify where delays, quality failures, or cost overruns could occur.

title: Industrial-Organizational Psychologist
shortDescription: Applies psychological research and data analysis to improve how organizations structure work, select and develop employees, evaluate leadership, manage change, and support workforce performance and well-being.

reasons: This internship can help you practice using employee surveys, workforce data, and statistical analysis to answer questions about retention, engagement, performance, and organizational effectiveness.
preparationSteps: Create a small simulated employee dataset containing engagement scores, tenure, department, performance, and turnover, then use Excel, Power BI, Python, or another tool to identify patterns and communicate them in a short management brief.
Apply to HR analytics, people analytics, workforce research, and organizational consulting teams rather than searching only for internships titled 'I-O Psychology.'

reasons: This internship can expose you to employee development, organizational change, surveys, training, team effectiveness, and other practical applications of workplace psychology.
preparationSteps: Choose a campus organization and design a short anonymous survey about role clarity, communication, workload, and team functioning, then summarize broad patterns without identifying individual members.
Apply to consulting firms and corporate HR teams for internships involving organizational development, talent management, employee experience, or learning and development.

reasons: Most professional I-O psychology roles require graduate-level preparation in workplace psychology, research methods, statistics, assessment, and organizational behavior.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola psychology or management professor about assisting with research involving teams, leadership, employee attitudes, motivation, selection, or organizational behavior.

Compare master's and Ph.D. programs in Industrial-Organizational Psychology and record their statistics, research-methods, recommendation, internship, thesis, and application requirements before deciding which level matches your career goals.

title: Clinical Psychologist
shortDescription: Assesses, diagnoses, and treats psychological and behavioral conditions through evidence-based psychotherapy, psychological testing, treatment planning, and collaboration with other healthcare professionals.

reasons: This pathway can help you build the research experience that is especially important for competitive clinical psychology doctoral applications.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola psychology professor about assisting with research involving mental health, cognition, development, treatment outcomes, assessment, or related behavioral questions.

Learn one concrete research task such as participant recruitment, literature review, survey administration, data cleaning, behavioral coding, or statistical analysis and document your contribution for future graduate applications.

reasons: This pathway can expose you to mental health services and multidisciplinary clinical environments without asking an undergraduate to perform work that requires professional licensure.
preparationSteps: Volunteer or work in an appropriate undergraduate support role at a hospital, crisis-support organization, behavioral health program, community organization, or research clinic.
Observe how licensed professionals handle confidentiality, documentation, referrals, boundaries, and collaboration while avoiding independent diagnosis or therapy outside your training.

reasons: Independent practice as a clinical psychologist generally requires doctoral education, supervised clinical training, and state licensure.
preparationSteps: By junior year, compare APA-accredited Ph.D. and Psy.D. clinical psychology programs and make a checklist of research experience, psychology coursework, statistics, recommendations, personal statements, interviews, and program-specific prerequisites.

Build relationships with psychology faculty who can evaluate your research ability and preparation, while learning the differences between research-intensive Ph.D. programs and clinically focused Psy.D. programs before choosing where to apply.

title: Behavioral Economist
shortDescription: Combines economics, psychology, experiments, and quantitative analysis to study how people respond to prices, incentives, product choices, and other decisions and to improve business or policy strategy.
usual_employers: Behavioral Science and Economic Consulting Firms

reasons: This internship can help you practice using economic data, statistical methods, and causal reasoning to answer questions about how people and markets respond to changes.
preparationSteps: Ask an economics professor about helping with research involving consumer behavior, experiments, incentives, labor, markets, or applied econometrics.
Use a public dataset to test one clearly defined behavioral or economic hypothesis and write a short report explaining the result, uncertainty, and alternative explanations.

reasons: This internship can show you how economists and data scientists measure demand, elasticity, experiments, and customer responses to pricing or product changes.
preparationSteps: Create a small simulated dataset containing prices, units sold, promotions, and customer segments and estimate how demand changes as price changes rather than assuming every observed correlation is causal.
Apply to technology companies, retailers, marketplaces, consulting firms, and consumer businesses for economics, pricing, analytics, experimentation, or data science internships.

reasons: Research-intensive behavioral economics and senior industry economist positions commonly require strong graduate-level preparation in economics, econometrics, experimentation, and quantitative methods.
preparationSteps: Build strong undergraduate preparation in intermediate microeconomics, econometrics, statistics, experimental methods, and programming while completing at least one substantial empirical economics project.

Compare master's and Ph.D. programs in economics, behavioral economics, applied economics, or related quantitative fields and identify faculty working on consumer behavior, experimental economics, pricing, or decision-making.

title: Demographic Modeler
shortDescription: Builds population, household, migration, and labor-force models that help governments and planners anticipate demographic change and make better long-range housing, transportation, infrastructure, and service decisions.

reasons: This internship can help you work with Census and population data while learning how demographic trends are translated into practical information for governments and communities.
preparationSteps: Download Census data for several Maryland counties and compare population growth, age structure, household composition, and migration over time using Excel, R, Python, or another analysis tool.
Turn the analysis into a short demographic brief containing several charts and a plain-language explanation of what the trends could mean for housing, schools, transportation, or public services.

reasons: This internship can show you how population projections and geographic data become inputs into long-range land-use and infrastructure planning.
preparationSteps: Use Census tract data and GIS to map population change or age distribution across one county and compare those patterns with roads, transit, schools, or housing development.
Apply to planning departments, metropolitan planning organizations, state agencies, and research organizations for internships involving planning, GIS, demographics, or policy analysis.

reasons: Advanced demographic modeling requires substantial experience with statistics, Census data, forecasting, databases, and programming even when a particular employer does not require a graduate degree.
preparationSteps: Build a simple population projection in Excel, R, or Python using a starting population and assumptions for births, deaths, and migration, then test how different assumptions alter the forecast.

Compare early-career roles such as demographic analyst, research analyst, GIS analyst, planning analyst, and applied demographer, and consider graduate study in demography, sociology, statistics, economics, or planning if it materially strengthens your modeling skills.

title: User Research Principal
shortDescription: Leads advanced qualitative and quantitative research on how people understand and use digital products, translating evidence about user needs, behavior, workflows, and usability into product and design strategy.

reasons: This internship can help you practice interviews, usability testing, surveys, research synthesis, and communicating user evidence to designers and product managers.
preparationSteps: Choose one website or application and conduct a small usability study in which several consenting participants attempt the same tasks, then document where they succeed, hesitate, misunderstand, or fail.
Turn the findings into a portfolio case study showing your research question, method, evidence, limitations, findings, and recommended product changes.

reasons: This pathway can build rigorous research skills in psychology or social science that transfer directly into professional user research.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola psychology, communication, sociology, or information-systems professor about assisting with human-subject research involving cognition, behavior, technology, communication, or decision-making.

Practice one or more research skills such as interviewing, survey design, behavioral coding, statistical analysis, literature review, or research synthesis while following the project's research-ethics procedures.

reasons: Principal User Researcher is normally reached after years of progressively complex product research and demonstrated influence across product, design, engineering, and business teams.
preparationSteps: Compare early-career roles such as UX researcher, user researcher, design researcher, human factors researcher, and product researcher and identify the research methods most frequently shared across them.

Build a portfolio containing several different research methods rather than only usability tests, and compare master's programs in HCI, Human Factors, Psychology, or related fields if graduate training would materially strengthen your research depth; graduate school is useful but not universally required.

title: DEI Strategy Consultant
shortDescription: Analyzes workplace policies, employee experiences, organizational data, and talent systems to identify barriers and help organizations build more inclusive, equitable, and legally compliant workplaces.
usual_employers: Large Employer People and HR Teams

reasons: This internship can help you understand how hiring, promotion, employee experience, organizational culture, and workforce policies are evaluated in real organizations.
preparationSteps: Choose three organizations and compare their publicly available recruiting, mentoring, accessibility, employee-development, and workplace policies in a one-page spreadsheet, noting specific differences rather than judging them only as good or bad.
Apply to HR, workforce consulting, organizational development, employee experience, and people strategy internships rather than limiting your search to positions labeled DEI.

reasons: This pathway can help you build the survey and data-analysis skills used to identify differences in employee experiences.
preparationSteps: Create a short anonymous survey for a student organization about role clarity, belonging, access to opportunities, communication, and workload, then summarize the results in Excel without identifying individual respondents.
Learn basic survey design by comparing two versions of each question and removing wording that is leading, emotionally loaded, or likely to push respondents toward a particular answer.

reasons: This pathway can help you learn how social-science evidence, employment rules, and organizational systems interact before you eventually advise larger employers.
preparationSteps: Read the current EEOC guidance on workplace discrimination and create a two-column note sheet separating lawful equal-opportunity goals from examples of employment practices that could create discrimination concerns.

Build a small portfolio containing one survey analysis, one workplace-policy comparison, and one short recommendation memo so you can demonstrate research and organizational thinking without pretending to have executive consulting experience.

title: Public Health Epidemiologist
shortDescription: Investigates patterns of disease and other health threats using population data, outbreak investigations, statistical analysis, and forecasting to help public-health agencies choose evidence-based responses.
usual_employers: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
Universities and Public Health Research Centers

reasons: This internship can help you learn how health departments collect, clean, analyze, visualize, and communicate population-health information.
preparationSteps: Download a public CDC dataset and create a simple chart showing how one disease or health outcome changes across time, age groups, or locations.
Write a one-page summary explaining what the data shows, what it does not show, and what additional information you would need before recommending a public-health response.

reasons: This pathway can help you practice turning real health questions into measurable research questions before graduate-level epidemiology training.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola biology, psychology, sociology, statistics, or health-related professor whether you can assist with a small project involving health behavior, disease, population data, or community outcomes.
Learn the difference between prevalence, incidence, correlation, and causation by finding a public-health article using each idea and explaining it in your own words with one simple example.

reasons: Professional epidemiologist roles typically require graduate education, commonly an MPH or master's degree with substantial epidemiology and biostatistics training.
preparationSteps: By junior year, compare several MPH or epidemiology master's programs and make a checklist of statistics, biology, research-methods, programming, recommendation, practicum, and application requirements.

Build one small public-health data project in Excel, Python, or another tool before graduation so you enter graduate study already comfortable cleaning data, making basic visualizations, and explaining results.

title: Trial Consultant Methodologist
shortDescription: Uses social-science research methods, surveys, focus groups, mock trials, and behavioral analysis to help legal teams understand juror reactions and improve trial strategy and jury-selection decisions.

reasons: This internship can help you build the survey, observation, data-analysis, and research-design skills used in professional trial consulting.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola psychology or sociology professor about helping with a project involving judgment, persuasion, decision-making, attitudes, memory, or group behavior.
Learn basic data coding by taking a small set of anonymous open-ended survey responses and grouping similar answers into clear categories, then count how frequently each category appears.

reasons: This pathway can help you practice observing how different people interpret the same evidence without assuming that demographics automatically determine opinions.
preparationSteps: Create a short fictional civil case with two competing arguments and ask several consenting classmates to read both sides and explain which evidence they found most persuasive.
Summarize the responses in a spreadsheet and identify recurring reasoning patterns, then write a short memo explaining the findings and the limits of your very small sample.

reasons: Senior methodology-focused consultants usually develop substantial expertise in psychology, sociology, statistics, communication, or legal psychology before leading complex jury research.
preparationSteps: Learn the basics of surveys, experiments, focus groups, sampling, and correlation by creating a one-page reference sheet explaining when each method would be useful and one major limitation of each.

Compare graduate programs in social psychology, legal psychology, sociology, communication, or behavioral science if you want a research-heavy path, but also compare entry-level litigation research roles because a graduate degree is helpful rather than universally mandatory.

title: Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO)
shortDescription: Leads an organization's overall people strategy across talent acquisition, development, compensation, employee and labor relations, workforce planning, culture, HR technology, compliance, and organizational change.

reasons: This internship can help you understand recruiting, onboarding, employee records, performance processes, training, and the everyday systems that eventually fall under senior HR leadership.
preparationSteps: Apply to HR departments for internships involving recruiting, talent management, employee experience, HR operations, or learning and development.

Map the employee journey at a student organization from recruitment through onboarding, role assignment, feedback, and leadership transition and identify two places where the process could be clearer.

reasons: This pathway can introduce you to workplace rules, employee concerns, collective bargaining, and the structured agreements that HR leaders may eventually oversee.
preparationSteps: Find a publicly available union collective bargaining agreement and identify its sections on wages, scheduling, discipline, grievances, benefits, and management responsibilities.
Create a one-page summary explaining what a grievance process is and trace the steps an employee and employer would follow under that specific agreement.

reasons: CHRO is normally reached after years of progressive responsibility across several HR specialties and eventually management of large teams and enterprise workforce strategy.
preparationSteps: Compare entry-level careers in recruiting, HR operations, compensation, learning and development, employee relations, and people analytics and make a one-page chart showing what each specialty actually does.

Build a small simulated workforce dashboard in Excel with employee count, hiring, turnover, departments, and tenure so you begin learning how HR leaders use basic metrics rather than relying only on qualitative judgments.

title: Social Policy Director
shortDescription: Leads research and policy analysis on social programs such as housing, poverty, or community development, directing studies that evaluate outcomes and translate evidence into recommendations for policymakers.

reasons: This internship can help you learn how researchers turn questions about housing, poverty, education, or community programs into data analysis and policy recommendations.
preparationSteps: Choose one local social program and write a one-page program map explaining the problem it addresses, who it serves, what services it provides, and which measurable outcomes would indicate improvement.
Apply to think tanks, nonprofits, government agencies, and university research centers for internships involving policy analysis, research, housing, community development, or program evaluation.

reasons: This pathway can help you practice evaluating a social program without starting from the assumption that it succeeded.
preparationSteps: Choose a housing program and use public Census, HUD, or local-government data to track one relevant outcome such as rent burden, housing production, homelessness, or eviction over time.
Write a short memo explaining whether the outcome improved or worsened while explicitly stating that the trend alone does not prove the program caused the change.

reasons: Policy Director positions normally follow experience as a research assistant, policy analyst, research associate, economist, planner, or program evaluator.
preparationSteps: Attend or watch one city council, planning commission, or housing-policy hearing and write a one-page summary identifying the policy proposal, evidence used, major stakeholders, and disagreements about expected outcomes.

By junior year, compare master's programs in public policy, public administration, sociology, economics, or urban planning and record their statistics, research, internship, recommendation, and capstone requirements; graduate study is common but the exact credential depends on the organization.

title: Hospital Bioethicist
shortDescription: Helps patients, families, clinicians, and hospital leaders analyze difficult ethical questions involving treatment decisions, end-of-life care, genetics, emerging therapies, patient autonomy, and competing values.
usual_employers: University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences

reasons: This pathway can help you practice structured ethical reasoning, literature research, and evidence-based analysis before pursuing advanced clinical ethics training.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Philosophy, Theology, Psychology, or health-related professor whether you can assist with research involving bioethics, healthcare decisions, genetics, disability, end-of-life care, or medical justice.

Choose one publicly documented bioethics case and write a two-page analysis identifying the stakeholders, competing values, relevant facts, unanswered questions, and at least two defensible courses of action.

reasons: This pathway can help you understand how ethical questions arise inside real healthcare systems without expecting an undergraduate to advise patients or clinicians.
preparationSteps: Attend public bioethics lectures, hospital ethics webinars, or university medical-ethics events and keep a one-page glossary of unfamiliar clinical and ethical concepts that repeatedly appear.

Volunteer in an appropriate non-clinical hospital or hospice role so you become familiar with healthcare environments, interdisciplinary teams, patient privacy, and the difference between clinical, legal, spiritual, and ethical responsibilities.

reasons: Professional hospital ethicist positions commonly require graduate or terminal education plus focused experience in healthcare ethics consultation.
preparationSteps: Compare graduate programs in bioethics, healthcare ethics, philosophy, theology, law, medicine, or related fields and record their prerequisites, clinical opportunities, research expectations, funding, and career outcomes.

Review the purpose of clinical ethics fellowships and the Healthcare Ethics Consultant-Certified credential so you understand which qualifications are earned later through graduate education and supervised professional experience.

title: Professor of Divinity / Theology
shortDescription: Researches and teaches theology or religious studies while producing scholarly books, articles, lectures, and textual analysis on religious traditions, ideas, histories, ethics, or sacred texts.
usual_employers: University Theology and Religious Studies Departments

reasons: This pathway can teach you how academic scholars build bibliographies, work with primary texts, evaluate secondary scholarship, and develop publishable research questions.
preparationSteps: Ask a Loyola Theology, Philosophy, or History professor whether you can assist with bibliography building, archival research, source summaries, transcription, or another small part of an existing research project.
Choose one theological question from a course and expand it into a carefully sourced research paper that compares several scholarly interpretations instead of simply arguing from personal belief.

reasons: This pathway can help you practice the historical and textual work needed for scholarship involving ancient or religious writings.
preparationSteps: Use a university library or reputable digital archive to compare several translations or manuscript witnesses of one short religious passage and record meaningful differences in wording, historical context, or interpretation.
Create a five-page source commentary explaining what is known about the text's date, authorship, historical setting, transmission, and major scholarly disagreements using academic sources.

reasons: Tenure-track university careers in theology and religious studies generally require a Ph.D. or closely related research doctorate and a developing scholarly publication record.
preparationSteps: By junior year, compare Ph.D. programs in theology or religious studies and create a checklist of language requirements, writing samples, faculty research fit, recommendation letters, master's prerequisites, funding, and application deadlines.

Identify two or three professors whose research genuinely interests you, read one publication from each, and use that reading to narrow the kind of theological or historical question you could eventually study in graduate school.

title: Senior Pastor / Clergy Director
shortDescription: Provides senior spiritual and organizational leadership for a congregation by preaching, guiding ministry strategy, developing staff and volunteers, providing pastoral care, and coordinating major church priorities across one or more campuses.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how worship, community programs, volunteers, pastoral care, staff, and administration work together inside a congregation.
preparationSteps: Volunteer or intern with Loyola Campus Ministry or a local congregation and take responsibility for one manageable activity such as event setup, volunteer coordination, outreach, small-group logistics, or service planning.

Ask the supervising clergy member to explain how the congregation divides responsibilities among pastoral, financial, administrative, worship, youth, and community-service leaders and make a simple organizational map.

reasons: This pathway can help you begin developing teaching and pastoral communication skills under supervision rather than expecting you to function as clergy before training.
preparationSteps: Prepare a five-to-ten-minute reflection or teaching for a supervised campus ministry, youth, or small-group setting and ask an experienced ministry leader for feedback on clarity, theological accuracy, structure, and delivery.

Shadow appropriate pastoral activities such as service planning, community outreach, staff meetings, or public ministry events while respecting confidentiality around private counseling and sensitive pastoral-care situations.

reasons: Senior pastoral leadership usually follows years of ministry formation, and many denominations require or strongly prefer seminary education and formal ordination.
preparationSteps: Speak with clergy from the denomination or tradition you are considering and write down its exact education, ordination, supervised-ministry, examination, and mentorship requirements because these differ substantially across traditions.

Compare several M.Div. programs and record their theology, preaching, pastoral-care, field-education, language, financial-aid, and denominational requirements before deciding whether seminary fits your intended ministry.

title: Interfaith Conflict Mediator
shortDescription: Facilitates dialogue among religious, cultural, governmental, and community groups to reduce tensions, strengthen trust, and support peaceful solutions to conflicts involving identity, belief, or communal division.

reasons: This internship can help you practice respectful dialogue, event facilitation, stakeholder outreach, and communication across differences in a low-risk environment.
preparationSteps: Join Loyola Campus Ministry, an interfaith student group, or a local interfaith organization and help organize one dialogue or service event involving participants from different religious or cultural backgrounds.

Write a short neutral discussion guide containing open-ended questions, ground rules, and follow-up prompts designed to help participants explain disagreements without turning the session into a debate.

reasons: This pathway can help you learn how serious mediators understand a conflict before attempting to facilitate dialogue.
preparationSteps: Choose one historical or current intercommunal conflict and create a stakeholder map showing the major groups, grievances, political interests, religious factors, shared interests, and previous attempts at dialogue using reputable public sources.

Write a one-page conflict analysis separating religious disagreements from political, economic, ethnic, territorial, or security factors so you do not automatically treat every identity conflict as primarily theological.

reasons: This pathway can build basic facilitation and conflict-resolution skills before you seek professional roles in high-risk international environments.
preparationSteps: Complete a beginner conflict-resolution or interreligious-dialogue course from an established peacebuilding organization such as KAICIID and keep notes on techniques you could practice in campus or community settings.

Compare master's programs in conflict resolution, peace studies, international affairs, theology, or diplomacy and identify which programs provide supervised mediation practice, regional study, language development, and field placements.

title: Grief / Trauma Counselor
shortDescription: Provides professional counseling and grief support to individuals and families coping with death, anticipatory loss, trauma, and major life transitions in hospice, healthcare, and community settings.

reasons: This pathway can expose you to end-of-life and bereavement settings while keeping you within appropriate undergraduate and volunteer boundaries.
preparationSteps: Complete volunteer training with a hospice or grief-support organization and serve in an approved non-clinical role such as companionship, administrative support, community events, resource preparation, or family-support logistics.
Keep a private skills reflection focused on listening, boundaries, cultural differences, teamwork, and what trained counselors do that volunteers should not attempt themselves.

reasons: This pathway can help you build evidence-based knowledge about grief and trauma before you are qualified to provide clinical treatment.
preparationSteps: Create an annotated resource guide comparing several evidence-based grief-support approaches, support groups, crisis resources, and hospice services available in your community.

Ask a Loyola Psychology or related professor about assisting with research involving grief, trauma, coping, stress, health, or family relationships and begin with a manageable task such as literature review or data organization.

grief_counseling_graduate_pathway.internshipTitle: Grief Counseling Graduate and Licensure Pathway
reasons: Professional grief and trauma counseling typically requires a qualifying master's degree, supervised clinical training, and state professional licensure.
preparationSteps: Compare master's programs in counseling, clinical social work, or related licensed mental health fields and create a checklist of prerequisites, practicum hours, internship requirements, licensure outcomes, and grief or trauma electives.

Look up the counseling or social-work licensure sequence for the state where you may practice so you understand which credentials come after graduate school and which undergraduate experiences are useful now.

title: Religious Non-Profit Executive Director
shortDescription: Leads a faith-based nonprofit's strategy, fundraising, finances, board relationships, staff, partnerships, and programs while ensuring donated resources support the organization's mission responsibly.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how mission-driven organizations turn donations and strategic goals into actual services and programs.
preparationSteps: Volunteer or intern with a faith-based nonprofit and assist with one concrete program task such as event coordination, participant registration, volunteer scheduling, program data entry, community outreach, or supply tracking.
Create a one-page process map showing how one program moves from funding and planning through staff or volunteers to the people receiving the service.

reasons: This internship can teach you how nonprofits research donors, communicate impact, prepare grants, and raise funds without placing executive-level fundraising responsibility on an undergraduate.
preparationSteps: Choose one nonprofit and identify three foundations or grant programs that appear relevant to its mission, recording eligibility, typical award size, priorities, deadlines, and why the nonprofit might fit.
Practice creating a one-page mock funding request containing the problem, proposed activity, simple budget, expected result, and method for measuring whether the project worked.

reasons: Executive Director positions normally follow years of progressively responsible nonprofit program, development, finance, operations, or management experience.
preparationSteps: Use a public nonprofit annual report or Form 990 to identify its major revenue sources, major expense categories, executive structure, and program spending, then summarize what you learned in one page.

Compare early-career roles such as program coordinator, development associate, grants assistant, operations coordinator, and international programs assistant; graduate study in nonprofit management, public administration, business, or international development can help but is not universally required.

title: Theological Archivist
shortDescription: Organizes, describes, digitizes, preserves, and provides access to religious manuscripts, institutional records, rare books, photographs, and other historical materials held by seminaries, religious communities, and archives.
usual_employers: Burke Library at Union Theological Seminary

reasons: This internship can give you hands-on experience with the basic archival tasks used to make religious and historical collections usable by researchers.
preparationSteps: Apply to seminaries, university archives, church archives, religious institutes, museums, and special collections for student positions involving scanning, processing, cataloging, metadata, or reference support.

Practice by creating a small inventory of a non-sensitive collection such as public-domain documents, student organization records, or family historical material, recording dates, creators, formats, subjects, and organization.

reasons: This pathway can help you develop practical information-management skills without requiring access to irreplaceable ancient manuscripts.
preparationSteps: Build a small digital collection of public-domain religious or historical documents and create a spreadsheet containing file name, title, creator, date, description, format, source, and rights information.

Create two backup copies of the collection, use consistent file naming and folder structures, and write a one-page preservation note explaining how you would reduce the risk of files becoming lost or unreadable.

reasons: Professional archivist positions frequently prefer or require master's-level library, information science, archival studies, or public-history preparation.
preparationSteps: Compare master's programs in library and information science, archives, or public history and make a checklist of archival processing, metadata, digital preservation, internships, language study, and special-collections coursework.

Look at several current religious-archive job descriptions and keep a running list of recurring skills such as ArchivesSpace, metadata, digitization, preservation, reference work, theology knowledge, and foreign languages.

title: Liturgical Music Composer
shortDescription: Composes and arranges sacred music for worship, cathedral choirs, churches, professional ensembles, and religious events while adapting musical ideas to liturgical texts, traditions, voices, and instruments.

reasons: This pathway can help you build a real composition portfolio using manageable pieces before attempting large cathedral commissions.
preparationSteps: Write a two-to-four-minute sacred choral piece for a manageable ensemble such as SATB choir with piano or organ, enter it cleanly in notation software, and ask a Loyola music professor or choir director for feedback.
Revise the piece after feedback and, if possible, organize a simple student reading or recording so your portfolio contains both the score and evidence of how the music sounds with real performers.

reasons: This internship can help you understand how repertoire, texts, choir ability, liturgical seasons, rehearsals, and worship schedules shape the music that can actually be used.
preparationSteps: Assist a campus ministry, church, synagogue, cathedral, or other religious music program with choir preparation, music-library organization, rehearsals, accompaniment, or service planning under an experienced music leader.
Choose a public-domain hymn or sacred melody and create a short original arrangement for a student-sized ensemble, then revise it after musicians test whether the parts are practical to perform.

reasons: Major cathedral and professional commissions normally follow a substantial composition portfolio, strong musicianship, performances, and relationships with conductors or ensembles.
preparationSteps: Build a portfolio of several contrasting works for voices and instruments and look for student composition competitions, reading sessions, church commissions, or campus performances where one piece can receive a real performance.

Compare M.M., sacred music, and D.M.A. programs in composition or related fields and record their portfolio, theory, audition, recommendation, performance, and funding requirements; graduate education is common but not universally required to compose professionally.

title: Refugee Resettlement Director
shortDescription: Leads programs that help refugees establish new lives by coordinating housing, employment, language access, community orientation, case-management services, legal referrals, partner agencies, funding, and integration support.

reasons: This internship can help you understand the practical housing, employment, language, transportation, education, and community needs that resettlement organizations coordinate.
preparationSteps: Volunteer with a refugee or immigrant services organization in an approved undergraduate role such as home setup, ESL tutoring, employment preparation, transportation orientation, donation organization, or community events.

Ask a program coordinator to explain the stages a newly arrived family moves through during its first several months and create a simple process map showing which organizations provide different forms of assistance.

reasons: This pathway can help you practice organizing complicated local service information into something understandable and useful for newly arrived families.
preparationSteps: Create a public-resource guide for one city listing ESL programs, public transportation, healthcare clinics, schools, employment services, food assistance, and qualified immigration legal-service providers without attempting to give legal advice yourself.
Translate a small non-legal section of the guide into a language you study, then ask a fluent speaker or instructor to review it for clarity and cultural appropriateness before treating it as usable.

reasons: Director-level resettlement positions normally follow experience in case management, employment services, grants, program coordination, community partnerships, or humanitarian operations.
preparationSteps: Compare early-career positions such as resettlement case aide, employment specialist, program assistant, immigration-services coordinator, and refugee case manager and note the skills that repeat across them.

Compare graduate programs in social work, international affairs, public administration, migration studies, or nonprofit management if you want advanced preparation, while recognizing that graduate school is not universally required for every resettlement-management pathway.

title: Social Justice Advocacy Lead
shortDescription: Organizes faith-based coalitions to advocate on legislation and public policy, mobilize communities around social issues, communicate with lawmakers, and support lawful nonpartisan civic engagement.
usual_employers: NETWORK Lobby for Catholic Social Justice
USCCB Secretariat of Justice and Peace
Religious Action Center of Reform Judaism

reasons: This internship can help you learn how religious advocacy organizations research issues, mobilize supporters, communicate with lawmakers, and organize around legislation.
preparationSteps: Apply to faith-based advocacy groups, environmental organizations, anti-poverty organizations, denominational public-policy offices, and interfaith coalitions for policy, organizing, communications, or advocacy internships.

Choose one active federal or Maryland bill involving poverty, housing, climate, hunger, or another social issue and create a one-page brief identifying what it changes, its sponsors, current status, major arguments, and groups supporting or opposing it.

reasons: This pathway can help you practice turning a policy issue into clear, lawful community participation rather than simply posting opinions online.
preparationSteps: With a campus or community organization, help plan a small nonpartisan issue-education or letter-writing activity where participants learn about one piece of legislation and contact lawmakers using accurate information.

Create a simple outreach tracker in Excel recording invitations, attendance, follow-up contacts, and participation so you begin learning how organizers measure whether outreach actually reaches people.

reasons: Senior advocacy leaders need to understand both public policy and the legal boundaries that apply to different kinds of religious and nonprofit organizations.
preparationSteps: Read the IRS guidance distinguishing lobbying on legislation from political campaign intervention by 501(c)(3) organizations and write a one-page note containing examples of activities that fall into each category.

Build a small portfolio containing one policy brief, one lawmaker meeting script, one advocacy email, and one coalition outreach plan so you develop practical policy communication skills before seeking professional advocacy roles.
